title: test(ui): keep the grid through both origin-axes switches
body:
## What and why

Add the two missing UI regression tests from #3377. The Display-menu test stays unchanged.

- `egui_app::tests::view_names::the_browser_axes_checkbox_leaves_the_ground_grid_visible` opens the Browser View menu and clicks `Show world origin axes`.
- `egui_app::tests::display_menu::the_viewport_axes_button_leaves_the_ground_grid_visible` clicks the actual viewport navigation button at its live HUD anchor.

Each test starts with axes and Grid on. Each checks that the action hides the axes, leaves Grid on, and keeps the production `ground_grid_lines` result nonempty. No test sets the axes field directly. The tests use the existing shell harness and directory suite. No new test binary or production seam is needed.

The existing Display-menu test and reverse grid-off/axes-on coverage stay unchanged. The two touched modules contain 11 tests, up from nine. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3377-grid-axes-switch-tests.md`.

## Verification

Tested source head: `b0ea9f8bc4e1d02d578cbfefff04c2b3e21be992`.
Base: upstream `main` at `231b17d8b4ce33d9825b48c69e81952167b74c1c`.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib leaves_the_ground_grid_visible -- --nocapture`: both new tests pass.
- Negative control: temporarily restore `!state.show_world_axes || !state.show_grid` in `ground_grid_lines`. Both tests fail at their final grid-output assertion. Restore the production guard. Both tests pass again. The negative control is not in the diff.
- Display-menu module: eight tests pass. Browser view-switch module: three tests pass.
- `the_ground_grid_is_a_round_spaced_floor`: passes, including the reverse grid-hidden/axes-visible direction.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 231b17d8b4ce33d9825b48c69e81952167b74c1c`: all 10 selected steps pass on the committed head. UI lib: 1796 passed, eight ignored. The selected integration suites pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes on the committed head.
- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: all five test-target steps pass on the committed head. This runs all 11 light twins. The broad all-app `--no-run` preparation step is excluded; each selected target builds normally.
- `git diff --check`: passes.

Linux checks use a three-job budget. The UI gate reports the software Vulkan adapter, llvmpipe.

## Scope and limits

Tests and the per-issue decision only. No production behavior, dependency, renderer, geometry, toolpath, post, simulation, collision, or numeric-policy change. No pixel golden changes. No full heavy, release, or example-catalog lane. The standalone app was not launched. No new before/after screenshots are claimed: this test-only change has no visual difference. The harness uses the real controls and production grid generator; it does not prove physical-machine safety.

The default rustfmt check reports existing formatting differences in these modules. Existing formatting is preserved outside the new tests. No broad formatting rewrite is included.

No green-CI claim is made. Required rules and actual PR checks are checked separately before handoff. This is an outside-contributor PR for manual maintainer handling, not a counted collaborator review.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3377#issuecomment-7226619228

No scout was commissioned. Bounded direct searches located the Browser switch, viewport dispatch and HUD anchor, existing Display tests, shell helpers, and ground-grid generator.

Changelog: none (test-only)
Effort: low

Fixes #3377

title: test(examples): add the wrapped A-axis catalog case
body:
## What changed

- New catalog case `examples/catalog/multiaxis/wrapped`. The part is a 20 mm x 20 mm bar along X with one round-bottom ring groove at X0.
- The model generator `model/gen_wrapped_obj.py` writes `wrapped.obj`. It checks that the mesh is closed and that each facet faces out.
- `build.camscript` uses the built-in `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4` machine. It adds the setup `Wrap` with the `Tormach PathPilot` post, and a cylinder stock along X.
- Three operations use the catalog ball mill `BN-0600`:
  - `Wrap rough`: Rotary Offset.
  - `Wrap finish`: Rotary Parallel. It also finishes the two end faces down to the A centreline.
  - `Groove rings`: Rotary Contour, from X-5 to X5.
- Each posted operation turns A. The program has no B word. Wrapped moves use `G93`, then `G94`.
- `cargo xtask catalog` added the case link under Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md`.
- The held pin from commit `cab66a8e2` moved into the `example_catalog` directory suite: `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_multiaxis_wrapped.rs`. No new top-level test binary remains.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2869-wrapped-case.md`.

## Cause

The catalog had no case for the three rotary kinds. The earlier attempt stopped on #3000, which is now closed.

## Refusals found (filed and linked on #2392)

- #2772 (already open): the rotary kinds refuse a groove that wanders along X (a barrel cam). The case uses a ring groove.
- #4422 (new, P3): without a setup, the post refuses a B word for this A-only program. The case adds a setup as the workaround.
- No MCP parameter was missing.

## Tests

- Pin: `catalog_multiaxis_wrapped::keeps_three_rotary_operations_and_posts_a_axis_moves`. It checks the three saved kinds, an `Ok` status for each, the embedded model, and A motion in each posted section.
- Red before the case: with the case folder removed, the pin fails with `the wrapped catalog project must load: Io(... NotFound ...)`.
- Mutation: with the A words removed from the `Groove rings` section of `wrapped.nc`, the pin fails with `each rotary operation must move the A axis`. With the file restored, it passes.
- `catalog_multiaxis_wrapped::regenerates` and `::rebuilds` are in the heavy lane. Each takes about 30 s alone in debug. The `2d/slots` case set this precedent.
- Commands on the final head `feec48b38` (after a merge of upstream/main `392980120`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 10 steps, 0 failed.
  - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 2 steps (heavy build, `app heavy: example_catalog`), 0 failed. The wrapped case took 10 s in that lane.
  - `cargo xtask catalog --check`: all 17 cases checked.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-app`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed. This ran before the merge of upstream/main. The merge changed no file of this PR except one `include!` line.

## Goldens moved

- None of the existing programs changed. `cargo xtask catalog --check` reproduces each committed `.nc` and `refusal.txt`.
- New: `examples/catalog/multiaxis/wrapped/wrapped.nc` and `wrapped.camproj` (about 3.7 MB).

## Not exercised

- No physical machine ran the program.
- No screenshots: the PR has no UI change.
- The full `example_catalog` debug suite ran in the quick gate. The full heavy lanes of other crates did not run.

## Overlaps

- #4410 (3D rest case) adds its own `include!` line to `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`, near this one. It touches the same file, different line. Whichever merges second refreshes; the fix keeps both lines.
- #4408 (five-axis case) changes the example blocks of other kinds (Swarf, Contour, Flow) in `site/content/guide/multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md`. It touches the same file, different blocks. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Example catalog: new case multiaxis/wrapped, a grooved bar cut with Rotary Offset, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Contour on the A axis.

Fixes #2869

title: test(motion): fold the motion integration tests into domain directory suites
body:
## What changed

- The 153 flat, non-slow test files of `crates/motion/tests/` move into ten domain directory suites:
  - `adaptive2d` (17 modules)
  - `contour2d` (20)
  - `machining2d` (22)
  - `holes` (13)
  - `entry_links` (12)
  - `machining3d` (16)
  - `finishing3d` (13)
  - `multiaxis` (14)
  - `turning` (20)
  - `edges_edm` (6)
- Each suite has a `main.rs` that declares one module for each former file.
- The `SLOW_BINARIES` `finish3d`, `pivot5d` and `flow` stay flat binaries. Batch still skips them, and release still runs them.
- `rest_adaptive` and `rotary_flow` were directory suites before. They do not change.
- `camcraft-motion` now has 15 test binaries. Before this change it had 158.
- The files move with `git mv`. Git shows most of them as pure renames. In 14 moved files, one or two lines change:
  - Five `mod common;` lines become `use crate::common;`. The suite root declares `common` one time.
  - The three `adaptive_troch_*` files share `common/adaptive_troch.rs`. The `adaptive2d` root declares it one time as `fixtures`. Clippy `duplicate_mod` refuses three copies in one binary. Their two ignore reasons now name the `motion heavy: adaptive2d` step.
  - `arc_turn_kinds`, `adaptive_orbit_seam` and `rotary_adaptive` get a `../` prefix on one `#[path]` or `include_str!`. `tests/fixtures/` and `tests/rotary_adaptive_fixture/` stay in place, because the lib unit tests also read them.
  - Two regenerate commands in doc comments name the new suite.
- The Gate map paragraphs stay in the modules. The gate reads them through the suite root (#3186).
- xtask: two live-tree tests named old binaries. Now they name the suites that hold `arcs` (`contour2d`) and `cross_invariance` (`holes`). This is an expected change.
- `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md`: the links to moved files point to the new paths.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3189-fold-motion-suites.md`.

## Cause

Each flat file was a separate test binary. Each binary links the full crate again. The issue measured 4.03 GB for one target set (#919).

## Tests

- Pin: `motion_tests_fold_into_at_most_sixteen_binaries` (xtask, `directory_selection_tests.rs`). The pin reads the live tree. It checks that motion has at most 16 test binaries, and that each motion slow binary is still a flat file.
  - Red on unchanged upstream/main c79c9b24f: `158 motion test binaries (at most 16)`.
  - Green after the fold (15 binaries).
- Test counts, `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests -- --list`:
  - before: 2014 tests, 78 ignored (`--list --ignored`);
  - after: 2014 tests, 78 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests` (all binaries, debug, 6 test threads): all green, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 12 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (19.4 min). It ran the ten new suites and the xtask unit tests.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head: 9 steps (release build and 8 `motion heavy:` suites), 0 failed, 0 stalled (9.0 min). `edges_edm` and `turning` have no ignored tests, so they have no heavy step.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`needless_bool`). This PR does not change that file; its text is the same as on upstream/main. xtask is not in the gate clippy list.

## Goldens moved

None. This PR changes no generator code, and no test writes a golden. I did not run `example_catalog`: it is an app suite, and this PR does not change app or any generator.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate batch`. The issue names it in "Done means". I ran the quick tier (all ten new suites) and the motion heavy lanes. The post-merge gate runs batch on main.
- `cargo xtask gate light`. The heavy run covers the full tests of the light twins.
- Disk and build time saving: not measured on this machine.
- Wall time: some suites are now long in debug. In the quick gate (16 test threads) `adaptive2d` took 190 s, `entry_links` 167 s and `machining3d` 96 s. Batch runs suites in parallel lanes. No single test changed. The decision record says how to split a suite that proves too slow.

## Overlaps

These open PRs change files that this PR moves. They change other lines, not the same functions. Git rename detection can carry their edits to the new paths. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #4379 (`rotary.rs`)
- #4316 (`center_cut_owed.rs`)
- #4173 (`chamfer_*`, `climb_direction.rs`, `deburr.rs`, and a new `chamfer_circular/leads.rs`: that support directory must move to `edges_edm/chamfer_circular/`)
- #3103 (draft: several files, and a new flat `bore_helix.rs`, which must join the `holes` suite)
- #4328 and #4383 add `kernel_laws` and change `common/`. They do not change the moved files.

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Effort: medium

Fixes #3189

title: feat(post): Cobra Cut D 0.25 qualities for one 40 mm Agie punch
body:
## What changed

- Two new machine conditions select two new Agie work qualities:
  - `AGIE_COBRA_RA030` requests `CCD030`: Ra 0.30, a main cut and three trims.
  - `AGIE_COBRA_RA070` requests `CCD070`: Ra 0.70, a main cut and two trims.
- `agie_setup::Quality` gets `Ccd030` and `Ccd070`. Each has its measured 40 mm offsets:
  - CCD030: 250, 170, 145 and 135 µm.
  - CCD070: 245, 165 and 140 µm.
- `Quality::wire()` gives the native wire name. The piece and each work write `ID_THREAD` from it. A Cobra job writes `Cobra Cut D 0.25` two times and no `Berco`.
- The clearance and miter checks use the rough (first) offset of the selected quality.
- The operator review names the wire, the offsets and the number of TECCUT passes.
- Refusals. No file is written for these:
  - The encoder refuses other heights with `SetupError::UnqualifiedCobraHeight`.
  - The post refuses a die opening, an open cutoff, a punch group and a DXF arc punch. The group and arc refusal now names the selected condition and its height.
- The 1 mm separation is unchanged.
- The user guide and the site page have a new Cobra Cut D section.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2986-agie-cobra-40.md`.

## Cause

The native post knew only Berco Cut 0.25 qualities. It wrote the wire as a fixed string at piece and work level.

## Tests

Pins (both red before the fix):
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::cobra_tests`:
  - `cobra_cut_d_sets_the_wire_and_quality_of_a_40_mm_punch`. The expected SBL is the Berco 40 mm SBL with only the quality line and the two wire values replaced.
  - `cobra_cut_d_refuses_other_heights_and_sides_without_files`
  - `the_setup_encoder_holds_cobra_cut_d_to_40_mm`
  - `cobra_cut_d_bounds_the_cut_with_its_own_rough_offset`
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` `cobra::`. These run the CLI on the shipped examples and include a project save and load:
  - `a_cobra_condition_requests_its_quality_and_wire_on_a_40_mm_punch`
  - `a_cobra_condition_refuses_other_heights_without_a_directory`
  - `a_cobra_condition_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff`
  - `a_cobra_condition_with_another_wire_diameter_is_refused`. This one is a guard. It already passed before the fix, because the existing condition and tool gate refuses the mismatch.

Red before the fix:
- The post pins did not compile, because `Ccd030`, `Ccd070`, `wire()` and `UnqualifiedCobraHeight` did not exist.
- The app pins failed with `Select AGIE_QN2 (Fine Ra 0.30 µm) or AGIE_BERCO_RA035 ...`.

Mutations. Each mutation was put in, run, and restored:
1. Old `piece.rs` with the fixed Berco wire: red in the post and app wire pins.
2. Clearance with the QN2 rough offset instead of the quality's offset: `cobra_cut_d_bounds_the_cut_with_its_own_rough_offset` red.
3. The encoder maps Cobra to `UnqualifiedQualityHeight`: `the_setup_encoder_holds_cobra_cut_d_to_40_mm` red.
4. The group refusal names `AGIE_BERCO_RA035`: the app refusal pin red. This mutation survived the first version of the test, so I made the test stronger.

Gate on the final tree (`7a68cb5b3`, base `b2afd64ed`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 361 steps, 0 failed. This includes `post suites: agie_safe_setup`, `agie_inspection`, `app suites: agie_native`, `example_catalog*`, `wire_post` and `wire_post_alias`.
- After the gate, one test edit fixed a clippy finding. Then `cargo xtask gate test cobra --binary agie_native` passed (4 of 4) and `cargo xtask gate test quality --binary agie_native` passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 1 step (release build), ok. No light twin was selected.
- Heavy lanes: not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 75 app heavy steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives no heavy step to a P6 PR and no full heavy lane to any PR.
- The branch merges cleanly with the current `upstream/main` (`878f8c2f2`). That main has no change in the touched files.

## Goldens moved

None. The `example_catalog*`, `agie_native` and `agie_safe_setup` suites ran green, with all Berco goldens byte-equal. No new golden file was added. The tests derive the Cobra SBL from the Berco output.

## Not exercised

- A real or emulated Agie control import of a Cobra job. The offsets come from the two synthetic offline jobs of the issue. They are motion values, not a surface measurement.
- Te, Tkm and the three options of the request copy CCB030 (1.50, 1.00, three disabled). The issue gives no other values. See the decision file.
- No UI change. The post dialog line still names only AGIE_QN2.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes the touched Agie files.

Changelog: Agie Wire EDM: conditions AGIE_COBRA_RA030 and AGIE_COBRA_RA070 request qualities CCD030 (Ra 0.30) and CCD070 (Ra 0.70) with Cobra Cut D 0.25 wire for one 40 mm polygon punch. Other heights and work types are refused.

Effort: high

Fixes #2986

title: feat(post): pattern folders with linear and grid copies at the post
body:
Effort: high

## What changed

This PR adds a pattern folder to the operation list. A folder holds member operations of one setup. The post writes the members again at each enabled copy of a linear or grid pattern. All copies use the WCS of the setup: the moves shift, and the work offset stays the same.

- Schema: `PatternDef` in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`. It has `setup`, `suppressed`, `order_mode` (`ByTool` is the default, or `ByPart`), `kind` (`Linear` or `Grid`), `members` and `disabled_instances`. The copy numbers start at 1. Copy 1 is where the members are now.
- Row law: a folder is a list row, the same as a Pause entry. It uses `OperationMeta::order` for its position. Its members stand directly after it, in folder order. The commands keep this order. A member moves only inside its folder.
- Commands (`crates/app/src/commands/pattern_folder.rs`): `CreatePatternFolder`, `EditPatternFolder`, `SetPatternMembers`, `SetPatternInstanceEnabled` and `DeletePatternFolder`. Delete ungroups the members. Each command is undoable.
  - `ReorderOperation` and `RenameOperation` take folders.
  - `DeleteOperation` and `DeleteEntity` remove a deleted member from its folder. Undo puts it back.
- Validation at command creation: the command checks counts (1-1000), the total copies (10000 at most), spacings (finite, above 0) and directions (finite, in XY, not zero). Grid directions must not be parallel. It also checks members: each is a milling operation, is not a probe, is in one setup, is named once and is in no other folder. Nested folders are not possible because a member must be an operation. At least one copy must stay on.
- cl: `cl::transform::copies` (`crates/cl/src/cl/transform_copies.rs`) joins the translated copies of one path. Between two copies, the link goes straight up to the clearance plane, across, then straight down. Cycle anchors and compensated spans move with their copy. Plasma and tilted moves are refused by name.
- Posting (`crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs`):
  - `ByTool`: each member is one section over all enabled copies, so it has one `T.. M6`.
  - `ByPart`: all members cut one copy, then the next copy. The after-action and the setup-change stop go only on the last section of each operation.
  - The post refuses these cases by name: a turned or flipped WCS, a member that is missing or in another setup, and members that are not directly after the folder.
  - `viewer_map` maps every line of every copy.
  - Per-operation files refuse a `ByPart` folder by name.
- Verification gate: each shifted copy is checked against the machine travel of the setup (`MachineCheck::check_path`) and against its fixtures (`fixture_struck::op_hits`). A not-judged line names the folders whose other copies the stock sim does not judge.
- Project file: a new entity kind, `pattern`, with no version step. A document with no folder saves the same bytes as before. An older build refuses the unknown kind by name. The folder's display name is saved too.
- MCP (`crates/app/src/mcp/pattern_tools.rs`): new tools `create_pattern_folder`, `edit_pattern_folder`, `set_pattern_members`, `set_pattern_instance_enabled` and `delete_pattern_folder`. `get_job` lists `pattern_folders` only when the document has one. `rename_operation` and `reorder_operation` accept a folder.
- Docs: I regenerated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`, and I added a row to the guide table (`site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md`). The camcraft-mcp skill has new tool rows (process file).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3012-pattern-folder.md`.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the new MCP tool rows only).

## Tests

These pins are in the `mcp` directory suite (`crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder.rs`, `pattern_folder_post.rs`) and in the cl unit tests:

- `pattern_folder::a_folder_is_created_reordered_renamed_and_undone`
- `pattern_folder::edits_members_copies_and_delete_are_undoable`
- `pattern_folder::bad_patterns_and_members_are_refused_when_the_command_is_made`
- `pattern_folder::folders_round_trip_and_documents_without_them_write_no_key`
- `pattern_folder_post::by_tool_posts_each_member_once_over_every_enabled_copy`: linear, copy 2 off, golden. The tool changes are the same as the program without the folder.
- `pattern_folder_post::by_part_posts_every_member_at_one_copy_then_the_next`: grid, copy 4 off, golden, and the per-op refusal.
- `pattern_folder_post::a_folder_the_post_cannot_write_refuses_by_name`: out-of-block member order, turned WCS.
- `pattern_folder_post::mcp_tools_create_edit_reorder_undo_save_and_open_a_folder`
- `cl::transform::copies::tests::*` (6 tests)

Mutation checks (each guard file put back to `upstream/main`, then the pins run):

- `posting.rs`: the by-tool, by-part and refusal pins are red.
- `commands/operation/meta.rs`, `commands/delete_entity.rs` and `posting_per_op.rs`: the reorder, delete, rename, MCP and per-op pins are red.
- With the fix restored, all pins are green.

Gate results, against `upstream/main`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: the cl change makes the quick tier fall back to the batch tier, with 1231 steps (36.4 min).
  - 1230 steps passed. This includes every app suite and the `example_catalog*` suites.
  - The one failure was a clippy lint (`err().expect()`) in the new per-op pin. Commit `eaa90f1d6` fixes it.
  - On the final head `eaa90f1d6`, the gate's own `clippy -D warnings` step and the `app suites: mcp` step ran again. Both are green.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass (15.9 min).
- Heavy lanes: not run (see "Not exercised"). `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 116 steps.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

There are two new goldens, made with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. No existing golden changed.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_linear_by_tool.nc`: 3 sections and 3 tool changes. Each link between copies is one `G00` at Z25.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_grid_by_part.nc`: 7 sections. Face1 is first, then Face2 and Face3 at copies 1, 2 and 3.

The example catalog suites ran as part of the gate. They have no folder, so their output does not change.

At the start of each copy, a `G00` repeats the point where the link ended. This line comes from the face path's own first rapid. It does not move the tool.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: I did not run them. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) says that a P6 PR gets no heavy step. `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` shows the reach.
- The stock sim and the gouge check judge each member at copy 1 only. The stock-bounds check for the copies is also not done. This work is #3013. The not-judged line says this on every surface that reports the post.
- If a setup has no machine, the travel of a shifted copy is not checked. The program's own limit check still uses the default machine.
- UI: the browser shows a folder as a plain row. The folder UI is #3016.
- G52 and M98 output for compact programs is #3017.
- `verification_report` translates each copy of each member when it runs. A very large pattern can make the report slow.

## Overlaps

These PRs change the same files but other functions. The PR that merges second must refresh:

- #4288: `posting.rs` (`post_serves`, `HeightRefs`) and `project/file.rs` (`ToolKindDto`).
- #4368: `schema.rs`, `delete_entity.rs`, `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs` (append rows).
- #4379 and #4173: `project/file.rs`.
- #4302 and #4238: `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs`.
- #4383: `lib.rs`.

title: test(post,sim): fold the flat integration tests into domain directory suites
body:
## What changed

- `crates/post/tests/` had 143 flat test binaries. It now has 9 directory suites.
- `crates/sim/tests/` had 95 flat test binaries. It now has 8 directory suites.
- Each old file is a module of one suite (`tests/<suite>/<old name>.rs`). Its text did not change, except for these mechanical edits:
  - `mod recorded;` and the other shared helpers (`inverted_support`, `mirror_trace`, `macro_b`, `ac_trunnion_support`) became `use crate::<helper>;`. Each suite's `main.rs` declares a helper one time, by `#[path]`.
  - `legacy_program` (in `script_dialects`) and `coincident_arcs/reader.rs` (in `script_arcs`) are declared one time in `main.rs`. `clippy::duplicate_mod` refuses two declarations in one binary.
  - Each relative `include_str!` / `include_bytes!` and `#[path]` path gained one `../`.
  - A doc command `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test <old>` now reads `--test <suite> <old>::`.
- A submodule directory with one owner moved with its owner: `agie_safe_setup`, `fanuc_post`, `heidenhain_cycles`, `sodick_ln2w`, `upright_after_tilt`, `richauto_safety` and sim `model_excess`.
- The data directories did not move: `golden/`, `recorded/`, `klartext/`, `coincident_arcs/`. Other crates read them by path.
- `recorded::tmp` adds a per-process counter to the temp file name. One process now runs all script modules in parallel. Two modules that post the same script and case must not write the same file.
- `every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` now looks in `tests/script_goldens/`. It also checks that `main.rs` declares each script module.
- Six `xtask` pins named old post and sim binaries. They now name the suite that holds the module (`fanuc_post` is in `script_dialects`, and so on).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` and `docs/tester-kits/fanuc-mgi-blank/README.md` name the new paths.

Post suites: `script_goldens`, `script_cycles`, `script_probe`, `script_wcs`, `script_rotary`, `script_edm`, `script_dialects`, `script_arcs`, `post_engine`.
Sim suites: `stock_engines`, `stock_field`, `stock_carry`, `fixture_laws`, `reach_laws`, `gouge_laws`, `rest_credit`, `sim_timeline`.

All post suite names match `OUTPUT_SUITES` in `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` (`post_engine`, `script_*`). A red post suite on main is still a wrong-output failure, and that workflow script does not change.

## Cause

Each flat file in `tests/` is its own binary. Each binary links the crate and its dependencies again. Issue #919 measured about 5.2 GB of disk for each worktree for these two crates.

## Tests

- Test list, before and after (`cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim --tests -- --list`): 2353 tests before and 2353 after. A script matched each old test name to exactly one new name with a module prefix: 0 missing, 0 extra.
- `#[test]` count in the source: 1579 before (post 917, sim 662) and 1579 after.
- Binaries: 242 test targets before, 21 after (17 suites, the 2 libs, and 2 bin targets).
- Pin `recorded_streams::every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` (suite `script_goldens`):
  - It was red after the fold and before the fix ("has no suite .../tests/script_fanuc.rs").
  - Mutation: I removed `mod script_fanuc;` from `script_goldens/main.rs`. The pin was red. I restored the line. The pin was green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 31 steps, 0 failed (post lib, the 9 post suites, the 8 sim suites, xtask unit tests). An earlier run on the first commit also ran about 70 app suites for a `crates/post/src` comment: all green; that comment is no longer in the diff.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 365 passed, 0 failed (with the asset and gate-map tests).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`if` guard returns a bool literal). This PR does not touch that file. The same error is on `upstream/main`.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans 0 steps. The heavy lanes cover only `HEAVY_CRATES` (kernel, motion, app). The 5 `#[ignore]`d heavy tests of sim had no heavy step before this PR, and they have none after; that is not a change. They are still in their suites (`stock_field`, `fixture_laws`, `rest_credit`) and `cargo test -- --list` lists them.

## Goldens moved

None. No post script, machine file or generator changed. The fold moves test sources only. The goldens and recorded streams stay at their paths, and every golden test ran green in the quick gate. I did not run the `example_catalog` suites: no post or toolpath output changed.

## Not exercised

- The `recorded::tmp` counter has no test of its own. A race between two modules with one tag is not deterministic, so a test cannot make it fail every time.
- The release tier was not run. The 5 heavy-lane sim tests (`#[ignore]`d) are still in the suites. The heavy plan finds them (see above).
- Windows and macOS were not built. The change is paths in Rust source with `/`, which all three hosts read.

## Overlaps

These open PRs edit files that this PR moves. Git applies their edits to the renamed files when they merge main. A PR that adds a new flat file must move it into a suite:
- #4395 (`script_heidenhain_klartext.rs`, `klartext/`).
- #4387 (`script_heidenhain.rs`).
- #4380 (`recorded/mod.rs`, different function).
- #4371 (`setup_change.rs`, `upright_after_tilt.rs` and their directories).
- #4298 (`tormach_lathe_post.rs`, `tormach_plasma_post.rs`).
- #4009 (sim `undercut_laws.rs`, `verify_avoid_undercut.rs`).
- #2646 (adds `script_hurco_winmax.rs` and other new post files). `every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` will ask for `script_goldens/script_hurco_winmax.rs`.

Whichever merges second refreshes.

Follow-up: #4420 (old test paths in code comments of `crates/post/src`, `crates/app/tests`, `crates/gcode/tests` and the GPU fixtures).

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Fixes #3188

## What changed

`assets/machines/fehlmann-picomax55.mch`:

## Readings and choices

- Travel zero point: the file format says a slide of stroke L is written -L..L (the full stroke each way from the work origin). The manual gives only the strokes: X 500, Y 255, Z (quill) 147 mm. The file follows that rule and the other shipped files.
- Spindle mount: SF32 is not in `SPINDLE_MOUNTS` and the holder library has no SF32 holders yet (#3919 waits for measurements). So `tooling.spindle_mount` stays out. The description says why.
- Max spindle speed stays 9000. This machine has the 9000 rpm spindle. The manual lists 7100 for the standard spindle.
- No maximum tap size is stored. The manual's M20 is for steel 700 N/mm2. The capacity depends on the material.
- Feed rates are unchanged.

title: fix(post): the Mazak preamble states G94
body:
## What changed

The Mazak post wrote every F word as a feed per minute, but it never wrote `G94`. A control in `G95` (from its power-on setting, an earlier program or MDI) reads `F1200` as 1200 mm per revolution.

Each section preamble of `assets/posts/mazak.cps` now writes `G94` with its other modal words:

```
G17 G90 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80
```

This is the block that the Haas post writes. #4150 (PR #4169) did the same for the Sinumerik 840D preamble. Each section restates `G94`, so a restart at a later section also gets it. The decision file `docs/decisions/4343-mazak-g94.md` records the dropped option (`G94` once in `onOpen`).

## Goldens moved

29 Mazak goldens. Each changes in its preamble line only (`G17 G90 G5x` to `G17 G90 G94 G5x`):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mazak/*.nc` (17), `golden/nc/inch/mazak/*.nc` (2) and `golden/nc/synth_mazak.nc`;
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/mazak/*.nc` (7), `golden/wcs_flip/mazak_x.nc` and `golden/explain/mazak.nc`.

In `golden/explain/mazak.nc` the preamble comment now reads `(XY PLANE, ABSOLUTE POSITIONS, FEED PER MINUTE)`. The post's `commentMax` of 60 keeps whole meanings only, so "WORK OFFSET 1" no longer fits. The Haas explain golden ends the same way for the same block.

No other post and no toolpath changes.

## Pinning tests

New suite `crates/post/tests/mazak_feed_mode.rs`:

- `every_mazak_section_states_g94_before_its_first_feed`: a two-section program, metric and inch. Each section preamble is `G17 G90 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80`, and no F word comes before a `G94`.
- `every_recorded_mazak_program_feeds_per_minute`: each recorded Mazak golden that feeds states `G94` first.

Both tests fail on `upstream/main`'s `mazak.cps` and goldens. Both pass with the fix.

The golden suites `script_mazak`, `conformance`, `program_units`, `control_comp` and `wear_comp` were rewritten with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` and pass.

- Quick gate on e33fc70b9 (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 859 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 94.7 min.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-post -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on e33fc70b9: 74 steps (1 build, 73 `app`), 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 47.6 min. The known fails #1950 and #2849 are red as expected.

PR #4380 (#2528) adds a recorded stream `drill_full_diameter` with a new golden `recorded/golden/mazak/drill_full_diameter.nc`. That golden has the old preamble. The PR that merges second must write that golden again (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_mazak`).

title: test(pathkernel): each law assertion can break, and a refusal is never held
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Fix for class A of the review of PR #4383 (2026-11-27T18:06:55Z, head `7cd322966`). This PR changes only test code in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/` and one decision file. It does not change `crates/pathkernel/src`.

## The rule that closes the class

Each law assertion can break, and a refusal never counts as held. `kit::LawVerdict` now has an `Outcome`: `Held`, `Broken` or `Refused(reason)`. A leg that a stage refused, or a leg with nothing to read, is `Refused`. A `Refused` leg is never held. `judge` gives `Broken` when a measure that it read is above its limit. Else it gives `Refused` when a leg was refused or unread, or when there is no measure. It gives `Held` only when it read each leg and each leg is at or below its limit. `refused_held` (0 against 0) is removed.

## Each item of class A, and its commit

All items are in commit `14d718ffe8f509c7dcd90343503998ba185cf05d`.

| Review item | Rule applied |
|---|---|
| `l7_move.rs:32-35`, `:58-62`: L7 compares the kernel with its own output | The record is read from a file in `tests/laws/records/`. The file was recorded one time and the test does not write it. The square record can be checked by hand: ten rings 0.8 mm apart in the 16 mm centre square. The old-planner L7 stays at the motion level, because this crate cannot depend on motion. The decision is in `docs/decisions/4406-law-suite-refusal-never-held.md`. |
| `kit.rs:116-118` with `l5_entry.rs:24-28`, `l6_load.rs:18-21`, `l3_order.rs:32-39`: a refusal is held | `Outcome::Refused`. L5, L6, the link rule and the registry use `kit::refused`. In L3, a refusal on each side is refused, and a refusal on one side only is broken. In the registry, `KindRecipe.refusals` (`ExpectedRefusal { case, reason }`) and `law_failures` make `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` fail for a broken law and for each refusal that the kind did not register. |
| `l5_entry.rs:40`: a full-fill IntoMaterial entry passes at 0.0 | The check reads an IntoMaterial descent onto material. The descent must move one grid cell or more in the plane, or be a plunge that the user asked for. Else the check is broken, measured by the fill. The stand-in helix was a one-point descent, and it is now one real turn. |
| `l6_load.rs:38-39`: a report row that is always held | The row is removed. The highest read is now in the place text of each cut row. |
| `l2_sides.rs:39-52`: a refused side reads 0.0/0.0 and the Inside leg is skipped | A refusal of one material side is broken. A refusal of both sides is refused. A side flip that the kit cannot make is broken. The order leg is never skipped. |
| Note `l1_guide.rs:34-35`: refusals match on the reason alone | Two refusals are not compared now. A refused first call is refused. A later call that refuses where the first call gave curves is broken. |
| Audit of the remaining checks | An empty measure list is refused. In L4, a guide with no curve or an entry verdict with no entry is unread. In L3, L5 and L6, an empty run is unread. In the link rule, a non-planar region is a refused leg, and a stay hop of zero length is read at its points. |

Citations: `tests/laws.rs` now points to `RECOMMENDED.md` (heading `#4024`) and `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`. No other file under `tests/laws/` cited `4024-path-kernel-design.md`.

## Pins

For each law, one stand-in breaks it, and one stand-in always refuses and is reported as refused:

| Law | Breaks (caught) | Always refuses (refused, not held) |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | `Drifting`, `Seam`, a shared guide that differs; `RingGuide` against a refusing shared `NoGuide` | `NoGuide` (`l1_is_refused_for_a_guide_that_always_refuses`) |
| L2 | `blind_region`, `MaterialOrder`, `no_outside` (`l2_breaks_for_a_region_that_refuses_one_material_side`) | `no_region`, `NoOrder` (`l2_is_refused_for_a_region_or_an_order_that_always_refuses`) |
| L3 | `SideMoves` (move, drop) | `NoGuide`, `NoOrder`, `NoLoad`, `NoEntry`, a refusing exit (`l3_l5_l6_and_the_link_rule_are_refused_for_a_refused_run`) |
| L4 | `RowsAsRings { named: false }`, `RampInstead { named: false }` | through `check_all` (`no_law_is_held_on_an_always_refusing_planner_set`) |
| L5 | `ClaimsFree` (air, column), `HiddenPlunge` (`l5_breaks_for_a_plunge_into_material_named_a_helix`) | `NoEntry` (`l5_is_refused_never_held_for_a_named_refusal`), the five refusing stages |
| L6 | `ReadLoad { blind: true }` | the five refusing stages |
| L7 | a moved ring, another direction, no record, an empty record against cuts, a record against a refused run | an empty record and a refused run (`l7_is_not_held_for_an_empty_record_or_a_refused_run`) |
| Link | `BadLink::{Silent, Always, Across}` | the five refusing stages |

`no_law_is_held_on_an_always_refusing_planner_set` runs every check on a planner set where each stage refuses, and on a case where the region refuses. No law is held. Each law except L7 is refused. L7 is broken, because the record has cuts and the kernel refused. The runner pins are `the_law_runner_fails_a_kind_whose_stage_refuses_a_case` and `an_expected_refusal_does_not_hide_a_broken_law`.

## What now fails for real (old passes that were hollow)

- `guide_laws.rs`: the medial planner, the circle rings and the helix planner held L2 only because their fixture regions had no stock. The real region stage refuses the Outside side by name: "an Outside material side needs the stock: the area outside the selection has no limit". The old L2 read that refusal as 0 against 0. With the new rule, L2 broke for each of the three (measured inf against the limit 0). The fix is in the test fixture: it now gives a stock box (10 mm and four tool radii at each side). L2 is now measured and holds. The check did not change, and no kernel source changed.
- The stand-in helix was a plunge with the name of a helix. The new L5 leg catches this case.
- L6 breaker pin: the real helix now clears the centre of the first ring. The worst unnamed read is now a ring corner at ae/D 0.711 against the cap 0.625, not 0.9 or more. The pin now asks for more than 0.7. The check did not change.
- No kind is `Moved` yet, so `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` still runs no case. The runner is pinned by the tests above.

## Results (final head `14d718ffe`)

- `cargo check --tests -p camcraft-pathkernel`: ok
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 173 passed, 0 failed (163 before)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 1 step (`pathkernel:laws`), ok

## Not exercised

- No motion or app tests: this PR does not touch them. The motion-level L7 comparison (`crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/`, `pass_start_levels/kernel_baseline`) did not change.
- The light lane did not run. The diff is only in the kernel laws suite, and it does not change a post or a toolpath.
- `records/pocket_with_an_island.txt` was recorded from the stand-ins. Only the square record was checked by hand.

New files: `tests/laws/kit_geo.rs` (the geometry helpers moved out of `kit.rs` because of the 400-line law), `tests/laws/refusals.rs` and `tests/laws/records/*.txt`. All of them are in the existing `laws` directory suite. No new test binary.

- One 6 mm move in `rest.nc` moved to `X5.79 Y-8.387 Z12`: the region pin goes red with `6 mm feed moves outside the rest region: [(5.79, -8.387, 12.0)]`. The case was rebuilt after: green.

Commands on the final head `d56e967f0`:

title: feat(ui): tool library U12 - Holders page search and the user holder form
body:
## What changed

U12 of #3663: the Holders page of the tool library window gets a search and a header row, and a user holder opens in an editable holder form.

**List (screen 4)**
- One header row: the search box, the count "N of M holders", **New holder…**, **Import…** and **Export…**.
- The search matches the taper, the clamp, a bore or collet size and the name. Each term must match ("BT40 ER32", "shrink 12"). A number also matches a holder that clamps a shank of that size ("er 16" shows the ER chucks that take Ø16). Esc in the box clears it.
- The search result is kept for its input (`state_holder_search.rs`). A still frame searches nothing.
- The read-only note and the empty "USER HOLDERS" text are removed from the list. The user holders section shows when the document has a user holder.
- **New holder…** copies the ER32 chuck of the machine taper (else BT40 ER32) as a user holder (one undo step) and opens it in the form.
- **Import…** and **Export…** are disabled. Their hover text names #4389.

**Holder form (screen 5)**
- Inputs: Name, Spindle taper, Clamp (ER11 to ER50, Weldon side lock, shrink fit), Clamps from / to, Gauge length, Largest diameter, Nose diameter (mm).
- The drawing to scale has the spindle nose box above the gauge line and the shank range below the nose. The drawing keeps room for its labels, so no label is cut off (`holder_drawing.rs`, shared with the read-only view).
- "Used by N tools" lists the tools whose component stack uses the holder. A click opens the tool.
- Footer: Duplicate, Cancel, Apply. The hint says "Apply updates N tools. It is one undo step."
- Apply is one undoable `EditDocumentComponent`. It derives each tool that uses the holder again in the same undo step. An edit that breaks the fit of a tool is refused by name, and nothing changes.
- A value that cannot describe steel is refused by name before Apply. Apply is then disabled with the reason, and the reason shows under the fields.
- A built-in holder opens read-only, with "Copy as user holder", as before.
- **Edit outline…** and **Import model (STEP)…** are disabled. Their hover text names #4390.

**Outline safety (crates/tools)**
- New `holder_library::HolderShape` (`holder_library_shape.rs`). The form's values build the outline with the holder library's own `HolderEntry::points`. Thus the law "never smaller than the steel" holds for the stated values: the ER nut over its full length, the Weldon body plus `WELDON_SCREW`, the shrink nose and body plus `SHRINK_MARGIN`, the flange as a full cylinder.
- `HolderShape::of` reads the shape back from a component. It accepts the shape only when the outline that the shape makes is the outline of the component. A holder with another outline (a DXF profile) opens in the generic component editor, as before.
- No project-file change: the shape comes from the machine side, the workpiece side and the outline.

UI choices: `docs/decisions/4338-holders-page.md`.

## Pinning tests

`crates/tools` (`holder_library::shape::tests`):
- `each_builtin_taper_holder_reads_back_as_its_shape`
- `an_edited_outline_is_never_smaller_than_the_steel` (samples the outline of a grid of edited shapes against the stated steel, and the flange)
- `a_value_that_cannot_be_steel_is_refused_by_name`
- `an_outline_from_elsewhere_is_not_a_form_shape`

`crates/ui` (`egui_app::tests::tool_library_holder_form`):

- `a_still_frame_searches_reads_and_checks_nothing` (counter tests for the search, the shape read, the check and the drawing; a changed input runs each again)
- `each_holder_field_lands_in_one_step_with_its_tools_and_undoes` (name, taper, gauge length, largest diameter, nose diameter: one undo step, both tools derive again, undo gives both back)
- `the_clamp_and_the_shank_range_land_and_undo` (New holder, clamp ER32 to Weldon, Clamps from / to sets the bore)
- `an_edit_that_breaks_a_tools_fit_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_built_in_holder_is_read_only_and_copies_and_duplicates`

Layout: `layout_window_holders` (updated: the header row) and `layout_window_holder_form` (new). Updated: `each_face_has_its_hint`, `a_built_in_holder_copies_as_a_user_holder_and_its_gauge_is_edited` (the copy opens in the form now).

`crates/ui` `#[test]` count: 1964 before, 1971 after.

All results are on head `82b8eca37` (lane mac-1, pool). This head merges `main` (the #1120 tool inks): the holder drawing uses the theme inks (`tool_axis`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge`, `tool_dim`, `tool_note`, `tool_ground`), so it adds no colour literal.

title: test(mcp): synchronize active-client idle refresh checks
body:
## What changed

The active-client test now queues each next complete ping before it releases the current owner reply. Client scheduling after a reply cannot create an unintended idle period. The test checks eight successful JSON replies over at least two idle windows. The same connection must then receive an idle notice and EOF when messages stop.

Only the test and its decision note changed. The listener, hello deadline, security rules, idle configuration, and existing negative tests did not change.

## Before and after

Baseline: `751a79b20327fa73743f032f2f3d99907334cbe3`.

The old test slept for 150 ms between replies and requests with a 400 ms idle window. A temporary Linux probe added a 300 ms scheduling delay after each reply. The old test failed with `BrokenPipe`. The synchronized test passed with the same delay and the original 400 ms window. This demonstrates the synchronization correction separately from the final scheduling allowance.

The final test uses a two-second idle window. Each owner reply waits for one quarter of that window. The elapsed assertion requires at least two windows of activity. Socket waits and request waits have a finite limit of three windows.

Two temporary negative controls confirmed the assertions:
- Removing the complete-message activity refresh failed during active replies with `ConnectionReset`.
- Disabling idle expiry failed at the final idle-notice read with `WouldBlock`.

Both mutations and all probe delays were removed before the final checks.

## Checks on `3f6a6c5e8950505e3caf29035a42c41749066856`

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: passed the complete `mcp_live` suite, 29 tests. This includes `a_client_that_keeps_talking_is_never_dropped_as_idle`, silent-client expiry, slow-loris expiry, idle configuration, and hello/security tests.
- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: passed all 11 light tests in five test steps. The broad build-only step was omitted; each selected test target compiled and ran.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The changed test function matches `rustfmt` output for edition 2024. `git diff --check` passed.

All checks used Linux and three jobs. Windows reproduction, Windows gates, full heavy lanes, release packaging, and machinery were not exercised. No post or toolpath changed, so catalog regeneration does not apply.

## Readings and decisions

Read the full issue thread, the current listener, the active-client test, and the idle-configuration tests. Decision: `docs/decisions/3230-live-idle-test.md`.

No scout was supplied. Direct reads covered those exact files, `crates/app/src/clock.rs`, the decision format, and current process skills. Direct Git history covered `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`. Fresh complete open-PR file inventories found no overlapping changed path and no release branch PR.

title: feat(ui-kit): a camcraft-ui-kit crate for the design system (tokens, theme files, contrast checks, gallery)
body:
Part of #4245 (step 0, PR K). This PR merges after PR R (#4393). The maintainer merges it: it adds a new crate edge and changes the workspace manifest.

Process change: yes

## What changed

- A new crate `crates/ui-kit` (`camcraft-ui-kit`). It depends on `egui` (`=0.36.2`, the workspace pin) and `serde_json` only. It has no `camcraft-*` dependency.
- These modules move from `crates/ui/src/egui_app/` into the kit. Their behaviour does not change:
  - `theme` (the `Tokens` table, `DARK`, `LIGHT`, `clamp`, `DropGeom`, `visuals`, `style`, `apply_to`, `ribbon_h`, `status_h`, the exhaustiveness guard);
  - `theme_files` (the `camcraft-theme/1` reader, the caps, the cache, `COLOR_NAMES`, `GEOM_NAMES`);
  - `contrast` (the WCAG arithmetic, the follow law, the readability gate), plus `light_ground` from `ground_ink`.
- The kit has its own `ThemeSource` enum and `resolve_source`, because it cannot see `camcraft_app::schema::ThemeRef`.
- `crates/ui` keeps the old module paths as re-exports: `egui_app::contrast`, `egui_app::theme::*`, `egui_app::theme_files::*` and `ground_ink::light_ground`. No other file of `crates/ui` changes, so the open UI PRs keep their paths. `panes.rs` is not touched.
- `crates/ui` keeps two things, and the decision entry gives the reasons:
  - the live theme cell (`current`, `set_current`, `apply`) and its tests, because its thread-local test form uses `#[cfg(test)]`, which applies per crate (#2373);
  - `theme_files::resolve(&mut Cache, &ThemeRef)`, which maps `ThemeRef` onto the kit's `ThemeSource`.
- A gallery page `camcraft_ui_kit::gallery`: widgets, the readability pairs, every colour token and every geometry token, for the dark and the light theme. The two token listings destructure `Tokens` without `..`, so a new token that the gallery does not show does not compile. The look follows the #4245 rules: a flat frame, a hairline, no shadow, a small radius, section headers from type.
- A gallery window `ui-kit-gallery` behind the feature `gallery`: `cargo run -p camcraft-ui-kit --features gallery --bin ui-kit-gallery`. `cargo test -p camcraft-ui-kit` does not build it.
- The decision entry `docs/decisions/4394-ui-kit-crate.md` for the edge `ui -> ui-kit`: the imported items, why the caller cannot pass them in, and what rebuilds.
- The colour-literal guard of `crates/ui` (`tests/theme_files/colour_literals.rs`) loses the rows of `contrast.rs` and `theme/tables.rs`, because these files are no longer in that crate.

## Gate crate lists (xtask, process file)

The gate does not discover crates. `xtask/src/plan.rs` has fixed lists. Without an entry, a diff in `crates/ui-kit` selects no test and no clippy run. This PR adds `ui-kit` to `ALL_CRATES`, `BATCH_CRATES` and `CLIPPY`, before `ui` (dependency order). Two xtask tests follow the new crate: `reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies` (the kernel does not reach `ui-kit`; `ui-kit` reaches `ui`) and the batch prebuild fixture in `step_tests.rs` (it writes a manifest for `ui-kit`). The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

## Dependency tree of the kit

`cargo tree -p camcraft-ui-kit -e normal,dev` (no feature): 58 crates, with no flecs, no `camcraft-*` crate, no wgpu, no winit and no eframe.

```
camcraft-ui-kit v0.27.0
├── egui v0.36.2
│   ├── accesskit, ahash, bitflags, emath, epaint, itertools, log,
│   └── nohash-hasher, profiling, smallvec, unicode-segmentation
└── serde_json v1.0.154
    └── itoa, memchr, serde_core, zmij
```

`Cargo.lock` adds only the `camcraft-ui-kit` package and its edge from `camcraft-ui`. There is no new third-party crate (`eframe` and `winit` are already in the lock).

## Tests

Pinning tests:

- `crates/ui-kit/tests/contrast.rs`: `both_builtin_columns_clear_their_own_gate`, `the_follow_law_round_trips_and_translates`, `an_accent_only_file_derives_its_family_and_says_so`, `unreadable_files_refuse_by_name` (moved unchanged).
- `crates/ui-kit/tests/gallery.rs`: `the_gallery_lists_each_token_once_by_its_file_name`, `hex_spells_colours_the_way_a_theme_file_does`, `the_reading_pairs_clear_their_floors_on_both_builtins`, `both_themes_lay_out_in_a_headless_context`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files/resolve_tests.rs`: `builtin_references_land_their_compiled_columns`, `a_stranger_name_refuses_by_name`, `a_file_reference_reads_through_the_kit_cache`, `the_old_paths_name_the_kit_items`.

Gate results on the final head `40e5d5d` (it includes a second merge of `origin/main` at `e4b08e9`, see "Merge of main"):

| Head | Lane | Step | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `40e5d5d` | mac-1 | `cargo xtask gate batch --only "debug build: ui" --only ui`: 32 steps (both builds, 3 ui-kit suites, all 29 ui suites including `ui suites: lib`) | 32 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled |
| `40e5d5d` | mac-1 | `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui-kit -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
| `40e5d5d` | mac-1 | `cargo test -p xtask` | ok |

Earlier heads: `376104a` had the same steps green (batch and clippy on winbuild, xtask on mac-1), plus `cargo build -p camcraft-ui-kit --features gallery --bin ui-kit-gallery` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui-kit -p xtask --all-targets --features camcraft-ui-kit/gallery -- -D warnings`. `c518ffe` had the same 32 steps green on winbuild.

The official `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` falls back to batch, because the diff touches `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. The runs above are the batch steps of the crates that this diff reaches. The winbuild plan shows that the gate finds the new crate: it has the steps `debug build: ui-kit` and `ui-kit suites: *`.

Not run: the batch steps of the engine crates and `camcraft-app` test binaries. The diff does not change these crates; `Cargo.lock` only adds the kit. The full builder run stopped at the full disk. No example catalog suite is required (no post or toolpath change). The light lane was not run (no heavy test is touched).

## Merge of main

First merge (`376104a`): `origin/main` added 18 tool tokens to `Tokens` and `with_alpha` (#1120, `d3e8dd705`, `5d2c2b2d6`). The merge carries them into the kit: `theme.rs`, `tables.rs`, `legal.rs`, `names.rs` and `overlay.rs` of the kit have them, and the gallery listings show them (the destructure guard asked for that). The new `theme/verdict.rs` stays in `crates/ui`: it holds impls on the shell types `Semantic` and `TextInks`. `ground_ink.rs` and the colour-literal rows take main's version with the change of this PR.

Second merge (`40e5d5d`): `origin/main` added the window close inks `close_hover` and `close_ink` (#1120 window chrome, `c859c79eb`).
- Git carried the new rows of `tables.rs`, `legal.rs`, `names.rs` and `overlay.rs` into the kit copies by rename detection.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme.rs` keeps the re-export seam of this PR. The two fields go into the `Tokens` struct and the `apply_to` destructure of `crates/ui-kit/src/theme.rs`.

- `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/colour_literals.rs` takes the list of main, minus the rows of the files that moved to the kit (`contrast.rs`, `theme/tables.rs`). Main removed the `error_text.rs` and `window_chrome.rs` rows, so they are gone here too.
- The new test `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/chrome_inks.rs` of main stays in `crates/ui`. It reads `Tokens` through the re-export.

## Test counts

- `origin/main` at `e4b08e9`: 1984 `#[test]` in `crates/ui`.
- This head: 1984 in `crates/ui` and 8 in `crates/ui-kit`, 1992 in total. Four contrast tests move to the kit. The PR adds 8 tests: four seam tests (`egui_app/theme_files/resolve_tests.rs`) and four gallery tests.

## Screenshots

This is a new page, so there is no "before". The images are a headless `egui_kittest` render of `gallery::show` and `gallery::show_theme` (a test file that is not committed). They are rendered again on `40e5d5d` and show the close inks.

title: feat(post): the Klartext post writes cycles 200, 206, 207 and the cycle 9 dwell
body:
## What changed

The Heidenhain Klartext post (`assets/posts/heidenhain-klartext.cps`) writes the drilling and tapping cycles and the dwell for the iTNC 530 NC 340490-03 (the Fehlmann Picomax 55 profile). Before this change, the post refused each cycle and each dwell.

| Stream cycle | Posted |
|---|---|
| DRILL, SPOT | `CYCL DEF 200 DRILLING` (Q200, Q201, Q206, Q202 = the whole depth, Q210 = 0, Q203, Q204 = Q200, Q211 = the dwell), then `CYCL CALL` |
| PECK, DEEP | the checked chain as `L` blocks (the #4224 precedent). No cycle 205 or 203. |
| TAP, rigid | `CYCL DEF 207 RIGID TAPPING NEW` (Q200, Q201, Q239 = feed / rpm, Q203, Q204) |
| TAP, floating holder | `CYCL DEF 206 TAPPING NEW` (Q200, Q201, Q206, Q211, Q203, Q204) |
| the dwell of PECK or DEEP | `CYCL DEF 9.0 DWELL TIME` and `CYCL DEF 9.1 DWELL <s>` after the feed to the depth |

- The parameter set is the resolver's `drillC200` level `q211` (no Q395; no Q208 or Q395 on cycle 205 either, because the post writes no cycle 205).
- The post defines a cycle again only when its words change. Each hole gets one `CYCL CALL`, with the tool at R over the hole.
- The post compares each chain move that a native cycle replaces with the motion of that cycle. A chain that differs is refused by name. Thus the native cycle does the motion that the simulation and the gouge check read.
- The post now accepts the tool kinds `drill` and `tap`. A drill or a tap cuts only inside its drilling cycle (a drill feeds only along the hole axis). A tapping cycle needs a tap tool.
- The post declares `floatingTapping = true`.
- The other output of the Picomax stays byte-identical: the `picomax.nc` golden and the refusal goldens did not change. The new code is below `onOpen`, so the script line numbers in the refusal goldens are the same.
- The DIN/ISO post `heidenhain.cps` did not change (#4226 works there).

Example (from the new golden `picomax_cycles.nc`):

```
30 L X+5 Y+5 Z+6 R0 FMAX
31 CYCL DEF 200 DRILLING ~
  Q200=+1 ~
  Q201=-10 ~
  Q206=+100 ~
  Q202=+10 ~
  Q210=+0 ~
  Q203=+5 ~
  Q204=+1 ~
  Q211=+0.5
32 CYCL CALL
...
79 L X+15 Y-5 Z-5 R0 F100
80 CYCL DEF 9.0 DWELL TIME
81 CYCL DEF 9.1 DWELL 0.3
...
104 CYCL DEF 207 RIGID TAPPING NEW ~
  Q200=+1 ~
  Q201=-8 ~
  Q239=+1 ~
  Q203=+5 ~
  Q204=+1
105 CYCL CALL
```

Decisions: `docs/decisions/4227-klartext-cycles.md`.

## Pinning tests

Binary `script_heidenhain_klartext` (crate `camcraft-post`), new module `crates/post/tests/klartext/cycle_tests.rs` (it joins the existing suite; no new test binary):
- `cycle_tests::klartext_cycles_post_on_the_picomax_golden` (new golden `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain-klartext/picomax_cycles.nc`, stream `crates/post/tests/klartext/cycles.cnc`)
- `cycle_tests::drill_posts_cycle_200_with_the_whole_depth_and_the_dwell_at_depth`
- `cycle_tests::peck_and_deep_post_the_checked_chain_and_deep_dwells_with_cycle_9`
- `cycle_tests::rigid_and_floating_taps_post_cycles_207_and_206`
- `cycle_tests::each_klartext_cycle_refusal_names_its_cause` (BORE, a cycle not at R, a chain that is not the cycle's motion, a tap cycle with a drill, a rigid tap dwell, a floating tap dwell above 0.5 s, a drill feed outside its cycle, a depth that differs from the chain)
- `cycle_tests::rigid_tapping_is_refused_on_a_machine_without_it`
- `milling_cutter_kinds_are_explicit_and_incompatible_tools_refuse_the_cli_save` (changed: drill and tap are refused outside a drilling cycle)

## Gate results

All results are on head `0ea1e7701f51886461703aa61a80b52f920112dd`.

- winbuild (`lanes --needs post`): `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_heidenhain_klartext`: 35 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- mac-1 (`lanes --needs app --pool`): `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 167 steps, all ok. These steps include the post suites, `conformance`, `klartext_builtin` and the example catalog suites `example_catalog` (28 s), `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`, and `first_part_programs`.
- mac-1: `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/main`: 6 steps, all ok.
- No heavy step (P6).

## Not exercised

- The program did not run on the control.
- The Klartext reader of PR #4361 is not on `main`. Thus there is no round-trip test through the reader. The reader reads cycle 200 and `CYCL CALL`. It does not read cycles 206 and 207 or the old-style cycle 9 blocks.
- The Picomax machine file states no `rigid_tapping`. The post writes cycle 207 when the machine does not state `false`, as the DIN/ISO post does with G207. The decision file says how to refuse it.
- The refusals for a cycle 200 level other than `q211` and for a dwell form other than cycle 9 cannot occur while the post accepts only NC 340490-03.

Changelog: The Heidenhain Klartext post writes drilling (cycle 200), rigid tapping (cycle 207), floating tapping (cycle 206) and the dwell (cycle 9) for the iTNC 530 NC 340490-03; peck and deep holes post as explicit moves.

Effort: high

Fixes #4227

body:
## Summary

- Report nonempty `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` and dynamic `CARGO_TARGET_<triple>_RUSTFLAGS` inputs. Preserve their values and the selected target.
- Report selected Cargo config paths from the plan's command directories, their ancestors, and Cargo home. Add ordinary rustflags, target and profile key hints.

- Apply the existing unit environment policy to the docs-images Cargo command.
- Test real inherited profile removal in isolated child processes. Inspect the renderer command without starting the renderer.

Every selected config file gets a warning, even without a recognized key. The hints are not effective configuration. Cargo still resolves precedence. The scan does not expand inline tables, escaped key names, includes, or multiline strings. No absence of a hint proves absence of an input. The decision record explains this conservative policy and the rejected alternatives.

- Issue #3155 and its complete current thread.

- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: PASS on the committed tree. The selected xtask tests and integration tests pass. The unit binary has 373 passing tests.

title: feat(post): Heidenhain DIN/ISO writes the G62 filter mode and checks the T range
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` writes the smoothing ask as `G62 T<tol> P01 <0|1> P02 0`. `P01 0` is finish and `P01 1` is rough, from `PARAM SmoothingMode`. `P02 0` is the value that the control inserts for a `G62` with T only.
- The dialect resolver has two new flags (`crates/post/src/post/heidenhain_profiles.rs`):
  - `g62_mode` (`no` / `yes` / `option2`): the control takes `P01`. On the iTNC 530 340 49x and 606 42x, `P01` needs software option 2 (HSC machining). The post writes it only when the machine file lists option 2.
  - `g62_t_max_um`: the largest documented T for each control and NC software (10 mm or 99999.999 mm; 0 = no cycle 32). Where a manual states no range, the post uses 10 mm, the narrowest documented range.
- The post refuses by name:
  - a T above the range of the control;
  - a positive T that rounds to `T0` (the control reads T 0 as the tolerance of the machine builder);
  - smoothing on a stated control without cycle 32 (TNC 410).
- Where `P01` is not written and the ask is rough, the post writes T only and gives a counted warning.
- A machine with no controller identity keeps the TNC 640 34059x-07 level of this post: `P01` is written.
- The sources and the dropped options are in `docs/decisions/4226-g62-smoothing.md`.

## Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03)

The output is byte-identical: `G62 T<tol>`. The machine file lists no installed options, and the iTNC 530 340 49x-03 ISO manual permits `P01`/`P02` only with option 2. The research does not prove that the current output is wrong for this control. New on this machine: a rough ask gives a warning, and a T above 10 mm is refused.

## What posts now (examples)

| Machine | Ask | Block |
|---|---|---|
| no controller identity, or TNC 640 340595-08 | 0.02 mm finish | `G62 T0.02 P01 0 P02 0` |
| same | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1 P01 1 P02 0` |
| Picomax 55 (no options listed) | 0.02 mm finish or rough | `G62 T0.02` (rough: warning) |
| iTNC 530 340490-03 with option 2 listed | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1 P01 1 P02 0` |
| TNC 430 280476-01 | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1` (warning) |
| TNC 640 340595-08 | 10.001 mm | refused: `smoothing tolerance T10.001 mm is above the largest T of TNC 640 NC 340595-08 (profile tnc640-c) (10 mm)` |
| TNC 410 286060-01 | 0.02 mm | refused: `has no tolerance cycle (cycle 32 / G62)` |

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `script_heidenhain`:

title: feat(ui): the Recipes tab explains recipes, stars the stock material, derives Vc and fz
body:
Was stacked on #4365. #4365 merged on 2026-11-27; this branch then took `git merge origin/main` (clean) and a new gate. The diff against `main` is now the commit of this PR only.

## What changed

U11 of the tool library refit (#3663): the Recipes tab of the tool library window.

- One line under the tabs says what a recipe is and which row operations take: "One recipe for each work material. The ★ marks the stock material of this document (Aluminium 6061): operations take that row." Other texts tell when no row names the stock material, or when no material is stated.
- A ★ stands in a narrow lead column on the row of the stock material in force. This is the stock material of the active setup, else the document material (`stock_material::in_force`). Operations use the same order. U5 marked the document material only.
- Under the table, each row has one dimmed line with its derived values: "= 226 m/min surface speed, 0.050 mm per tooth (Aluminium 6061)". The lines are read-only. They are computed only when their input changes (frame-cost rule, #2238). The cache is `ToolLibraryView::recipes`. The U5 columns "Vc" and "fz" are removed: they stood right of Stepover and scrolled out of view.
- The buttons stand on one row: **Add material…** (a menu of the materials without a row), **Suggest feeds and speeds** (a menu: the stock material first with the ★, then each material with a row) and **Copy recipes from tool…** (a menu of the other document tools). A disabled button or entry tells why on hover. A units note follows. Tool material and Flutes follow the note (U10 keeps them on this tab).
- Each button writes the window's draft only. The editor's one Apply lands the draft as one `ChangeTool`, so each button is one undo step. No command is new, so no MCP tool is owed.
- With the Recipes tab, the shared table does not draw its own "Add material row" button. Properties' Cutting data group keeps it.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/4337-recipes-tab.md`.

Files: `recipes_tab.rs`, the new `recipes_actions.rs` and `recipes_derived.rs`, `recipes_fill.rs`, the `Extra` hook in `tool_cutting_rows.rs`, one field in `state_tool_library_dialog.rs` and one `pub use` line in `state.rs`. Centre cutting stays where U10 puts it: this PR does not change `tool_settings_grid::cutting_base`.

## Screenshots

Before (#4365 head `b1365b233`, the U8 frame) and after, 1366 x 768, a three-flute carbide end mill with three material rows, document material Aluminium 6061:

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4385/before.png)

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4385/after.png)

## Tests

Pinning tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_recipes.rs` unless named):

- `the_star_follows_the_stock_material` (new): the ★ stands on the Brass row of the document material, then on the Mild steel row when the setup stock states Mild steel. The first line names the material.
- `the_derived_line_follows_rpm_and_feed` (new): a row's line changes with its rpm and with its feed; the other row's line stays; a still frame computes nothing; one change is one computation.
- `add_material_is_one_undo_step` (new): Add material… writes the draft and queues nothing; Apply is one undo step; one undo restores the tool.
- `suggest_fills_the_draft_and_apply_is_one_undo_step`, `copy_from_tool_copies_the_rows` (updated to the menus): each lands as one undo step.
- `the_document_material_row_is_marked` (updated to the ★ and the derived line).
- `layout_window_tool_editor` in `page_layout_tool_library.rs` (updated): the explanation heads the table; Material, Spindle rpm, Stepdown read left to right; Add, Suggest, Copy follow the table on one row; the units note follows them above Apply.
- `recipes_derived::tests::the_derived_line_follows_rpm_and_feed` and `recipes_fill::tests::add_material_adds_one_row_for_a_new_material` (new unit tests).
- `tool_library_mockup.rs`: the column check uses Stepover (the Vc and fz columns are gone).

`#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 1961 before, 1966 after.

Final head `7ea9ab7b1` (the commit plus the merge of `origin/main`), lane mac-1 (Mac, `lanes run --needs app --pool`), log `gate-4385-7ea9ab7b1.log`:

title: feat(pathkernel): the path kernel comes to main, dormant behind the planner switch
body:
The path kernel comes to `main`, dormant. This is the one PR from `side/path-kernel` to `main` of the plan of 2026-11-27 (#4023, `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`, rule **Side branch** of `AGENTS.md`).

## What a user sees

Nothing changes. The default planner of each operation kind is the old planner. Each program that the app makes is the same as before this PR. The pins `switch_default_is_the_old_planner` and the recorded baselines of the old planners hold that.

The setting `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new` (for tests and for the work on the kernel) selects the kernel. At this head no kind is moved, so with `new` each phase-1 kind is refused by name ("the new path planner does not plan <kind> yet"). There is no silent fallback. The first kind (2D Pocket, PR #4328) is not in this PR.

## What the PR brings

- The crate `camcraft-pathkernel` (`crates/pathkernel/`). It depends only on `camcraft-geometry`; `camcraft-motion` depends on it. The maintainer approved the crate, its name and its edges (2026-11-25; record of #4024 in `RECOMMENDED.md`).
- The stages: the region (K1), the guides (K2: rings, rows, medial line, trace, helix), the load control (K3), the order and the link with the proved approach from the air (K4), the entry and the exit (K5).
- The law suite of the crate (K7, `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/`), the law measures on a finished toolpath, and the recorded baselines of the old planners for the 16 phase-1 kinds.
- The converter from a kernel plan to a toolpath (`camcraft_motion::kernel_emit`). No operation calls it yet.
- The planner switch, read in one place (`crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`).
- Additions to `camcraft-geometry` (segment tests, arc points, a medial axis, a side offset), each with unit tests.
- The gate lists of `xtask` and the `-p` list of `AGENTS.md` for the new crate.

Sub-PRs that were reviewed and merged into the side branch: #4123, #4165, #4167, #4175, #4181, #4189, #4193, #4234, #4244, #4253, #4265, #4275, #4279, and the syncs #4112 and #4375.

## Open items (they do not block this PR; each one must be closed before the switch of a kind that it touches)

- #4300: a stay link along the air crosses the arc lead of the first entry (Outside).

## Gates

Reason: no existing directory suite of `camcraft-motion` covers all 16 phase-1 kinds, and the law readings of each kind and of the kernel stages must be one suite that the switch of each kind extends (decision `docs/decisions/4154-law-measures.md`).

title: fix(post): state G17 and G94 in the Fanuc and Doosan DNM preambles
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`: the section preamble is now `G90 G17 G94 <wcs> G40 G49 G80`. Before, it was `G90 <wcs> G40 G49 G80`. The post also sets its plane memory (`planeG`) to 17 after the block.
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: the section preamble is now `G90 G17 G94 <wcs> G40 G49 G80`. Before, it had no `G94`.
- 77 recorded programs are made again. Each one changes only in its preamble line.
- `docs/decisions/4346-preamble-g17-g94.md` records the decision.

## Cause

A FANUC control can keep G18 / G19 or G95 from an earlier program, from MDI or from its power-on parameters (FANUC Series 0i-F operator's manual B-64604EN-2). The Fanuc preamble did not state the plane or the feed mode. The Doosan DNM preamble did not state the feed mode. Then XY arcs, cutter compensation and drilling cycles can run in the wrong plane. An F word in mm/min is then read as mm per revolution. Neither post writes G93 or G95, so G94 is always the correct mode.

## Tests

- New pin: `fanuc_post::preamble::the_fanuc_family_preamble_states_g17_and_g94_before_the_first_motion` (`crates/post/tests/fanuc_post/preamble.rs`). It is a module of the existing `fanuc_post` binary, not a new top-level test. It posts two sections through each of the two posts. It checks that each preamble has `G17` and `G94` and that the first preamble comes before the first motion.
- Red before the fix: "fanuc: the preamble `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80` states G17".
- Mutation checks, one post at a time:
  - old `fanuc.cps` with the new `doosan-dnm.cps`: red;
  - old `doosan-dnm.cps` with the new `fanuc.cps`: red ("doosan-dnm: the preamble `G90 G17 G54 G40 G49 G80` states G94");
  - both new: green.
- `conformance::the_dialects_actually_differ`: with the fix, Fanuc and Doosan DNM write the same `drill_peck` program. Before, the missing G17 was their only difference there, and that was the defect. Each Doosan DNM word (brake, conveyor, AICC) is opt-in. Now a pair that is identical on `drill_peck` must differ on a rotary index on the DNM machine file with `rotaryBrake: true`. The test still finds two scripts that are copies of each other.
- Literal asserts that read `G90 G54` / `G90 G55` as the work-offset word now read `G94 G54` / `G94 G55`. Their purpose does not change. Files: `crates/app/tests/posting.rs`, `crates/app/tests/setup_mount_trace.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`. The full-preamble literals changed in `crates/app/tests/mcp_open/mod.rs`, `crates/post/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs` and `crates/post/tests/declared_options.rs`.

Commands and results on the final head `129ebbe6e`, base `9fb406cd6`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 9fb406cd6...`: 867 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base 9fb406cd6...`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The same for `-p camcraft-app` and `-p camcraft-ui`.
- No heavy step: this is a P3, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a heavy step only to a P1 under the safety floor.

## Goldens moved

77 programs. Every changed line is the preamble line and nothing else (`git diff -U0`, counted):

- 73 `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80` and 23 `G90 G17 G54 G40 G49 G80` became `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80`;
- 1 `G90 G55 ...` and 1 `G90 G17 G55 ...` became `G90 G17 G94 G55 G40 G49 G80`;
- 2 Explain goldens: the comment on the preamble now reads `(ABSOLUTE POSITIONS, XY PLANE, FEED PER MINUTE)`. The comment cap (60 characters) drops the work-offset words, as it did before for the words that did not fit.

Groups:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` (Fanuc, Doosan DNM, inch, explain, inverted, wcs-flip, probe and synth programs), written by `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` on `conformance`, `fanuc_post` and the app suites;
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/` and `.../doosan-dnm/`, written by `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` on `script_fanuc` and `script_doosan_dnm`;
- `examples/catalog/*/*/*.nc` (9 programs), written by `cargo xtask catalog`. The tool also rewrote the `.camproj` files (project version 83 to 84). I put those back, because that change is not part of this fix;
- `examples/first-part.nc`, written by `camcraft-cli process`;
- `docs/tester-kits/fanuc-mgi-blank/mgi_blank_{box,bar}.nc`. This kit has no writer, so I changed the one preamble line in each file. `fanuc_mgi_blank::the_tester_kit_is_what_the_post_writes` passes on it.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control.
- The full heavy lanes. They run at the cut.

## Overlaps

None. When I claimed the issue, no open PR touched `fanuc.cps` or `doosan-dnm.cps`. #4347 and #4348 merged after my first base. This branch is made again on `9fb406cd6`, which contains both.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: The Fanuc mill post now writes G17 and G94 in each section preamble, and the Doosan DNM post writes G94, so a control left in G18 / G19 or G95 runs the program in the XY plane and in mm/min.

Fixes #4346
