title: fix(drilling): Break-through follow-ups - the note, an idle selector, a full-diameter post case
body:
## What changed

This PR does the five items of #2528 (follow-ups of #2504).

1. **The Break-through note agrees with the field.** A Drill measured from its full diameter said "through holes run 2.803 mm past the part bottom (Break-through)" for a 1 mm Break-through. The note now says "through holes run 2.803 mm past the part bottom (Break-through 1.000 mm from the full diameter, plus the 1.803 mm drill point), the deepest to Z-2.803". `break_through::Broke` carries the point length (`with_point`). The Tip case, Bore and Thread keep "(Break-through)". The words "run X past the part bottom" stay, so readers of the note keep working.
2. **The "Break-through from" selector is disabled where it has no effect.** `holes_page::break_through_from_idle` gives the reason, in the generator's order:
   - a lathe's axial drill (it always measures to the tip);
   - a stated Bottom;
   - a Spot, Tap, Floating tap or Ream cycle (`drilling::through_tip_run`);
   - no through hole in the list.

   The combo is disabled. The reason shows when the user hovers the row (`on_disabled_hover_text`, the pattern of `fixture_menu.rs` and `feeds_page.rs`). A disabled widget shows no plain hover text, so the normal hint is used only while the row is enabled. I chose "disable" over "hide": a hidden row reads as a missing feature.
3. **A correction to the #2441 decision entry.** Issue branches do not edit `RECOMMENDED.md`, so `docs/decisions/2528-drill-point-followups.md` records the correction:
   - PR #2504 did not keep the examples byte-identical. It rebuilt the catalog case `2d/first-part` (`G73 ... Z-1. Q18.` to `G83 ... Z-2.803 Q6.`) and `examples/first-router-part.camproj` (v62 to v68, `full_diameter`, depth -1.0 to -2.802582). Only `examples/first-part.camproj` stayed the same.
   - An MCP or script patch does not default to `FullDiameter`. `add_operation` starts from the seed (`FullDiameter`). `edit_operation` applies a JSON merge patch over the stored parameters, so an omitted `break_through_from` keeps the stored value.
4. **Three file splits, structure only.** The `#[test]` counts do not change (app lib 322, motion lib 777 before item 1).
   - `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (469 lines): the program plan moves to `stock_sim_plan.rs` (225 + 256 lines).
   - `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` (409 lines): `PlayIndex` and `PlaySeed` move to `stock_play_index.rs` (330 + 93 lines). Their fields become `pub(super)`, because `FieldPlay` and `stock_play_head` read them.
   - `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests.rs` (508 lines): the five recognition tests move to `tests_recognize.rs` (404 + 110 lines). The shared helpers stay, so the other test modules keep their imports.
5. **Every post records a full-diameter through hole.** A new recorded stream `drill_full_diameter` (one 10 mm through hole, the default Full diameter, tip at Z-12.803) joins `recorded::CASES` and the `post_suite!` macro. Its generator guard is `recorded_post_streams::drill_full_diameter_stream_is_current`. The 15 mill posts record a program with `Z-12.803`. LinuxCNC and Heidenhain Klartext refuse it by name, as they refuse `drill_retract`. The lathe, wire, sinker, plasma and waterjet posts keep their named refusals.

## Goldens moved

None. Item 5 adds 27 new goldens (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/<post>/drill_full_diameter.{nc,refusal}`) and one stream. No existing `.nc` golden changes.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib: `break_through::tests::a_full_diameter_drill_names_the_field_and_its_point`.
- `camcraft-app` `break_through`: `the_default_is_today_s_millimetre_and_is_said` (the note names 1.000 mm and the 1.803 mm point for the Full-diameter drill, and "(Break-through)" for Tip and Bore).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `holes_break_through::drill_break_through_from_is_disabled_where_it_has_no_effect` (the four reasons; the combo is disabled until a hole is through; a hover over the disabled row paints the reason, and a hover over the enabled row paints the normal hint). `drill_break_through_from_defaults_to_full_diameter_and_switches_to_tip` now gives the draft a through hole first.
- `camcraft-app` `recorded_post_streams`: `drill_full_diameter_stream_is_current`.
- `camcraft-post` `script_*`: `drill_full_diameter` in each of the 27 post suites.

## Readings

- Quick gate on 31438caa1 (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 393 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 49.5 min.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-post -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` after the merge of `upstream/main` (with #4367): all pass, and no golden changes.
- `#[test]` counts before and after the splits: app lib 322, motion lib 777.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on 31438caa1: 115 steps (1 build, 41 `motion`, 73 `app`), 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 73.0 min. The known fails #1950 (3) and #2849 (1) are red as expected.

## Screenshots

The Levels group on the Heights tab of a Drill operation, with the pointer over "Break-through from".

| No through hole: disabled, the reason on hover | A through hole: enabled, the normal hint |
|---|---|
| ![disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2528/bt-from-disabled.png) | ![enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2528/bt-from-enabled.png) |

## Not exercised

- A real machine.

Changelog: Drill: the Break-through note names the field's value and the drill point apart for a full-diameter drill. The "Break-through from" choice is disabled, with the reason, where it has no effect (lathe axial drill, stated Bottom, spot/tap/ream cycles, no through hole).

Fixes #2528

title: fix(multiaxis): the banded parallel retip read agrees with the envelope law on slanted skins
body:
## What the feature brings (#2774, brought to the current main)

A rotary operation may state its heights as radii about the fitted
rotation axis: `RadialHeight { source, offset }` - the stock OD, the
model's max radius, or an absolute radius - as `clearance_r`,
`retract_r`, `top_r`, `bottom_r` on Rotary Contour and Rotary Parallel
and `clearance_r` + `top_r` on Rotary Offset. `None` on every field
keeps the Z-plane law byte for byte; the `*_z` fields stay.

- Heights as radii: one resolver (`app::operation::radial_heights`)
  fits the same axis the generators pose about; the radial gate
  refuses, at create/edit/retype, a clearance or retract radius that
  stands inside the work or a band that crosses.
- Band windowing: Rotary Contour keeps whole rings by tip radius
  (`band_select`); Rotary Parallel trims each skin-following pass at
  the band edges (`band_trim`); Rotary Offset caps its rho ladder at
  the bottom radius. A band that crosses no part skin refuses by name
  at the generate.
- Wrap hand-off: a band whose cylinders cover the path's whole radial
  reach hands the base path on unchanged (commit 815075be7).
- Project ladder v84 -> v85: the radii are serde-default fields, a v84
  file steps up unchanged, and a v84 reader refuses a v85 file rather
  than drop the stated radii. The three held commits (9a4da2e5f,
  8f6e59d1e, 815075be7) are cherry-picked; the two obsolete v74
  commits of the held branch are dropped and their content redone as
  the current next rung.

## The #3490 diagnosis: the two reads, what disagreed

The verdict the branch could not shake:
`Envelope { at: 38, gouge_mm: 1.544, rest_mm: 0.096 }` on a radial
band 4.0..5.5 over the r6/r5 stepped bar - the post refused a legal
program.

Both reads were re-read side by side:

- The RETIP READ the band uses, `hypot(y, z + r) - r`, is the ball
  center's radius about the axis minus the ball - the emitted tip's
  radius under the radial pose. Instrumented against the verifier it
  is exact on every kept cut move: the pose on cuts is the radial
  (lead/lag 0), so the emitted tip and the read agree.
- The ENVELOPE LAW (`stock_sim::facet_gouge`) reconstructs each ball
  center exactly (tip lifted along the pose it holds) and measures
  the exact distance of each model triangle to it. It is untouched.

What disagreed was neither read: the band trim's kept-stretch join
GLUED touching spans by extending the previous output move's end -
two arc-fit chords of a run became one straight chord. On the
raster's wrap chains (the arc around the cone's edge, ball centers on
the radius-8.5 ring) the glued chord dips 1.46 mm below the arc the
base plan rode; the reconstructed ball there stands 1.4554 mm from
the cone facet - the 1.5446 mm gouge, move for move. The verifier was
right; the kept geometry was corrupted.

## The fix

Touching spans stay consecutive Feed records (`radial_band.rs`). The
relink already reads consecutive non-lift Feeds as one run, so the
spans keep one cut - never a link between them - and the run's
polyline survives with every corner. The envelope law is untouched.

## Pins

- `rotary_verify::the_stated_radial_heights_move_the_generated_path`:
  red at the held branch with the reported verdict, green here.
- The correct-refusal side stands: a band that crosses no part skin
  refuses by name at the generate
  (`a_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`,
  `a_parallel_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`), and a
  gouging path still blocks the post.
- Motion band tests: `the_parallel_band_cuts_between_two_cylinders`,
  `a_band_that_wraps_the_whole_skin_adds_no_links`.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion`: 161 suites, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: 98 suites, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`: 84 suites, 0 failed (incl. the lib
  suite, the v85 round trip and the project-version suites).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1764 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

A real machine run. The banded parallel's posted G-code is pinned by
the document-level test only (the verifier's own envelope law); no
cut was made on steel.

Unblocks #2774: with the retip read and the envelope law agreeing,
the held feature's last blocker is gone.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read
their heights as radii about the fitted axis and window their cut
band by radii; a wrapping band no longer chops its passes; banded
parallel paths verify clean on slanted skins.

Fixes #3490



## Screenshots (the review's evidence, item 9)

The Heights tab and the viewport, before and after the feature - the
same turned bar, stock, tool and operation on both sides, captured
off-screen through the guide-images harness (page and viewport crops):

Before (the Z planes only, no radial rows, no rings):

- Page: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-before-page.png
- Viewport: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-before-viewport.png

After (the radial rows checked with their echoes, and the two rings
about the judged axis):

- Page: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-after-page.png
- Viewport: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-after-viewport.png

## Review rework (the nine requested findings)

Fixed on the branch in four commits; the review's own probes are
reproduced as tests:

1. Tip-to-center conversion (commit 167249f6b): the contour's radial
   relink now applies ONE tip-to-center conversion to every link (the
   ball center stands one ball radius outside the stated radius, the
   parallel twin's own law), so the posed tip stands AT the stated
   radius. Pinned by
   	he_stated_radii_are_the_tips_radii_on_every_link and the
   reviewer's app probe as
   	he_stated_contour_radii_clear_the_work (stated R8/R6.5 on the
   d12.4 bar verifies silent; it read Envelope { gouge_mm: 2.5 }
   before).
2. One-sided radial bands (commit 167249f6b):  and_window honors a
   Bottom radius alone (floor cylinder out to the skin's end) and a Top
   radius alone (axis out to the ceiling), for all three rotary kinds.
   Pinned by ^G_bottom_only_band_windows_the_parallel_passes,
   ^G_top_only_band_windows_the_parallel_passes,
   ^G_bottom_only_contour_band_windows_its_rings and the direct
   adial_band_tests.rs band-window pins.
3. Inclusive band edges (commit 167249f6b): each_band_span keeps
   constant and tangent spans with one closed-interval rule, so a span
   ON a band cylinder keeps both exact edges. The review's probe
   (constant span on the bottom cylinder beside a trimming span) is
   pinned in adial_band_tests.rs
   (^G_constant_span_on_the_bottom_cylinder_is_kept_to_its_end), with
   the start-edge, tangent, mixed enter/leave and whole-band pins
   beside it.
4. The selected rotary axis (commit 1009ddeb9): adial_context
   resolves the radii about the SAME axis generation turns about (the
   stated axis judged by ^Gxis_stated::judged_any, the free fit only
   when nothing is stated). The display cache keys the axis statement,
   the machine's work-turning rotary lines and the work offset origin.
   Pinned by ^G_stated_axis_resolves_the_radii_generation_judges (the
   R5 sphere fixture) and
   	he_radial_axis_cache_follows_a_new_axis_statement.
5. Radial input validation (commit 1009ddeb9): every set radial field is
   validated before storage - RadialHeight::is_sane keeps a finite
   offset and an absolute radius never under the axis, OpParams::is_sane
   checks each set field, and adial_gate surfaces the resolution
   failures it used to discard, with the range and ordering laws. The
   same door runs on create, edit, paste and retype. Pinned by
   ^G_radial_radius_that_is_no_radius_is_refused_at_the_command and
   ^G_radial_radius_its_source_cannot_answer_is_refused_by_name.
6. Radial overlay basis (commit 8fa787d07): the ring's second
   perpendicular is the unit dir x u (one orthonormal basis), never
   re-perpendicularized through off_axis. The plane and radius of
   every generated ring point are pinned for X, Y, Z and an oblique
   axis, and end to end through the overlay
   (	he_overlay_rings_stand_in_planes_about_the_judged_axis).
7. Valid zero-radius display (commit 8fa787d07): the echo displays the
   resolved zero for the field that permits it. The page test
   	he_default_bottom_radius_echoes_its_valid_zero drives the check
   row the way a user's click lands.
8. Project-format rollout (commit 1db582e7f): the committed example is
   regenerated by the suite's own WRITE_GOLDEN path; the diff is the
   version number and the operation stamp, and the committed .nc posts
   unchanged. See "Goldens moved" below. The compatibility break is
   declared with a BREAKING CHANGE: footer on that commit, and the
   decision entry identifies the current v85 step.
9. UI screenshots (this body): captured off-screen through the
   guide-images harness in detached worktrees, at the PR's base commit
   (before) and the rework head (after); the capture tests were
   uncommitted and deleted. The PNGs live only on the fork's
   pr-screenshots branch.

## Goldens moved

examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj: version 84 -> 85 and the
operation stamp refresh - no stored parameter, setup, machine or program
statement moved. examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc: unchanged
(the loaded project posts it move for move).

title: refactor(ui): split viewport modules along domain seams
body:
## Summary

Split the viewport along its existing domain seams. This is a code-only move.
There is no intended rendering, public API, shader or safety behavior change.

- Keep `viewport` as the public facade and the owner of private GPU resources.
- Move construction, uploads, rendering, readback and WGSL to private modules.
- Split the orbit camera from its private projection implementation.
- Keep all method bodies and shader composition unchanged.
- Keep the existing pipeline, wide-line and test files unchanged.

Effort: medium. The maintainer classified this as no new behavior:
https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3052#issuecomment-7047618632

Writer record:
https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3052#issuecomment-7221431845

Exact starting base: `NeoTech/Camcraft main 9fb406cd646c55ce12058dfd2930f509892240f1`.
This branch starts directly from upstream. It does not change the fork's main branch.
Head: `c65b9dabf82b6af8dbd2dc59718a6fc4452abac6`.

## Readings

Line counts include comments and blank lines.

| Viewport source file | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `viewport.rs` | 1313 | 166 |
| `viewport/camera.rs` | — | 251 |
| `viewport/camera/projection.rs` | — | 228 |
| `viewport/init.rs` | — | 156 |
| `viewport/upload.rs` | — | 201 |
| `viewport/render.rs` | — | 155 |
| `viewport/readback.rs` | — | 76 |
| `viewport/shader.rs` | — | 129 |
| `viewport/pipes.rs` | 235 | 235 |
| `viewport/wide.rs` | 188 | 188 |
| `viewport/wide_tests.rs` | 61 | 61 |

All viewport source files are below 400 lines.
The UI source inventory keeps 1,956 test functions and 9,187 assertion macros.
Every existing test file and viewport child remains byte-identical.
An exact-block comparison accounts for every nonstructural line from the original file.
Only private module declarations, imports, implementation wrappers and shader visibility are added.
`Camera` and `ProjectionMode` remain available through their existing public paths.

## Verification

Linux, Rust 1.100.0, three build/test jobs, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.
GPU checks use `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`, with llvmpipe/Vulkan.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 9fb406cd646c55ce12058dfd2930f509892240f1`: PASS.
  - UI lib: 1,760 passed, 8 existing ignored tests.
  - `catalog_render`: 2 passed, 1 existing ignored capture.
  - `gpu_render`: 19 passed, 1 existing ignored release snapshot.
  - Includes the camera, orthographic picking, draw partition and wide-line unit tests.
  - Includes rendered display modes, stock, fills, shadows, occlusion, wide lines and MSAA.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: PASS.
  All 11 light twins run in the five named test steps. Each step compiles its own target.
  Only the redundant all-target release prebuild is omitted.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test trace_composite -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`: PASS, 5 tests.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test theme_files -- --test-threads=3`: PASS, 30 tests, including the source color-literal guard.
- `git diff --check 9fb406cd646c55ce12058dfd2930f509892240f1 HEAD`: PASS.

### Actual output equivalence

Before editing, the unchanged catalog capture ran on the exact starting base.
It ran again after the split, using the same adapter and `2d/first-part` project:

```sh
CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1 CAMCRAFT_CATALOG_CASE=2d/first-part \
CAMCRAFT_CATALOG_SCREENSHOTS_OUT=<separate-before-or-after-directory> \
cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test catalog_render \
  render_all_catalog_screenshots -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

The four 1200×760 PNGs are byte-identical, including the blank selection and each operation.
This means zero different decoded pixels in those four scenes.
Their SHA-256 values match before and after:

| Capture | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `0-blank.png` | `775c1b45bac37d828d9b010491fb21f6cdf320461383833c87cae81666c60273` |
| `1-Face1.png` | `2fb239a5284c65460d7bb1f0b3257efdcfef2e972065d566d2e97c3f6e78ad4f` |
| `2-2D-Pocket1.png` | `3a5aaf82750a8379471791516e10380c5cf5ecf4947e47b6147f931c79aff383` |
| `3-Drill1.png` | `d717ea1d9d6080b84dd38169e2ee17e4d833d60595e950723a80d93deca34b37` |

#### Before/after viewport images

Before source: `9fb406cd646c55ce12058dfd2930f509892240f1`.
After source: `c65b9dabf82b6af8dbd2dc59718a6fc4452abac6`.
The saved captures use the same `2d/first-part` project, 1200×760 viewport and llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8)/Vulkan adapter.
These are unmodified viewport-only renders from the existing catalog harness, not full-window or dialog captures.
Each before/after pair is byte-identical. A separate rerender on the after source also matches all four captures.
Only the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch holds these images. No image enters this PR's source branch.

Images commit: [`e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9`](https://github.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/tree/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052).

| Scene | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| No operation selected | ![Before — No operation selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/before/0-blank.png) | ![After — No operation selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/after/0-blank.png) |
| Face1 | ![Before — Face1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/before/1-Face1.png) | ![After — Face1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/after/1-Face1.png) |
| 2D-Pocket1 | ![Before — 2D-Pocket1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/before/2-2D-Pocket1.png) | ![After — 2D-Pocket1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/after/2-2D-Pocket1.png) |
| Drill1 | ![Before — Drill1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/before/3-Drill1.png) | ![After — Drill1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/e749b883b83773305fe05fe661a383f177f2eee9/3052/after/3-Drill1.png) |
No golden is refreshed. The captures are test evidence, not replacement goldens.

## Limits and decisions

The byte comparison covers one catalog project, not every possible scene or GPU.
Other rendering modes are exercised by the existing GPU regression assertions.
No new behavior test is added for an unchanged implementation.
The pinning evidence is the exact source-block comparison, preserved tests and actual render comparison.
Full workspace, batch, heavy, release-snapshot and example-generation gates are not run.
No post, toolpath generator, dependency, process file or physical machine is changed.
These are software checks, not physical-machine safety acceptance.

See `docs/decisions/3052-split-viewport.md` for the seam choices and rejected alternatives.

Changelog: none (internal code-only move; no behavior change).

Fixes #3052

title: feat(ui): tool editor fields, clamping check and a side drawing to scale (U10)
body:
The parent #4365 is merged (`75e9b0ad7`); this PR now shows only its own commits.

## What changed

U10 of the tool library refit (#3663): the tool editor page. Only the tool editor page files and their tests change.

- **Tool tab** (`tool_tab.rs`): Name, Type, Tool number; a CUTTER group (Diameter, Flute length, Corner radius, Flutes, Helix angle, Tool material, Centre cutting, then the rows that only the kind reads); a SHANK group (Shank diameter, Shank length); then the assembly group. The rows are the row pieces of `tool_settings_grid` (split from `geometry()`, which Properties still uses in its old order). Each value is a draft field with its unit as a suffix. The footer's Apply lands them through `ChangeTool` (the number through `SetToolNumber`).
- **Moved rows:** the tool number and centre cutting moved from Details and Recipes to the Tool tab. The helix angle moved from Details to the CUTTER group. Flutes and Tool material also stay on the Recipes tab (inputs of the feed per tooth).
- **Name** is shown, not typed: no command renames a tool. Follow-up #4370 asks for `RenameTool` with its MCP tool.

title: perf(kernel): instrument the step import stages (profile for #4200)
body:
perf(kernel): instrument the step import stages (profile for #4200)

Instrumentation and profile only. No behaviour change, no verdict change.

## What changed

- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs`: `tracing::info!` timings with the
  stable stage names `parse` (Part 21 parse, with progress milestones from
  the `Watch` hook and the parse total), `topology` (unit/curve guards,
  face-winding check, topology read) and `build` (per-solid build with one
  line per solid, plus the loop total).
- `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs`: `mesh_plan` (plan and the
  judge/redivide pass), `mesh_deviation` (the sample measure), `facets`
  (plan evaluation) and `weld` (vertex weld).
- `crates/geometry/src/step.rs`: the kernel read total and one line per
  solid meshed in the per-solid loop.
- `crates/kernel/Cargo.toml`: `tracing` (a workspace dependency) for the
  events, `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency for the bench.
- `crates/kernel/tests/mesh_deviation_bench.rs`: a new `#[ignore]`d
  release-lane row `rotor_step_profile_bench` that reads the reporter's
  rotor from `CAMCRAFT_ROTOR_STEP` and prints the read and mesh timings.
  Without the variable set the row prints `rotor: skipped (set
  CAMCRAFT_ROTOR_STEP)` and passes, so CI without it stays green.
  Nothing pinned.
- Log level: the per-parse progress lines and the per-stage and
  per-attempt timing lines are `tracing::debug!` now, so the app's default
  `info` filter no longer prints about 11 progress lines per STEP import
  to stderr and the log. Reporters who want the lines set the filter to
  `camcraft_kernel=debug` (`RUST_LOG=camcraft_kernel=debug`); the bench
  sets its own filter to that level and still prints them.

## Rotor profile (3,723,412 bytes, Windows x64, release)

Measured 2026-11-27, Windows x64, release. Rotor.STEP, one solid
'Fillet2', 58 faces.

| stage | time | note |
|---|---|---|
| `parse` | 33 ms | Part 21 parse of the 3.7 MB file |
| `topology` (guards) | 3 ms | unit and curve checks |
| `topology` (winding) | <1 ms | |
| `topology` (read) | 16.5 s | kernel topology read and pcurve sewing |
| `build` | 3.4 s | one solid, 58 faces |
| read_step total | ~20 s | |
| mesh at 0.005 mm: `mesh_plan` 64.0 s, judge/redivide 12.3 s, `mesh_deviation` 126.8 s; replan at 2.5e-3 mm: `mesh_plan` 37.2 s | ~240 s | refused: face 35 capped at 9.8e-3 mm sag |
| mesh at 0.01 mm, attempt 1: `mesh_plan` 18.0 s, judge/redivide 2.4 s, `mesh_deviation` 167.4 s | ~188 s | rejected: measured 1.79e-2 mm over the 1e-2 mm tolerance |
| mesh at 0.01 mm, attempt 2 (chord 5e-3): `mesh_plan` 64.8 s, judge/redivide 12.3 s, `mesh_deviation` 114.5 s, `facets` 0.85 s, `weld` 0.4 s | ~195 s | success: 5,830,496 triangles, judged 5.98e-3 mm |

The import loop of `crates/geometry/src/step.rs` runs the read (~20 s),
then a full 0.005 mm mesh attempt that ends refused (~240 s), then the
0.01 mm loose-chord path (~380 s over its two attempts). That is about
640 s of work before any mesh is handed out, so the 300 s watchdog
cancels mid-way.

Where the time goes: `mesh_deviation` is the largest stage (115-167 s per
attempt, 88-95 million samples over 5.8M triangles). `mesh_plan` is next
(18-65 s per attempt, inside the pinned solidcore planner). The kernel
read is 20 s of the 640 s.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_twisted_flank`: green (the
  logging changed no verdict).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --lib`: green (22 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets --
  -D warnings`: clean.

## Fix options for #4200 (from the profile)

1. A seam-level pre-pass: measure the deviation per face as the plan is
   built, so a plan that cannot meet the tolerance is refused before it
   is fully made (the 126 s and 167 s measures of plans that were then
   rejected or refused would shrink).
2. Start at the edge-gap loose chord: the first full 0.005 mm attempt
   (240 s) always ends refused for this file, and the 0.01 mm path then
   replans to 5e-3 anyway.
3. Raise the solidcore pin per `docs/decisions/916-solidcore-step-bench.md`
   for the `topology` read and `mesh_plan` stages (36 s of 640 s; the
   largest stage is our own `mesh_deviation` code, so the pin move alone
   does not fix the bound).
4. Parallel per-solid does not help here: the rotor is one solid.

Refs #4200

title: fix(post): clean the Doosan DNM header name and refuse O-numbers past O9999
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `onOpen`: the header writes the machine name through the post's own `clean()`. `(`, `)`, `%` and `;` become a space. The name is cut to 40 characters. This is the rule of `fanuc.cps` and `fanuc-lathe.cps` (#594).
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `oWord()`: a program number below 1 or above 9999 is refused by name. The text is the text of `fanuc.cps`: `program number 10000 is outside O0001-O9999, the control's program numbers`. The old code clamped the number to O9999.
- `oWord()` reads the number with `isNaN`, not with `|| 1`. Thus a program number of 0 is refused. Before, it became O0001.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` (the #594 suite):
  - `doosan-dnm` joins the dialect list of `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_in_every_mill_dialect`.
  - New pin `doosan_dnm_header_cleans_the_name_and_refuses_a_number_past_o9999`.
- `docs/decisions/4349-dnm-header-name-onumber.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

- `onOpen` wrote `"(" + nm + ")"` with the raw `machine.name`. `DNM 5700 (5AX) 100%` gave `O0001 (DNM 5700 (5AX) 100%)`: a nested comment, and a `%` that ends the tape.
- `oWord()` did `Math.max(1, Math.min(n, 9999))`. The engine sets `programNumber` from the document (`crates/post/src/post/js.rs` `set_program`). A document number of 10000 posted as `O9999`, which is another program.

New output: `O0001 (DNM 5700 5AX 100)`. Program number 10000 or 0: the post is refused with the message above. Program number 9999: `O9999 (DNM)`.

## Tests (final head, against upstream/main 79f4dbe4a)

- Pins:
  - `doosan_dnm_header_cleans_the_name_and_refuses_a_number_past_o9999`
  - `hostile_names_post_well_formed_comments_in_every_mill_dialect` (now with `doosan-dnm`)
- Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the two pins failed: `left: Some("O0001 (DNM 5700 (5AX) 100%)")` and `doosan-dnm: unbalanced or nested comment "O0001 (MSG, Mill (A); B*)"`.
- Mutations (each one alone, then restored):
  - `clean(nm)` back to `nm`: the two pins fail.
  - Range guard removed: the new pin fails (`program number 0 must be refused`).
  - Only the upper bound removed (`n < 1`): the new pin fails (`program number 10000 must be refused`).
  - `isNaN` back to `|| 1`: the new pin fails (`program number 0 must be refused`).
  - Fix restored: all pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test comment_escape --test doosan_dnm_post --test script_doosan_dnm`: 5 + 9 + 11 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 73 steps, 0 failed. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `conformance` and `doosan_dnm_a_state`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 2 steps (release build, `app heavy: probe_no_coolant`), 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps (motion light: lib, three adaptive_troch twins; app light: pocket_pass_start), 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

None. I ran the example catalog suites, `conformance` and `script_doosan_dnm`. They passed. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/catalog/**"` is empty. The shipped Doosan machine name (`Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table`) has no character that `clean()` changes.

## Not exercised

- The program was not run on a Doosan control.
- A machine name longer than 40 characters is now cut to 40. No shipped machine has such a name. No test pins the cut for this post; the #594 suite pins it for the sister posts.
- `fanuc.cps` `progNo()` also uses `|| 1`, so a program number of 0 becomes O0001 there. This PR does not change `fanuc.cps`. The engine's document number is normally 1 or more.

## Overlaps

- #4363 changes `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` in other functions (`endPreamble`, `onLinear`, `onCircular`). It touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2646 changes `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` in a different test (`header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound`). Same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post: the header cleans the machine name (no nested parentheses, no `%`), and a program number outside O0001-O9999 is refused by name instead of becoming O9999.

Fixes #4349

title: fix(post): retract Z before a later tool change's G49 (mazak, fanuc, doosan)
body:
## What changed

- The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts now lift Z before the preamble of each section after the first.
- The lift uses the `safeRetract` method of the post: `G91 G28 Z0` (default) or `G53 G00 Z<safeRetractZ>`.
- The lift comes immediately before the `G90 ... G49 G80` block. The `G90` of that block ends the `G91` of the `G28` lift. `T M6` and `G43 H` follow as before.
- The first section gets no lift. Single-tool programs do not change.
- A Go home or a setup-change lift already raises Z. The post then writes no second lift (`zUp` flag).
- Fanuc and Doosan: a tilted section leaves `G43.4` armed until the next `G49`. The post then writes `G49` before the lift, in the same order as its Go home. The upright return after a tilt (#3466) no longer writes its own lift.

## Cause

Each later preamble wrote `G49` and `T M6` at the clearance height of the previous operation. The Mazak EIA/ISO manual says that `G49` moves the axis to remove the length offset. Z could move down by the tool length, near the part. The `safeRetract` option text says "Z retract command before tool changes and at program end", but the post wrote it only at program end and on Go home.

Fanuc and Doosan had the same order. A FANUC-family control can move Z on a `G49` block with no axis word. The issue asks to fix the two posts or to record them as not affected. This PR fixes them.

## Tests

Pinning tests (new):
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g28`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g53`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_the_same_tool_called_again`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_trip_home_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_setup_change_stop_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `upright_after_tilt::tool_change_retract::fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract`

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code, the three `retract_z_before` pins fail with `left: 0, right: 1` (no Z retract before the second G49).

Mutation results (each reverted, run, restored):
- `mazak.cps` from upstream: the three `retract_z_before` pins are red.
- `fanuc.cps` from upstream: the three pins are red.
- `doosan-dnm.cps` from upstream: the three pins are red.
- The `!zUp` guard removed (Doosan): `a_trip_home_...` and `a_setup_change_stop_...` are red (two retracts).
- The `tcpmLeft` G49 removed (Fanuc): `fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract` is red.

Gates on the final head `ce23fdaa8` (base `a5e993538`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base a5e993538`: 149 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `app suites: example_catalog`, `first_part_programs`, `program_entry`, `thread_boss`, `thread_mill`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: 1 step, 0 failed.
- Upstream main moved to `a721fd4dc` during the work. It changed `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. `git merge-tree` merges clean. Upstream's `conformance` passes on this fix (7 passed). The `comment_escape` change only replaces a fixed post count.

## Goldens moved

Each change is one `G91 G28 Z0` line before a later preamble of a multi-tool Fanuc program. The default post is Fanuc. No Mazak or Doosan golden has two tools.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/program_entry/fanuc_pause_home.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `examples/first-part.nc` (+2), regenerated with `camcraft-cli process`
- `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work/edge-work.nc` (+3)
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/2d/hole-work/hole-work.nc` (+4)
- `examples/catalog/2d/slots/slots.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/probing/probe-face/probe-face.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: after each tilted section the order is now `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, then `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80`. Before, it was `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80`, `G91 G28 Z0`, `G90`. Z is up before the preamble, and TCPM is off before the `G28`.

The catalog was regenerated with `cargo xtask catalog`. That command also rewrote the `.camproj` files: a project `version` 83 to 84, and float digits in the last place. These changes are not from this fix and are not in this PR.

`crates/app/tests/program_entry.rs`: `z_homes` counts trip homes. It no longer counts the new lift immediately before a preamble `G49` line. The tests keep their intent: one trailing home, and the mid home plus the close home.

## Not exercised

- No run on a Mazak, Fanuc or Doosan control.
- After a tilted section, the post writes `G49` before the lift, as its Go home did before. On a control where `G49` alone moves Z, that `G49` still runs before the lift. It runs in the same place as before this PR, so it is not new. A reference return under TCPM can alarm, so the post does not lift first.
- Haas, Tormach and LinuxCNC also write `G49` in each section preamble. They are out of the scope of this issue. A follow-up issue asks for the same check.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `fanuc.cps` or `doosan-dnm.cps`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4341-mazak-retract-before-toolchange.md`.
Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4341#issuecomment-7218043395

Effort: high

Changelog: The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts lift Z by the safe retract method before each later tool change, so the G49 of the next preamble never runs at the clearance height of the previous operation.

Fixes #4341

title: test(app): re-band shared_face_bodies_finish by measured time
body:
## What changed

- `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` no longer cuts the Z span of the sample into 6 equal bands.
- The span is now measured in 48 equal parts from the model's top. The table `EDGES` gives 12 bands: `0, 26, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 48`.
- The upper band (0..26) holds the fast upper half. Below the half, each band is 1 to 3 parts deep.
- The heavy band tests go from 6 to 12. The `#[test]` count of the file goes from 8 to 15.
- The assert body of each band (`the_3d_finish_band_generates_with_no_gouge`) does not change. Each band still asserts generate `ok`, the full verify gate, no gouge, `gate.ok`, the blocking `shank_hit`, `ok == false` and `held_by == ["S1"]`.
- A new default-suite test, `the_3d_finish_bands_are_narrow_where_the_levels_are_slow`, keeps the table narrow in the slow half. It also keeps the top band at the model's top.
- A `const` assert keeps the `band!` list and `EDGES` in step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3513-reband-shared-face-finish.md`.

## Cause

The generate time per level is not even over the span. The lower half of the sample holds almost all of it. The time is also not additive in the band depth. Old band 4 took 559 s alone, but its eight 1/48 parts took 247 s together. The time depends on where the level ladder of each band falls. So the edges come from measured bands.

## Readings (release, host with 32 cores, each band alone)

Each band ran alone, one after the other, in one process. The work is the same as the band test: `sample_job`, `edit_operation`, `generate`, `verify`. A temporary probe took the readings. The probe is not in the PR.

Before (6 equal bands):

| Band | Parts of 48 | Time (s) |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 0..8 | 12.1 |
| 2 | 8..16 | 7.4 |
| 3 | 16..24 | 13.0 |
| 4 | 24..32 | 558.9 |
| 5 | 32..40 | 162.0 |
| 6 | 40..48 | 217.8 |

Slowest / fastest: 75x. Sum: 971 s.

After (12 bands):

| Band | Parts of 48 | Time (s) |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 0..26 | 48.5 |
| 2 | 26..29 | 59.2 |
| 3 | 29..30 | 46.5 |
| 4 | 30..32 | 53.5 |
| 5 | 32..33 | 44.0 |
| 6 | 33..35 | 56.7 |
| 7 | 35..37 | 53.4 |
| 8 | 37..39 | 35.4 (first run 103.1, see below) |
| 9 | 39..41 | 67.3 |
| 10 | 41..43 | 58.7 |
| 11 | 43..45 | 51.4 |
| 12 | 45..48 | 71.5 |

Slowest / fastest: 2.0x. Sum: 646 s.

The host was loaded (load average 21-30) during the readings. Band 8 read 103.1 s on the first run and 35.4 s on a re-run, with the same code. The other readings can also move by that amount.

Wall time of the whole heavy step (all bands in one process at the same time):

- Before: 564.5 s (6 bands, probe run).
- After: 70.6 s (`cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish"`, `--test-threads=32`).

The 1/48 parts 0..3 at the model's top have no `shank_hit` finding. So the top band must start at the top and must be deep.

## Tests (on the final head)

- Pin: `the_3d_finish_bands_are_narrow_where_the_levels_are_slow`.
  - Red on unchanged code: `band 1 in the fast upper half starts at the model's top`.
  - Mutation 1, `EDGES` as equal twelfths: red, same message.
  - Mutation 2, last band 44..48 (4 parts): red, `band 11 in the slow lower half is too wide`.
  - Restored: green.
- `the_3d_finish_bands_tile_the_whole_span`: green (not changed).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base HEAD` on the final tree before the commit (the diff of this PR): `app suites: shared_face_bodies_finish` ok (3 passed, 12 ignored).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --only "app suites: example_catalog"`: ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy step `app heavy: shared_face_bodies_finish` (release, `--ignored`), 1 step:
  - on the branch head `efd49acdc`: ok, 12 passed, 70.6 s;
  - on a trial merge with upstream/main `c2fd4fe62`: ok, 12 passed, 64.3 s.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff is one test file and one decision file. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) can change. The example catalog suite ran and is green.

## Not exercised

- No readings from the cut runner. The edges come from one host. A different host can move an edge by one part.
- No light twin. The issue does not ask for one.
- The generate time of old band 4 (559 s against 247 s for its parts) can be a performance defect in the 3D Finish level ladder. This PR does not examine it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs`.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: none (test only)

Fixes #3513

title: feat(mcp): show SolidCraft face names and re-import changes
body:
Stacked on #4364 (#4212). This PR depends on #4364: it reads the source face record that #4364 adds. This PR is opened against `main`, so its diff also shows the commits of that PR until it merges.

## Build status

- The commits of this PR were built and tested on the earlier base `773736856`. "Tests" below gives those runs.
- Then they were rebased onto `main` `a721fd4dc` and the stacked PR, with no local build. The rebase had no conflicts. The code diff did not change: the patch-ids are the same.
- This head was not built or tested locally. The maintainer's runners test it.

## What changed

This PR adds two optional parts to MCP answers. No existing key changes. A model that has no SolidCraft names gives the same answers as before.

### 1. SolidCraft face names

When a model has the source face record of a `.sc` import (#4212), these rows get new keys:

- each face row and each patch row of `list_features`;
- each face pick and each patch pick that `picks_view` shows. This one hook serves `get_operation_geometry`, `set_operation_geometry`, `get_selection`, the area and "Do not touch" views, and `pick_in_box`.

The keys:

- `source_name`: the SolidCraft name, when the face has one name.
- `source_names`: the names, sorted, when the face or the patch has more than one name.
- `source_unverified: true`: SolidCraft did not verify one of the names.

A row gets no new key in these cases:

- the model has no record;
- the record does not tile the facets of the model;
- the pick is not in the model now;
- the name is blank.

The code never shows a wrong name set or a partial name set. Chains get no names (#4215).

### 2. `changes` in the `import_model` answer for an update

When `import_model` updates a model that was in the document before the call, the answer gets this key:

```text
"changes": {
  "faces":   { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "patches": { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "chains":  { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "summary": "the phrase that the window shows after a re-import"
}
```

- The counts come from `revision::changes`. The window gets the same diff from `UpdateModel::changes`.
- `summary` is `FeatureChanges::describe`.
- A first import gets no `changes`. A refused import gets no `changes`.
- This is the change summary that #3814 asks for. It is one of the five scope items of #3814.

### Where the code is

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/source_names.rs` (new, 264 lines): the name set of a face id or of a patch. It is pure code and has 7 unit tests.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/source_names.rs` (new, 157 lines): it finds the record, builds the features and writes the keys.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/reimport_changes.rs` (new, 81 lines): it keeps the models before the import and adds `changes` after the import.
- The hooks: 4 lines in `mcp/tools.rs::import_model`, 3 lines in `mcp/features.rs::list_features`, 2 lines in `mcp/pick.rs::picks_view`, and the `mod` lines.
- `mcp/tools.rs` (444 lines on `main`, 448 after this PR) and `mcp/features.rs` (435 lines, 438 after) had more than 400 lines before this PR. This PR adds only the hook lines to them. The logic is in the new files.
- `script/api.rs` does not change. #4212 and #4213 change `v_import`, so this PR does not touch that function. Thus a `cam.import` script does not get `changes`.
- The name code builds the features from the model's own facets (`features_of_facets`). The feature caches use the content as the key, not the facet order. A cached `Features` can have a different facet order, and then each facet index points to a different facet.
- No tool description changes. `mcp_doc_drift` passed on the earlier base.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/4214-mcp-face-names.md`.

### Commits

The first 5 commits are the commits of #4364. They go out of this diff when it merges. The commits of this PR:

1. `feat(mcp): import_model answers an update with its feature changes`
2. `feat(mcp): show SolidCraft face names on features and picks`
3. `test(mcp): a face pick on the .sc fixture shows its name`
4. `test(mcp): fix the .sc pick test's pocket heights`
5. `fix(mcp): name the snapshot type of reimport_changes::Before`
6. `docs(decisions): file the PR's decisions under #4214`

Commits 4 and 5 are the fixes that the build on the earlier base found: a test setup and a clippy `type_complexity` error.

## Tests

New in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/source_names.rs`:

- `each_box_side_reads_its_own_name`
- `a_face_over_two_record_faces_has_both_names_sorted`
- `an_unverified_name_is_flagged`
- `a_record_that_does_not_fit_gives_no_names`
- `an_id_that_is_not_in_the_mesh_has_no_name`
- `a_blank_name_gives_no_name`
- `a_patch_reads_the_names_of_all_its_strips`

New in `crates/app/tests/mcp/source_names.rs`:

- `each_face_row_names_its_solidcraft_face`
- `a_face_over_two_record_faces_lists_both_and_flags_an_unverified_one`
- `no_record_or_a_record_that_does_not_fit_shows_no_names`
- `a_face_pick_shows_its_name_in_the_operation_geometry`
- `a_patch_pick_names_all_its_faces_and_a_missing_pick_names_none`
- `a_sc_import_names_every_face_and_patch`

New in `crates/app/tests/mcp/reimport_changes.rs`:

- `a_first_import_answers_with_no_changes`
- `an_update_counts_what_moved_in_each_domain`
- `the_same_file_again_carries_every_id`
- `a_refused_update_answers_with_no_changes`

`a_sc_import_names_every_face_and_patch` imports `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` through the real import. Each face row and each patch row has a name. A face pick in `get_operation_geometry` shows the same keys as its `list_features` row.

Results on the earlier base `773736856`, with the stacked PR's commits of that time:

- All 17 tests of this PR: pass.
- The app lib and the 167 app test binaries that `quick` maps to this diff: pass (1,372 tests, 0 failures).
- All 39 geometry test binaries: pass (440 tests).
- The clippy step of the batch tier (`-D warnings`, all gate crates) and the kernel: pass.
- `mcp_doc_drift` and `mcp_pick`: pass.

## Not exercised

- **This head.** It was not built or tested locally (see "Build status").
- **The full batch tier.** The diff touches `crates/geometry/`, so `quick` becomes `batch`. Batch needs more disk than the build machine has. The runs above are the replacement.
- The light lane.
- `cargo fmt --check`. On the build machine it fails for `camcraft-app` with "os error 206": the command line is too long. The repository has no `rustfmt.toml`. The new files use 120 columns, as the code around them.
- The wasm build.
- The cost of the names on a large `.sc` model. The names build the features from the facets for each call, with no cache. A model without a record does no extra work.
- Linux and macOS.

## Open points for the maintainer

- **Fit with #3814.** The triage note on #4214 asks for your answer. This PR gives the counts that #3814 asks for, and `summary` in addition. It does not do the other four scope items of #3814. If you want #3814 separate, the commits for `changes` (1 and 5) can go as a PR of their own, with no dependency on #4364.
- **The followed and lost picks** of the "Done means" of #4214 come from the PR of #4213: the `picks` key of the `import_model` answer. This PR and that PR together meet #4214.
- **The counts do not match the `list_features` totals in two domains.** `changes.faces` counts each face id; `faces_total` counts planar faces only. `changes.chains` counts tangent chains; `chains_total` counts the chains of the pick graph.
- **Unverified names are shown**, with `source_unverified: true`. The PR of #4213 does not follow them.
- **No tool description changes.** One sentence for `changes` and one for `source_name` can come in a later PR, with the regenerated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.

Changelog: MCP: `list_features` and the pick views give the SolidCraft name of each face and patch of a `.sc` model (`source_name`, `source_names`), and `import_model` gives the carried, added and missing feature counts of an update (`changes`).
Effort: medium

Fixes #4214

title: fix(post): write G49 before the program-end retract when G43.4 is active
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` and `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: a new flag `tcpmLeft`. `endPreamble` copies `tcpmOn` into it before the reset.
- `onClose` in the two posts writes `G49` before its own retract when `tcpmLeft` is true.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/rotary.nc`: one new `G49` line after `M5`.
- Two new pins in `crates/post/tests/upright_after_tilt/program_end.rs` (no new test binary).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/4348-g49-before-end-home.md`.

## Cause

`tilt()` arms `G43.4 H<n>`. A section that tilts and then stands upright again ends with no rotary off zero. Then `uprightAtEnd()` writes nothing. `endPreamble` sets `tcpmOn = false` and writes no `G49`, because the next preamble writes `G49`. At the program end there is no next preamble. So `onClose` wrote `G91 G28 Z0` and `G28 X0 Y0` under `G43.4`. The FANUC 30i manual (B-63944EN/02) does not permit a reference return in `G43.4` mode.

The other exits are unchanged. They already write `G49`: a held rotary (`uprightAtEnd()`), a trailing Go home (`afterOp`), and the next preamble.

## Tests

Pins (binary `upright_after_tilt`):
- `program_end::fanuc_cancels_tcpm_before_program_end_after_a_tilt_back_to_zero` (G28 and G53 retract modes)
- `program_end::doosan_cancels_tcpm_before_program_end_after_a_tilt_back_to_zero` (G28 and G53 retract modes)

Each pin asserts a `G49` between the last `G43.4` and the end retract. In G28 mode it also asserts the exact tail: `M5`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, `G28 X0 Y0`, `M30`, `%`.

The recorded golden `script_fanuc` `rotary` also pins the order now.

Red before the fix: yes. Both pins failed on unchanged `a721fd4dc` with "G49 cancels G43.4 before the end retract". The program showed `M5` then `G91 G28 Z0`.

Mutation checks (old post put back with `git checkout upstream/main -- <post>`, then restored):
- old `fanuc.cps`: the Fanuc pin is red, the Doosan pin is green.
- old `doosan-dnm.cps`: the Doosan pin is red, the Fanuc pin is green.
- restored: the two pins are green. The `upright_after_tilt` binary passes 19 of 19.

Gate on the final head `23972c2d8` (base `a721fd4dc`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 148 steps. The first run had one red step, `post suites: script_fanuc` (`rotary`), because the recorded golden recorded the defect. I updated the golden (one `G49` line). Then `--only "post suites: script_fanuc"` passed 11 of 11. The other 147 steps were green, including `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `conformance`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `fanuc_post` and `setup_change`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on `23972c2d8`: 7 steps, 0 failed (release build, and the app heavy steps `do_not_touch`, `do_not_touch_adaptive`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `mcp`, `probe_no_coolant`, `sinker_burn`).
- `cargo xtask gate light` on `23972c2d8`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

One: `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/rotary.nc`. It is a tilted section that ends at `A0 B0`. It gains one `G49` line after `M5`, before `G91 G28 Z0`. No other line changed. The example catalog suites and the app `nc/` goldens (`conformance`) did not move: their programs end through a path that already writes `G49`, or never arm `G43.4`.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real FANUC or Doosan control.
- The Fanuc setup-change path (`afterOp` with a next setup and a stop ask) also writes `G91 G28 Z0` under `G43.4`. The Doosan post already writes `G49` there (#1647). This is outside the scope of #4348, and this PR does not change it. It needs a follow-up issue.

## Overlaps

No open PR changes `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` or `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`. Upstream `main` moved to `79f4dbe4a` after the base. The new commits do not touch `assets/posts` or `crates/post`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts: a program whose last tilted section ends at zero angles now writes G49 before the program-end reference return, so G43.4 is not active at G28.

Fixes #4348

title: feat(import): face picks follow their SolidCraft names at a re-import
body:
Stacked on #4364 (#4212). This PR is opened against `main`, so it holds the commits of #4364 under its own. Until #4364 merges, review only the 9 commits that "Commits of this PR" lists. Part of #3915.

**Test state, in short:** the first 6 commits were built and tested on the earlier base `773736856` (results below). The rebase onto `a721fd4dc` was not built here. The last 3 commits were never compiled: one is a code fix with a new test, two are docs and comments. Please test it with your runners.

## What changes

A model from a SolidCraft `.sc` file can import again after a change in SolidCraft. Then a face or patch pick inside an operation can lose its geometry id, and today the operation refuses until the user picks again. Now such a pick follows the face that has the same SolidCraft names. The follow is in the undo step of the update.

- **The match** (`camcraft_geometry::source_follow`, D8). A pick follows only when the names leave no doubt:
  - its id was in the old revision only, and no other old feature of the same kind has the same names;
  - each old name and each new name is verified;
  - exactly one new feature of the same kind has the same names, and it is new. A record face's former name counts too (the pieces of a Split Face);
  - that new feature answers to no other old feature's names;
  - a face keeps its plane kind.
- **The stores** (D7): the source selection, the extra and open boundaries, "Do not touch", and the two deburr exclude lists. A Probe pick or a Slot pick never follows, because its pick set the operation's numbers.
- **The review line** (D5): each operation with a followed pick gets one `needs_review` line. The line holds the post until `mark_operation_reviewed`. The line is cleaned and cut to 240 bytes, so the project file always opens (D10).
- **The report** (D6): a pick that cannot follow stays as it was, and generation refuses it as before. The window's re-import message names each such pick with its reason. The `cam.import` / MCP `import_model` answer gets the new key `picks`.
- **The project file** (D4): a model saves its source face record under the new optional entity key `source_faces`. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. A record that does not read, or does not tile the facets, is dropped with a logged note. The key never refuses a project.
- **The facet order** (D8, not compiled yet): the follow builds the features of the two revisions from their facets. It does not read them from the features caches. Those caches key a mesh by an order-free digest (`feature::digest_of`), so a hit can carry the facet order of another mesh with the same triangles. The record names facets by index, so the follow would give a face the name of another face.
- **Not followed:** setup WCS and alignment picks, fixture-locate picks, electrodes, chains and vertices.
- Nothing changes in `operation/mod.rs`. There is no new crate dependency and no new test binary: the tests join `model_link` and the geometry lib.

## Maintainer questions (open on #4213)

- **Q1: a version step or not.** The code adds no step (D4). An old reader drops the key and reads the model as today: it loses only the follow (the `solids` #917 precedent). On 2026-11-27 the last release, v0.27.0, writes v82, and `main` writes v84. If this PR merges before the cut that ships v84, each released build that opens the file knows `source_faces`. If it merges later, a released v84 build drops the key. A step is one line in `project/file.rs`.
- **Q2: follow automatically, or as a step that the user accepts.** The code follows automatically, with a review line that holds the post (D5). `posting::review_problems` refuses the post, and `cam.verify` reports the operation as holding the post, until the user marks the operation reviewed. An accept step costs a new command and its MCP tool.

## Commits of this PR

Built and tested on the earlier base `773736856`, then rebased without a build:
- `803a0337e` feat(geometry): find a missing face's successor by its SolidCraft names
- `4b8016b27` feat(project): save a .sc model's source face record, with no version step
- `19154a8b8` feat(import): face picks follow their SolidCraft names at a re-import
- `9647755aa` test(import): land the follow fixtures through ImportModel::source_faces
- `9d34f05ff` fix(import): no follow for Probe and Slot picks, and no two picks on one face
- `54c9a03eb` test(import): the review-line pin generates a facing pass, not a pocket

Never compiled:
- `90ec352b4` fix(import): the name follow builds its own features, not a cached facet order (code and the new test `model_link::facet_order`)
- `aca171657` docs(decisions): D4 holds with v83 and v84 not in a release yet (docs only)
- `22f99b4b7` docs(decisions): file the face-name follow decisions under #4213 (docs, and the provenance comments of three `.rs` files)

## Tests

The pinning tests (33):
- `camcraft-geometry` lib, `source_follow::tests` (14): the match rules, on a box at two widths and a faceted cylinder.
- `camcraft-app` lib, `commands::update_model_follow::{report,stores}::tests` (7): the review line, the report, the walk over each pick store, and the Probe and Slot exclusion.

title: feat(ui): the tool library window has one header and one footer
body:
Part of #3663 (step U8 of the tool library refit). This PR changes the frame of the tool library window. It does not change the content of the pages; U9 to U12 change the pages.

## What changed

- New file `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/frame.rs` with one header and one footer for all pages.
- The header has these parts:
  - "‹ List" when the tool editor, the component editor or the read-only holder view is open.
  - The title. A list page shows "Tool library". An editor shows the tool, holder or component name and a dim subtitle (for example "end mill · T1").
  - The "Cutting tools" and "Holders" tabs.
  - A "×" close button at the right. Its AccessKit name is "Close the tool library".
- The footer shows a hint on the left. Its buttons are:
  - list pages and the holder view: **Close**;
  - tool editor: **Duplicate** (disabled, the hover text gives the reason, follow-up #4340), **Cancel** and **Apply**;
  - component editor: **Cancel** and **Apply component**.
- The header and the footer are `egui::Panel`s in the window. The footer stays at the bottom of the window while a list scrolls.
- The window has no egui title bar and no shadow. The header replaces the title bar. The AccessKit name of the window stays "Tool library".
- Apply queues the same commands as before (`ChangeTool` or `ReshapeTool`, then `SetToolNumber` when the number changed). Apply stays one undo step.
- Cancel and "‹ List" drop the unapplied draft and go back to the list, as the old way back did. Close and "×" are view state and queue no command.
- `holder_view.rs` and `component_edit.rs` lose their own back buttons and headings, because the header now has them. "Apply component" moves to the footer. Sync and Save stay in the page.
- The tool editor loses its "Tool: name" heading and its Apply row.
- Visual style follows the rules on #4245 with the existing theme tokens: flat, hairline panel separators, no shadow, Apply filled with the theme accent. There is no new theme or kit crate.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/4334-tool-library-dialog-frame.md`.
  - The window stays non-modal, at the same place and size.
  - There is no egui title bar.
  - The tab keeps the label "Cutting tools": the ribbon already has a "Tools" button.
  - Duplicate is disabled until #4340.
  - The back button reads "‹ List", because the egui fonts have no "←".

The PR does not touch the stack group of #4331 (`stack.rs`, `assembly_group.rs`, `tool_tab.rs`).

## Screenshots (1366 × 768, rendered headlessly)

## Pinning tests

- New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_frame.rs` (5 tests):
  - `the_tool_list_has_the_header_and_the_close_footer`: the title, the tabs, the "×", no way back, the hint, Close enabled, and no Apply, Cancel or Duplicate. Close closes the window and queues no command.

title: feat(import): keep the SolidCraft source face and name of each .sc facet
body:
## What changes

A `.sc` import now keeps the SolidCraft source face and its name for each facet of the model. This is the first sub-issue of #3915. The other sub-issues use the names: #4213 (face picks follow the names) and #4214 (MCP). Nothing reads the names in this PR, and the project file does not change. A user sees no change, except one new import note in a rare case (D2).

- **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/`, new `names.rs`):
  - The `.sc` reader reads the name of each record face of the final body from `cache/model.json`. The names are `model.names[n]`, where `n` is the final model body's `names` field.
  - It keeps `faces[i]`, and from `info[i]` the `verified` flag and the optional fifth item `former`. `info` with four items and with five items both read.
  - It reads names only from model cache format 10 (`NAMES_FORMAT`).
  - `SolidcraftImport` gets `names` (one entry for each record face, in record order) and `names_note`.
- **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/`, new `source_faces.rs`):
  - `SourceFaces` holds the names and one facet range for each run of a record face. The ranges come from `MachiningMesh::tri_face`.
  - `solidcraft::parse` returns the record beside the mesh, on native and on wasm.
  - A record whose ranges do not tile the facets is dropped with a note.
- **App** (`crates/app/src/`, new `source_faces.rs`):
  - A new component `schema::SourceFaces` holds the record on the model, in memory only. Code reads and writes it only through `source_faces::{of, set}`.
  - The record keeps the model revision and the facet count that it landed with. When other facets land (a repair, an update without a record), `of` gives `None`.
  - `ImportModel` lands the record. Undo and redo trade it.
  - `UpdateModel::with_source_faces` trades it on undo. An update that does not state it drops it. `RepairModel` drops it (`keeping_fidelity` does not keep it).
  - `DeleteEntity` puts it back on undo.
  - The window (`ui/src/state.rs`), the script and MCP import (`script/api.rs`) and the fixture re-import (`commands/import_fixture.rs`) pass it. Each is one builder call.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/4212-sc-face-names.md`.
- D1: names from model cache format 10 only.
- D2: the import never fails because of names. Names that do not fit give no names and one note ("Solidcraft: the face names were not read: ..."). A partial or shifted list is never kept.
- D3: the names are in memory only in this PR. The project file does not change.

No new dependency. No change to `project/*`, to a post, or to a toolpath.

## Maintainer questions on #4212 (open)

The triage note on #4212 says that Q4 and Q5 are open. The code takes the recommended option for each. These answers are open to the maintainer. A different answer changes only the parts named here.

- **Q5 (names from cache format 10 only?):** yes in this code (D1). A format-8 `.sc` gives no names and no note, and imports as before (`a_format_8_cache_reads_no_names_and_says_nothing`). To read more formats: one constant and one pin.
- **Q4 (which fixtures?):**
  - Most pins use containers that the tests build in code, with names of our own. This includes the alignment pin, the misfit pins and the hostile cases.
  - Three pins also read `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc`. That file is already in the repository and is already used by `hole_on_pocket_wall.rs`. The three pins are:
    - kernel `names::a_solidcraft_written_file_names_its_faces_in_record_order`;
    - geometry `source_faces::a_solidcraft_import_hands_out_the_record_of_its_own_facets`;
    - app `source_faces::a_solidcraft_import_lands_its_face_names`.
  - No pair made by SolidCraft from `examples/bracket.json` is used.
  - If the answer is "test-built containers only", remove those three pins. The other pins stay.

## Tests

**This branch is not built.** It was rebased onto `a721fd4dc` with no conflicts and not built locally, at the maintainer's request. Upstream changed four files that this PR also changes: `crates/app/src/commands/delete_entity.rs`, `crates/app/src/lib.rs`, `crates/app/src/schema.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs`. The text merges clean. Nothing was compiled on the new base.

Pinning tests (16 new test functions):
- Kernel `solidcraft_import`:
  - `names::format_10_names_are_read_one_for_each_record_face`
  - `names::every_triangle_of_a_named_face_lies_on_that_faces_plane` (the alignment pin: a block that the test builds, each face named by its plane; a list shifted by one must fail)
  - `names::a_format_8_cache_reads_no_names_and_says_nothing`
  - `names::a_solidcraft_written_file_names_its_faces_in_record_order`
  - `names_misfit::names_that_do_not_fit_give_a_note_never_a_refusal` (18 misfits)
- Kernel `solidcraft_hostile`: `hostile_names_never_panic_or_refuse_the_import` (30 hostile values in the names record and its index, on a six-face block)
- Geometry `solidcraft`: `source_faces::{ranges_follow_the_runs_of_the_record_face_of_each_facet, a_face_past_the_names_gives_no_record, a_record_that_does_not_tile_is_told_apart, a_solidcraft_import_hands_out_the_record_of_its_own_facets}`
- App `import_solidcraft`: `source_faces::{a_solidcraft_import_lands_its_face_names, stl_obj_and_step_models_have_no_face_names, an_update_trades_the_names_on_undo_and_drops_them_unstated, a_repair_drops_the_names_and_undo_brings_them_back, a_deleted_model_comes_back_with_its_names, names_that_do_not_describe_the_facets_are_never_handed_out}`

Runs on the earlier base `773736856`, at the same code (Windows 11, debug, 2026-11-26). All 16 pinning tests passed.

| What | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test solidcraft_import --test solidcraft_hostile` | ok: 13/13 and 4/4 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test solidcraft` | ok: 5/5 |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import_solidcraft` | ok: 11 passed, 3 ignored (heavy-lane tests that were there before) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` + the 82 app suites that `quick` maps to this diff | ok, after the asset re-run below |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` + the 14 UI suites that `quick` maps to this diff | ok: 14/14 suites; lib ok after the asset re-run and the intermittent test below |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry` (all 39 targets) and `cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --lib` | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-{geometry,cl,gcode,tools,post,sim,motion,app,gpu,ui} --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then the same for `camcraft-kernel` | ok, both |

Readings: the hostile names run took 18.8 s (its bound is 120 s). The app `import_solidcraft` binary ran in 1.7 s.

Red steps on the earlier base, none from this PR:
- Seven app targets and one UI lib test read an old `assets/` folder. Our shared build folder was inside an older checkout, and `post::data_dir` looks two levels above the cargo profile folder. Run against this branch's own `assets/`, all pass: app lib 318/318, `after_op` 10/10, `explain_option` 4/4, `machine` 57/57, `per_op_files` 9/9, `posting` 17/17, `tormach_end_units` 8/8, UI `machines_pane`.
- `egui_app::tests::recent_door::an_empty_list_and_browse_open_todays_dialog` failed one time in a full UI lib run. It passed 8/8 three times alone. It expects an empty recent-files list.

Not exercised:
- Any build or test on the new base `a721fd4dc`.
- The full batch tier. `quick` becomes `batch` for a change under `crates/geometry/`. Batch builds each debug test binary first (about 169 GB for app on our machine), and that did not fit on the disk. In its place, we ran the mapped suites, all geometry suites and batch's clippy step above.
- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`).
- The wasm build of `geometry` and `app`.
- A pin for a body that the fallback mesher meshes. No fixture forces that path today (`machining_mesh_shortfalls.rs`). By reading only: the fallback also gives `tri_face` face by face.
- The three caller hooks have no test of their own. Each is one builder call, and clippy compiled them.
- `cargo fmt --check`: the new files are rustfmt-clean. Edits inside existing statements follow the style of each file.

On `a721fd4dc`, the `quick` map for this diff picks the app lib and 92 app suites, the UI lib and 14 UI suites, the kernel lib with `solidcraft_import` and `solidcraft_hostile`, and the geometry suite `solidcraft`. Because geometry changes, `quick` runs as `batch`.

## Overlap with open PRs

- #4235 (draft): it and this PR both add `mod` lines after `mod blend;` in `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import.rs`. Keep both. Its test reads no names and no notes.
- #4066, #4270 and #4238 also change `crates/app/src/schema.rs` or `crates/ui/src/state.rs`. A trial merge of each with `a721fd4dc` and this PR is clean.

title: fix(post): keep Doosan DNM G5.1 out of an open canned-cycle group
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `onLinear` and `onCircular`: the post arms AICC smoothing (`G5.1 Q1 R<n>`) only when no canned-cycle group is open (`!inCycle`).
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, `endPreamble`: the post writes `G80` before `disableSmoothing()`. Thus `G5.1 Q0` never comes while G81-G89 is modal.
- `crates/post/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`: new pin `doosan_dnm_smoothing_stays_out_of_open_cycle_group`.
- `docs/decisions/4347-dnm-smoothing-cycle.md`: the decision record.

## Cause

The hole chain of a cycle (plunge, retract to R) reaches `onLinear`. The old code called `enableSmoothing()` before `chainCut()` dropped the move. Each hole wrote `G5.1 Q1 R5`, and the next cycle block or the section end wrote `G5.1 Q0`. All these words were inside the group. The section end also wrote `G5.1 Q0` before `G80`. The FANUC 0i-F manual (B-64604EN-2/01, 3.3.2) does not permit `G5.1` in canned-cycle mode.

Old output for a smoothed two-hole section (the pin's stream):

```
G81 X20. Y10. Z-5. R2. F200.
G5.1 Q1 R5
G5.1 Q0
X20. Y10.
G5.1 Q1 R5
G5.1 Q0
G80
```

New output: `G81 ...`, `X20. Y10.`, `G80`, with no `G5.1` word between them.

## Tests (final head 3484c8b3b)

- Pin: `doosan_dnm_smoothing_stays_out_of_open_cycle_group`. It fails on unchanged upstream/main a721fd4dc ("no G5.1 word inside the open cycle group").
- Mutation: I put the old `onLinear` line back. The pin failed. I restored the fix. The pin passed. With only the `endPreamble` reorder, that run wrote `G80` before `G5.1 Q0`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test doosan_dnm_post`: 10 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 73 steps, 0 failed. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `conformance` and `doosan_dnm_a_state`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 2 steps (release build, `app heavy: probe_no_coolant`), 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: 6 steps, 0 failed.

## Goldens moved

None. I ran the example catalog suites and `conformance`. They passed, and `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. Outside a cycle group the output is byte-identical.

## Not exercised

- No test stream puts an arc inside a cycle group. The `onCircular` guard has no pin of its own. It uses the same test as `onLinear`.
- After the `onLinear` guard, smoothing cannot be active while a group is open. The `endPreamble` reorder thus has no independent pin. It is a second guard.
- The program was not run on a Doosan control.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` or `crates/post/tests/doosan_dnm_post.rs`.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post: with AICC smoothing on, a drilling section no longer writes G5.1 inside a canned-cycle group, and G80 now comes before G5.1 Q0.

Fixes #4347
