title: feat(gcode): read a first slice of HEIDENHAIN Klartext (.H) programs
body:
## What changed

This PR adds a first slice of a HEIDENHAIN Klartext (`.H`) reader to `camcraft-gcode`.

- New entry points: `parse_klartext(program)` and `parse_klartext_with(program, &KlartextOptions)`. The output is the same `ParsedProgram` / `ParsedSection` / `cl::Toolpath` as the RS-274 reader gives.
- New module `crates/gcode/src/klartext/` (7 files, each below 400 lines). It uses the section builder, the arc resolver, the numeric domain checks and the peck bound of the RS-274 reader.
- `ParsedSection` gets a `tool_name: Option<String>` field. A named `TOOL CALL "FLAT-6"` has no tool number. Without the field, two named tools would merge into one section. The RS-274 reader sets `None`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2227-klartext-reader.md`.

### The reader reads

- `BEGIN PGM <name> MM` and `END PGM` (the names must agree; a missing `END PGM` is refused as a truncated program).
- `BLK FORM 0.1 Z` / `0.2` (checked; not part of the toolpath).
- `TOOL CALL` with a tool number or a `"NAME"`, axis Z, `S`, `F` (`DL` / `DR` only when zero). `TOOL DEF` (no effect).
- `L` with `X Y Z`, `IX IY IZ`, `R0`, modal `F`, and `FMAX` for one block only.
- `CC` (both axes or none), `C` with `DR+` / `DR-` (a full circle gives two arcs), `CR` with `R+` / `R-`, and `CT` (tangent to the previous element).
- `CYCL DEF 247` (preset `Q339` 1 to 6, read as work offset G54 to G59).
- `CYCL DEF 200`, `203`, `205`, called by `CYCL CALL` or `M99`. Each infeed goes `Q202` deeper from the surface `Q203`. The tool ends at the higher of the two set-up clearances. Each call records a `cl::Cycle`.
- `FN 0: Qn = <literal>`, `Qn = <literal>`, and Q references in values (`X+Q1`, `X-Q1`).
- `STOP`, `;` comments, `*` structure blocks, `~` continuation lines.
- M functions 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 13, 14, 30, 99, 137, and `M140 MB MAX` / `M140 MB <n>`. `M140 MB MAX` needs `KlartextOptions::tool_axis_max_z`, because the end of the traverse range is a machine value.

### The reader refuses (by name, with the line; the message starts with `block N:`)

`RND`, `CHF`, `LP`, `CP`, `CTP`, `APPR`, `DEP`, FK blocks, `LBL`, `CALL`, `RL`, `RR`, axes other than X/Y/Z, polar words, `FAUTO` / `FU` / `FZ`, `M91`, `M92`, `M89`, `M136` and other M functions, `FN` other than `FN 0`, Q formulas, `BEGIN PGM ... INCH`, a tool axis other than Z, a helix (arc with a Z change), old-style cycles (`CYCL DEF 1.0`), cycles other than 200 / 203 / 205 / 247, `CYCL CALL PAT` / `POS`, and the cycle options that change the motion when they are not zero (`Q210`, `Q212`, `Q213`, `Q257`, `Q379`, `Q395`). The decision record gives the reason for each.

## Tests

New test binary `crates/gcode/tests/klartext` (25 tests). Pinning tests:

Reason for the new top-level test binary: `tests/parse/` is the suite of the RS-274 reader; Klartext is a different input language with its own entry point (`parse_klartext`), so it gets its own directory suite. `camcraft-gcode` then has two small test binaries.


- `klartext_post_golden_reads_back_into_the_stream_motion`: the recorded Klartext post golden (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain-klartext/picomax.nc`) reads back into the motion of its CL stream (`crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc`): points, rapid or feed, feeds, arc centres and directions. It also checks tool, rpm, preset, stops and the line map across the continuation line.
- `klartext_post_golden_needs_the_traverse_end_for_m140`.
- Review fix: `klartext_stop_with_m0_or_m1_records_one_program_stop` (a `STOP M0` or `STOP M1` block records one `ProgramStop`, not two stops).
- Paths: `klartext_fmax_is_blockwise_and_f_is_modal`, `klartext_incremental_words_and_literal_q_parameters`, `klartext_cc_and_c_arcs_with_both_directions_and_a_full_circle`, `klartext_cr_radius_sign_picks_the_minor_or_major_arc`, `klartext_ct_continues_the_tangent_of_the_previous_element`, `klartext_tool_calls_by_number_and_name_split_sections`, `klartext_m_functions_set_spindle_coolant_and_stops`.
- Cycles: `klartext_cycle_200_pecks_from_the_surface_and_ends_at_the_2nd_clearance`, `klartext_cycles_203_and_205_without_chip_breaking_drill_at_cycl_call`, `klartext_cycle_247_selects_the_preset_as_work_offset`, `klartext_unsupported_cycles_and_cycle_options_are_refused_by_name`, `klartext_invalid_cycle_definitions_and_calls_are_refused`.
- Refusals: `klartext_functions_outside_the_slice_are_refused_by_name_and_block` (17 functions, line and block number), `klartext_inch_programs_and_unknown_words_are_refused`, `klartext_program_frame_is_checked`, `klartext_arc_preconditions_are_refused`, `klartext_m140_mb_max_needs_the_traverse_end`.
- Degenerate input (each run on a worker thread with a time limit; a panic or a hang fails): `klartext_every_truncation_of_the_golden_is_refused_without_a_panic` (each prefix before `END PGM`), `klartext_bad_numbers_are_refused` (22 cases), `klartext_huge_programs_parse_or_refuse_in_time` (200 000 blocks, a 1 MB block, 100 000 continuation lines), `klartext_seeded_mutations_of_the_golden_never_panic` (3000 seeded mutations), `klartext_empty_and_comment_only_input_is_refused`.

## Gate results (head d94707823, main 9fb406cd6 merged in, Mac lane, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`)

The first head 6482595d3 had the same results on the Windows lane `winbuild`.

| Step | Result |

| gcode suites: lib | ok |

title: feat(motion): exact radial ball drop kernel about a stated axis
body:
## What changed

- A new motion kernel: `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::radial_drop::RadialDrop` (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/radial_drop.rs`).
- It gives the exact ball-centre radius at an (axial station, angle) about a stated rotation axis.
- It works for any model. The model does not have to be a shape of revolution (for example a helical rotor or a carving).
- The ball comes in along the radial line from far outside. It stops at its first contact with the mesh.
- The contact is the largest valid root over the face, edge and vertex patches of each facet, grown by the ball radius.
- No contact gives `None`. The kernel never makes up a radius.
- Input that cannot be meant is refused by name: a ball radius that is not positive and finite, an empty mesh, a facet with a corner that is not finite, an axis that is not a direction.
- Angle zero follows the axis.rs basis law (`rotary_flow_unwrap::basis`). Rotary Flow uses the same frame.
- A cull keeps queries fast: axial bins about one ball radius wide (4096 at most), then a bounding-sphere test against the ray's line.
- No operation calls the kernel yet. This PR is the third slice of #2772 (`Refs`, not `Fixes`).
- `docs/decisions/2772-radial-drop.md` records the choices and what was dropped.

## Cause

The rotary kinds fit their contact for a turned surface. On a part that is not a shape of revolution, the merged slices keep them locked, which is correct. The next safe step is a contact law that is exact for any mesh, proved alone before an operation uses it.

## Tests

Pins, in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/radial_drop_tests.rs` (9 tests):

- `a_face_contact_rests_the_ball_r_off_the_plane`
- `an_edge_contact_rests_the_ball_on_the_ridge`
- `a_vertex_contact_rests_the_ball_on_the_tip`
- `the_screw_rotor_drop_touches_and_never_gouges`: 216 stations on a helical screw rotor. At each station the ball touches (distance = r within 1e-7). 200 centres farther out on each ray do not come nearer than r.
- `the_kernel_agrees_with_a_brute_force_march`: an independent march and bisection agree within 1e-6.
- `a_facet_reaches_every_station_within_the_ball_radius`: pins the cull.
- `a_ray_past_the_part_meets_nothing`
- `the_radial_is_a_unit_vector_square_to_the_axis`
- `input_that_cannot_be_meant_is_refused_by_name`

Red before the fix: yes. With the test file and no kernel, the build fails with `error[E0432]: unresolved import super::radial_drop`.

Mutation checks. For each check I changed the kernel, ran the pins, and then restored the code:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M1 no face candidate | red (face, screw, march) |
| M2 no edge candidate | red (edge, screw, march) |
| M3 no vertex candidate | red (vertex, screw) |
| M4 edge foot not checked against the segment | red (vertex, screw, march) |
| M5 face foot not checked against the triangle | red (vertex, edge, screw, march) |
| M6 bounding-sphere cull without `+ r` | red (screw) |
| M7 radius guard accepts 0 and negative | red (refusals) |
| M8 axial bins without the `r` padding | red (`a_facet_reaches_every_station_within_the_ball_radius`; the first test set missed this, so I added that pin) |

Restored: 9 of 9 pass.

Commands on the final head:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib radial_drop`: 9 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 41 steps, 0 failed (includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `rotary_verify`, `rotary_parallel_keyway`, `continuous_4axis_part`).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` (base c16df4e7d): 115 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 26.4 min (app heavy and motion heavy, every target).

## Goldens moved

None. I ran the quick gate with `app suites: example_catalog` and the rotary suites. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed (`git diff --stat upstream/main` shows only the 4 files of this PR).

## Not exercised

- No operation, post or verify path calls the kernel yet. Wiring Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) to it is the next slice. That slice changes posted G-code.
- The shank is clear only for a ball nose on the same radial line, with a shank no wider than the ball. A tapered or wider holder is not covered here. The wiring slice must keep the existing holder checks.
- Not timed on the reporter's 1.15 M-facet STEP mesh.
- No UI change, so no screenshots.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR touches `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs` or the new files.

Changelog: none (an internal kernel with no caller yet; the row comes with the wiring slice)

Refs #2772

title: feat(xtask): the heavy reach of a library file follows the Gate maps
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate heavy` maps a changed library file of crate `d` to fewer targets. It reaches:
  - the `lib`, `bins` and `doc` targets of `d`, when `d` is a heavy crate;
  - each heavy integration binary whose Gate map names a module of the file.
- The quick plan uses the same Gate map rule. The rule moves out of `quick::map_modules` into three functions: `quick::src_modules`, `quick::gate_maps` and `quick::suites_naming`. The quick plan calls them and its behaviour does not change.
- The crate reach (each heavy lane of each dependent crate) stays in these cases:
  - a shared crate (`geometry`, `cl`), where quick runs batch;
  - a crate root (`lib.rs`, `main.rs`, `bin/`) or a file outside `src/`;
  - a file that no Gate map names under any of its module names.
- A `#[path]` file has two names. One named module is enough, as in quick.
- `--dry-run` names each reached target with its reason (`the gate map names motion::drilling`). It names each skipped target as `not run` (from PR #3737).

Example: `crates/motion/src/drilling/boss.rs` goes from 115 heavy steps to 11 heavy steps.

## Cause

PR #3737 narrowed only `#[cfg(test)]` files and binary files. A library file still reached the whole heavy lane of its crate and of each dependent crate. The issue asks to map a file to the heavy targets that touch it, with the crate reach as the fallback.

## Tests

Pins (new file `xtask/src/heavy_gate_map_tests.rs`):
- `a_library_module_reaches_its_crate_targets_and_the_binaries_whose_gate_map_names_it`
- `a_module_that_no_gate_map_names_and_a_shared_crate_keep_the_crate_reach`
- `a_path_included_file_reaches_through_the_gate_map_of_its_includer`

Expected change: `heavy_files_tests::library_code_keeps_the_crate_reach` used `drilling/boss.rs` as its wide example. It now uses the crate root `lib.rs`. The new pins cover the module case.

Mutation results (each pin run on the changed code, then restored):
- Old `heavy.rs` from main: the first and third pins FAIL. The second pin passes (it pins the fallback).
- Remove the "no Gate map names it" guard: the second pin FAILS (line 61).
- Remove the shared-crate guard: the second pin FAILS (line 66).
- Restored: all three pins pass (36 s).

Commands on the final head `e3f3517e6`:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1 step (xtask unit tests), 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: one error, in `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`clippy::needless_bool`). This PR does not touch that file. The same error is on main with the local toolchain. With `-A clippy::needless_bool` clippy is clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: 0 steps reached, 122 skipped. The diff changes only `xtask/` and docs.

## Goldens moved

None. Not run: the diff changes only `xtask/` and a decision file. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) can move. The example catalog suites and the light lane were not run for the same reason.

## Not exercised

- No full heavy lane ran. The narrow reach is a review tool. The cut gate still runs all heavy lanes.
- A test that exercises a module without a Gate map line for it is not reached at review. The cut gate runs it. The decision file records this trade-off.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `xtask/src/heavy.rs`, `xtask/src/quick.rs` or the heavy tests.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3560-heavy-gate-map.md`.

Process change: yes

Effort: high

Changelog: `cargo xtask gate heavy` runs only the heavy targets whose Gate map names a changed library module; the crate reach stays as the fallback.

Fixes #3560

title: test(post): derive the per-post conformance rows from the registry
body:
This PR does item 2 of #3461 only: the per-post rows of the conformance and comment-escape tests. Items 1, 3 and 4 stay open on the issue. Thus the PR ends with `Refs #3461`, not `Fixes`.

## What changed
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` has no table with one row for each post. The tables `POSTS`, `LATHE_POSTS`, `PLASMA_POSTS`, `WIRE_POSTS`, `SINKER_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS` are removed.
- The rows come from `posting::BUILTINS` and the four family lists of `posting.rs`. A milling dialect is each registry entry that no family lists, except Klartext. Fanuc's goldens stay at the top of `golden/nc/`.
- The extension check reads each post's own `extension = "..."` manifest line. Each post must declare `nc`, except the seven posts in the sorted table `NOT_NC`. Each of these seven keeps its citation.
- `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles` now asserts a partition:
  - the names are unique;
  - each entry has a shipped `.cps` file;
  - each family name is in `BUILTINS`;
  - each entry is in exactly one family;
  - Fanuc is entry 0.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` counts the `.cps` files that it finds. It no longer compares with the fixed number 26.
- `docs/decisions/3461-post-test-rows.md` records the choices and what was dropped.

The same 16 mill posts, in the same order, and the same lathe, plasma, wire and sinker posts are checked as before. No post, golden or stream changed.

## Cause
Each new post added rows at the end of shared tables in two test files. Two new-post branches therefore conflicted in `conformance.rs`. In `comment_escape.rs` both branches changed `26` to `27`. Git merges two identical changes with no conflict. The merged count was one too low, so main went red after the second merge.

## Tests
- Reproduction before the change (red). I made two branches off 470d1a27c. Each added one new mill post's test rows, as a new-post PR does today. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads gave `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`. `comment_escape.rs` merged to the wrong count, 27.
- After the change (green). The same row edit on this head finds no table in either file (`git diff` is empty). A new post changes neither file.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test comment_escape`: 4 passed.
- This change touches tests only. Thus no product test can start red. The pins are the four mutations below. Each mutation was put in, run, and then removed:
  1. Fanuc's goldens read from a subdirectory: `every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` is red (`golden/nc/fanuc/contour_disc_hole.nc: No such file`).
  2. `mill_posts()` returns no post: `every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles` is red (`each registry entry is in exactly one family`).
  3. The `richauto` row is removed from `NOT_NC`: `every_builtin_declares_its_controls_file_extension` is red (`richauto.cps declares the .nc extension`).
  4. One post (`haas`) is skipped without a result: `header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` is red (`every shipped text post writes both notes`).
- Quick gate on the final head 4c5b49c45 (`cargo xtask gate quick --base 470d1a27c`): 2 steps, 0 failed (`post comment_escape (1 fn)`, `app suites: conformance`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reports `heavy reach: 0 step(s) reached, 122 skipped`. The diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Goldens moved
None. `git diff --stat 470d1a27c HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/**"` is empty. The conformance suite posted every golden byte for byte on this head. I did not run `example_catalog`, because no post, toolpath or recorded program changed.

## Not exercised
- Items 1, 3 and 4 of #3461. `BUILTINS`, the `embedded()` match and the family lists in `posting.rs` still have one line for each post. Thus two new-post branches still conflict there. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is not changed.
- The `cargo xtask merge-plan` test in "Done means" needs item 1, so this PR does not add it.
- The base is 470d1a27c. After that, upstream/main got #4251 (holders). That merge changes none of these files, and `git merge-tree` with it is clean.

## Overlaps
- #2646 (Hurco WinMax post, draft, `needs-rework`, `conflicts`, `P6`) adds rows to `POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS` and changes the count to 27. These are the lines that this PR removes. I did not stack on it: it is a `feat` that merges only at a cut, and a stack would hold this tooling fix until then. When #2646 is refreshed, it drops those three hunks. The decision file has the reason.

Changelog: none (test-only; no behaviour change)

Refs #3461

title: feat(ui): a turning tool is assembled from linked components in the tool library window
body:
## What changed

The Component stack group on the Tool tab of the tool library window now works for a turning tool. Before this change, the group showed only "A lathe tool's component stack is not resolved yet (#3643)." PR #4278 added the lathe resolver caller, so the group can now use it.

- The group shows for a lathe-held tool (Turning, Groove, Thread, Form). It uses the same rows, Add component, Remove, Apply stack, Detach and Swap as a spindle tool.
- An empty stack of a lathe tool offers only the roots that the lathe resolver accepts: a part with a rectangular shank or a round bar shank (`RectShank`, `Cylindrical`, `Weldon`). After the holder, the combo box offers the inserts that fit the holder's seat (`component_fit::compatible_children`).
- An empty stack of a spindle tool no longer offers a lathe holder (a rectangular shank or a row with a lathe body). The spindle resolver refuses these rows.
- The values row of a lathe stack shows the gauge length (0, as #4278 decided), "Inscribed circle (diameter)", the nose radius and the orientation code. It shows no corner radius, because the lathe resolver does not derive one. A refusal shows by name ("The stack does not resolve: ...").
- Apply stack lands one undoable `SetToolAssembly`, as before.
- The turning-tool line in the holder area also points to the Component stack.
- The "lathe" test uses the stored record's kind (`tool_body::LATHE_HELD`), the same test as `tool_assembly::derive`.

No built-in lathe holders or inserts are added. The tools crate has the ISO 5608 and ISO 1832 parsers, but no lathe holder table with sourced seat positions. A user adds lathe holders and inserts to the document from the My library page, from a project file, or with the component editor. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3898-tool-library-components-3.md`.

## Screenshots

Before (main): the group refuses a turning tool.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4331/3898-turning-stack-before.png)

After: PCLNR2525M12 and CNMG120408 from the document, with the ports, the derived values, and the stack applied.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4331/3898-turning-stack-after.png)

The screenshots come from a headless render of a test that is not committed.

## Tests

New file `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_turning_stack.rs` (the #3648 Done-means item "assembling a turning tool from linked components"):

- `a_turning_tool_is_assembled_from_linked_lathe_components_in_one_undo_step`: The user's library holds two PCLNR holders and a CNMG120408 insert. Each "Add to document" click is one undo step. The combo box offers only the two lathe holders (not the built-in BT40 ER32 holder in the document), then the insert in seat CSW1. The test clicks both items. The draft shows gauge 0, the IC 12.700 mm, the nose radius 0.800 mm and orientation 2. Apply stack is one undo step and changes the record. Swap is available for the other holder. One undo restores the record exactly, and redo applies the stack again.
- `a_lathe_stack_the_resolver_refuses_shows_the_refusal_by_name`: A spindle tool's empty stack offers no lathe holder. A groove tool with the same stack shows the resolver's refusal by name. Apply adds no undo step and stores nothing.

The `#[test]` count of the `camcraft-ui` lib goes from 1766 to 1768.

## Gate results

All results are on head `d96c8964b`. The runs used macOS, lane 1, with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4` and no sccache.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Pinning tests `tool_library_turning_stack::*` (2) | pass |
| Nearby suites `tool_library_stack`, `tool_library_components`, `tool_library_assembly` (21) | pass |
| Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (18 steps) | 17 ok. `ui suites: lib` has 1 failure: `setup_wcs_tests::the_combo_lists_the_setups_post_range_by_its_names`. This test is also red on main (#4322) and this PR does not touch it. The other ui lib tests pass: 1759 passed, 1 failed, 8 ignored. |
| Strict clippy `-p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean target) | clean |
| Light lane `cargo xtask gate light` (6 steps) | 6 ok |
| Example catalog suites | not run. No post and no toolpath changed. |

## Not exercised

- A lathe holder with a lathe body from the user library: the library refuses rows with a lathe body (#3645). A holder from the library builds the record and no holder body. A holder with a body comes from a project file (pinned on the app side by `lathe_stack.rs`).
- MCP tools for the component commands are #3647 (PR #4268).

## Done-means check

- #3898: "a user edits a user holder and a component assembly in the window, with undo, and the Done means list of #3648 is met". User holders and spindle assemblies merged in #4271 and #4280. This PR adds the turning assembly.
- #3648: filtering (#4271), assembling a turning tool from linked components (this PR), live update across two tools (#4271), sync from the user library (#4271), undo and redo (all). The UI layout and behaviour tests stay green. The test count does not go down.

Changelog: The tool library window builds a turning tool from linked components: the Component stack offers lathe holders and the inserts that fit them, shows the nose radius, orientation and inscribed circle, and Apply stack is one undo step.

title: feat(pocket): 2D Pocket runs on the path kernel behind the planner switch
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

The first recipe on the path kernel (K6 of #4023): the 2D Pocket runs on the kernel when the planner switch is `new`. With the default switch (`old`) the old pocket planner runs, unchanged.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3752#issuecomment-7211302888

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_pocket.rs` (new): the 2D Pocket recipe. It maps the op parameters to one choice for each stage. It plans each Z level with the heights of that level, and the converter (`kernel_emit::emit_levels`) makes the level plans into one toolpath.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_level.rs` (new): `plan_level`, the stages of one level in the order of the record (guide, order, load, then link and entry for each cut, then the exit). It is not specific to the pocket. The fallbacks and the notes of the stages go to the status line.
- `crates/app/src/operation/planner_switch.rs`: `KERNEL_KINDS = [Pocket]`. Under `new`, `check_engine` lets the 2D Pocket through. Each other phase-1 kind is still refused by name.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs`, `generate.rs`: `run_job_on(job, engine)` and `generate_on(world, op, name, engine)`. `run_job` passes the one reading of the process setting (`planner_engine()`). The Pocket arm reads the engine that it gets and calls `pocket_on_kernel` under `new`.
- `crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`: `GenerateOperation::new_on(world, name, engine)`, the test hook of #4055 for the real command path.
- `crates/app/src/operation/pocket_kernel.rs` (new): the refusals by name under `new` for the options that this recipe does not plan.
- `crates/motion/src/kernel_emit/` (`mod.rs`, `pen.rs`): `LevelPlan::top_z`, the proved material top of a level (`None` is the stock top). The converter still refuses an approach under it (`APPROACH_IN_MATERIAL`) and a level top above the stock top (`BAD_LEVEL_TOP`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/kernel_region.rs`: `without_slivers` (the stock less the fig8 band left a loop with all its points on one line, and the selection refused it).
- `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/kind_pocket.rs` (new), `registry.rs`: the 2D Pocket row is `Moved`, with the real stage planners and the Waterline choices of the pocket.
- `docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`: the decisions.

## In scope and out of scope

What a 2D Pocket does under `CAMCRAFT_PLANNER=new`:

| Strategy | Under `new` |
|---|---|
| Waterline | Kernel: rings of the boundary at the stepover, load control `None` (each cut above the stated load is named), rings linked at depth, each lift named |
| Offset rings | Kernel: rings at the load step, `ConstantEngagement` with `Reach::Rings` (passes inserted where a ring cuts above the load) |
| Zigzag | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ZIGZAG`, points to #3753) |
| Auto | The old rule: Waterline for a round outline (kernel), else Zigzag (refused by name, the text says that Auto chose Zigzag) |
| Adaptive | Refused by name (`KERNEL_POCKET_ADAPTIVE`; the old arm refuses it too) |

Also refused by name under `new`: rest machining (#3753), "do not touch" areas (#3754), the corner relief. 3D levels are the 3D Pocket kind, which `check_engine` still refuses under `new`. No silent fallback to the old planner.

The entry: a selected Helix or Ramp is used where the tool must enter material. Plunge asks for an entry outside material (an arc lead in air, a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column). A closed pocket with none of them is refused with `NO_SAFE_ENTRY` and its fix text.

## Old against new (law measures, #4154)

The disc of #3934 and the dog bone of #3741 in the 80 x 50 stock, tool radius 4, one level. Old: the pinned table of `laws_pockets::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_old_planner` (Auto). New: `k6_pocket::pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel` (Waterline on the kernel).

| Case | Planner | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Feeds out of reach | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Fallback notes | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| disc Inside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Inside | new | 4 (4) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 2 / 1 (1 ramp) | 1205 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| disc Outside | old | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 18 (9 plunge, 9 helix) | 20 (178) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| disc Outside | new | 5 (5) | 0 | 10 | 2 / 0 / 4 (4 ramp) | 362 (180) | 172 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Inside | new | 10 (10) | 1 | 6 | 2 / 8 / 1 (1 ramp) | 812 (173) | 0 | 0 | link L4 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | old | 26 (0) | 0 | 0 | 1 / 0 / 26 (13 plunge, 13 helix) | 32 (180) | 1 | 0 | link L4 L5 L6 |
| dog bone Outside | new | 9 (9) | 0 | 2 | 2 / 0 / 8 (8 ramp) | 310 (180) | 103 | 0 | link L4 L6 |

`testdata/models/fig8.step` (EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, Waterline, stepover 3, stepdown 10, Helix; 3 levels). Old and new on the same op, read by `kernel_route::fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and its light twin:

| Start | Planner | Moves | Lifts (named) | Crossings | Entries: air / column / solid | Over the limit (worst deg) | Full width | Laws broken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Auto | old | 2780 | 18 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 18 (18 helix) | 1236 (180) | 183 | link L6 |
| Auto | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |
| Inside | old | - | 24 (0) | 0 | 0 / 24 / 3 (3 helix) | 1521 (180) | 339 | link L6 |
| Inside | new | refused by name (#4324: the order stage cannot restart a ring and keep its circle and lead) | | | | | | |
| Outside | old | 7573 | 96 (0) | 0 | 0 / 3 / 96 (96 helix) | 85 (135) | 0 | link L6 |
| Outside | new | 27996 | 18 (18) | 6 | 6 / 0 / 15 (15 ramp) | 8595 (180) | 4179 | link L4 L6 |

On fig8 the kernel's Auto resolves to Outside (the band reaches the stock edge with air beyond it), so the two rows are the same path. The fig8 spec of the meter has no part outline (the stock box only), so the meter does not judge the part walls here; the verifier does.

The open items, named and not hidden:
- #4260 and #4272: the full-width reads on Outside (172 and 103) are at the stock edge and on the approach of a stay link. The load stage and the #4154 meter read them differently.
- #4300: a feed of the plan crosses the arc lead of an entry. On the disc Inside and the dog bone Inside it is 1 crossing each (move 11 is in the arc lead of the first entry). On fig8 it is 6 (2 on each level): after a lift, the arc lead of the next air entry runs in from the air across the two outer rings cut before it. `Crossing` blocks the post, so the fig8 pocket does not post under `new` yet. The lead runs in stock that the rings cleared before (no gouge). I added this case to #4300.
- #4324 (new): the order stage refuses the fig8 pocket on the Inside start by name.
- Full width and over the limit on fig8 (4179 and 8595 against 183 and 1236): the same class as #4260 and #4272 (the full-width reads at the stock edge on the Outside start), with no load control (Waterline). The kernel path has about 10 times the moves of the old one (chords, not arcs), so the counts are not one to one. This is the largest open item of the recipe.
- "Over the limit": Waterline has no load control by design. The kernel names each read above the stated load (stepover / D) in one status line note. The meter counts each feed move, and the kernel rings are chords, so the count is higher than the old count of arc moves. The worst angle is the same or lower.
- The entries "solid ... ramp": the helix of the entry stage is chords (#4269 decision 5), so the meter reads it as a ramp. That gives the L4 mark (helix asked, ramp read, no fallback note). The entry stage did fly a helix.
- "Feeds out of reach": the arc leads of the air entries (#4254, #4269).
- #4236 (the chain region of a trace) is not reached by this recipe: the 2D Pocket region is a planar region.

## The verifier

On fig8 (app, through the real generate path): no `Gouge`, `RapidInStock`, `RapidInPart` or `PlungeIntoStock`. `FluteShort` and `ShankHit` are on the old path too (the 20 mm flute of EM-0800-4FL is short for the 20.5 mm pocket). The kernel adds 6 `Crossing` findings (#4300), and the post is blocked by them, as the rule says.

`k6_pocket::the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket` runs the verifier of `camcraft-sim` on each kernel pocket of the pins (square pocket and pocket with a round island, Waterline and Offset rings, Auto / Inside / Outside; disc and dog bone, Auto / Inside / Outside). No `RapidInStock`, no `RapidInPart`, no `PlungeIntoStock`, no `Gouge`. The findings that it reports: `Crossing` on the disc Inside and on the dog bone Inside (#4300). On the closed pockets the kernel has no more crossings than the old planner (0 and 0). The Zigzag trial (not in this PR) gave 30 and 48 `Crossing` findings against 0 for the old planner: that is why Zigzag is refused.

## Pins

Motion (`kernel_laws`, `k6_pocket.rs`):
- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: the square pocket and the pocket with a round island; Auto, Inside and Outside (Waterline) cut the same multiset of rings (`Curve::same_cut`, 1 um, restart and reverse free).
- `pocket_rings_do_not_lift`: 0 lifts on the square pocket; each lift on the pocket with an island (Auto: 5, Outside: 4) has a named reason.
- `pocket_has_no_dead_end_ramp`: each ramp entry descends along its own first cut and ends at its start.
- `a_closed_pocket_without_a_safe_entry_is_refused_by_name`, `the_zigzag_pocket_is_refused_by_name_on_the_kernel`.
- `the_verifier_passes_each_kernel_pocket`, `pocket_2d_readings_of_the_kernel`.

Motion lib: `kernel_emit::tests::a_level_top_lets_the_approach_start_over_the_floor_above`, `kernel_region::tests::kernel_pocket_selection_drops_a_sliver_loop`.

App (`pocket_pass_start`, `kernel_route.rs`):
- `kernel_route_pocket_generates_verifies_and_posts`: a closed pocket through the real generate path with the engine `new`; no blocking verifier warning; it posts with the shipped Fanuc post.
- `kernel_route_default_engine_keeps_the_old_pocket`: the same op with the default engine is the old planner's path, move for move (the command, `generate_on(Old)` and `generate_on(default)`). The fig8 baseline goldens of #4153 (`kernel_baseline`) are unchanged.
- `kernel_route_refuses_what_the_recipe_does_not_plan`: Plunge in a closed pocket (`NO_SAFE_ENTRY`), Adaptive, rest machining; each other phase-1 kind is still refused under `new`.
- `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named` (heavy) and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`: fig8, Waterline, old against new with the law measures. Each start is planned or refused by name (Auto must plan); each lift of the kernel is named; the kernel lifts no more than the old planner; the verifier finds no unsafe kind, and `Crossing` (#4300) is the one blocking kind that the kernel adds.
- `offset_pass_start::planner_switch::switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet`: updated, the 2D Pocket now passes under `new`.

Kernel (`laws`): `registry::each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` runs L1-L7 and the link rule on the registered 2D Pocket.

The app suite includes the law measure helpers of `camcraft-motion` (`crates/motion/tests/common/law_measure`, `mask_grid`) with `#[path]`. They are test helpers that read a toolpath; no generator of another crate is imported.

## Gate results (final head)

All on head `42a68699e` (the final commit of this PR), Linux, `-j 6`:
- `cargo check --tests` for `camcraft-pathkernel`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` (one at a time): clean.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` for the same three crates: clean.
- Quick gate, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (under `xvfb-run -a`): 463 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. It holds `pathkernel suites: laws`, `motion suites: kernel_laws`, `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, the motion pocket suites, `app suites: pocket_pass_start`, `offset_pass_start` and the other app pocket suites.
- Example catalog by name (in the quick plan, default switch): `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`: ok.
- Light lane, `cargo xtask gate light`: 7 steps, 0 failed (`app light: pocket_pass_start` holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline_light` and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named_light`).
- The targeted heavy step of this P1 under the safety floor: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/side/path-kernel --only "app heavy: pocket_pass_start"`: ok (it holds `fig8_pocket_kernel_baseline`, the #4153 goldens of the default switch, unchanged, and `fig8_kernel_pocket_lifts_are_named`).

## Not exercised

- Zigzag, Adaptive, rest machining, "do not touch" and the corner relief on the kernel (refused by name, out of scope).
- A tilted (3+2) frame: the converter refuses a plane that is not the setup XY plane by name (`NOT_SETUP_XY`). No test generates a tilted 2D Pocket under `new`.
- Pre-drilled holes on the kernel route: the holes go into the entry choice, but no pin runs them.
- The example catalog under `new`: the catalog suites ran with the default switch only.

## Decisions

`docs/decisions/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe.md`. The main ones:
- The pass link `Retract` (the `Links::PLANAR` default) and `KeepDown` become "stay down where proved"; only `Clearance` is the user's retract between cuts.
- A lower level enters over the floor of the level above, where the approach of each entry stands on a cut of every level above (else from over the stock top). The first trial (each level from over the stock top) gave a helix through the cut levels and 6 more `Crossing` findings on fig8.
- The verifier gets the pocket area and the air round the stock (`kernel_pocket_reach`), so an air entry is no `Gouge` of the stock edge; the part walls stay judged.
- An incomplete verdict is refused; only a done verdict reaches the post.
- Zigzag waits for #3753.

Changelog: none (the default stays `old`, so no user sees a change; the switch-over PR writes the row).

Refs #3752

title: docs(process): the path kernel merges to main first, and the kinds switch one at a time
body:
## What changed

The delivery plan of the path kernel changed on 2026-11-27 (#4023, comment https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4023#issuecomment-7215353049). This PR makes the docs agree with it. It changes no code.

- New decision record `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`. It quotes the maintainer's words of 2026-11-27, gives the new delivery (merge to `main` with the default at the old planner, a switch PR for each kind, removal after each switch, the four switch conditions for each kind, a question to the maintainer before the first switch), and names the sections of the K0 record (#4024 in `RECOMMENDED.md`) that it replaces. It lists what is dropped and what stays. `RECOMMENDED.md` is not edited.
- `AGENTS.md`, rule **Side branch** (the stable name stays):
  - the plan pointer: the file `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` does not exist; the rule now points to the `#4024` heading in `RECOMMENDED.md` and to the new record;
  - the bullet on the issue of a merged sub-PR: it keeps `in-review` until the switch PR of its kind, or until its own work is complete on `main`;
  - the last bullet: the PR from the side branch to `main` replaces the one switch-over PR.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: two lines that named the one switch-over PR (who merges a `side/*` PR, and the comment text on a sub-PR issue).
- The four lines of `AGENTS.md` that cite **Side branch** do not contradict the new text and are not changed. `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md` has no wrong line and is not changed.

## The new text of the rule

```text
- **Side branch** (#4023, #4042). A side branch `side/<name>` collects the
  sub-PRs of one large change. Then one PR takes it to `main`. Only the
  maintainer permits a side branch. `side/path-kernel` is the one that
  exists. It is made from `main` after this rule merges. Its plan is in
  `RECOMMENDED.md` under `## #4024 - Path kernel K0`, and its delivery is
  in `docs/decisions/4325-path-kernel-delivery.md`.
  - The branch is protected against a force-push and a deletion. It is
    never rebased. Each change goes to it through a sub-PR.
  - A sub-PR has one issue. Its worktree is made from `origin/side/<name>`,
    on a branch `issue/N-<slug>`. It opens as a draft with `--base
    side/<name>`.
  - The body of a sub-PR starts with `Side branch: side/<name>`. It ends
    with `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`: a merge into a side branch closes no
    issue.
  - A sub-PR gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other
    PR. It merges with a merge commit when its review is clean, also as a
    `feat`. `--delete-branch` deletes only the sub-PR's own branch.
  - The issue of a merged sub-PR keeps `in-review` until the switch PR of
    its kind merges, or until the issue's own work is complete on `main`.
    The merging session comments `merged to side/<name> in PR #M; closes
    at the switch of its kind` on the issue.
  - `main` is merged into the side branch with `git merge`, through a sync
    PR into the side branch. Never rebase, never force-push. Do this after
    each merge batch on `main` that touches the code of the side branch,
    and at least each week. If the two sides changed the same logic, the
    sync stops and the maintainer decides (`resolve-conflicts` skill).
  - The gates are local: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR
    runs its pinning tests, the quick gate of its diff against
    `origin/side/<name>`, the example catalog suites and the light lane.
    The head of the side branch gets one local batch gate after each sync,
    inside the build limit. A red batch is fixed on the side branch before
    the next sub-PR merges.
  - The lane and in-flight limits count a sub-PR as each other PR.
  - One PR takes `side/<name>` to `main`. It can come before the
    switches. It uses `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`. An issue closes with the
    switch PR of its kind or with its own work. The PR merges without
    `--delete-branch`. The maintainer's word for that PR says who merges
    it. For `side/path-kernel` it is the coordinator session (his answer
    of 2026-11-27). It merges when an independent review is clean on the
    head, and the batch gate, the heavy `motion` and `app` tests and the
    example catalog suites are green.
```

## Tests

Docs and process only. No build and no gate ran. `git grep` finds no other file that pins the changed strings (`switch-over`, `4024-path-kernel-design`) in `xtask/`, `crates/`, `scripts/` or `.claude/`.

Not exercised: no contract check reads these lines.

title: feat(tools): tool component bodies from STEP, STL and OBJ files
body:
## What changed

This PR adds a first slice of a HEIDENHAIN Klartext (`.H`) reader to `camcraft-gcode`.

- New entry points: `parse_klartext(program)` and `parse_klartext_with(program, &KlartextOptions)`. The output is the same `ParsedProgram` / `ParsedSection` / `cl::Toolpath` as the RS-274 reader gives.
- New module `crates/gcode/src/klartext/` (7 files, each below 400 lines). It uses the section builder, the arc resolver, the numeric domain checks and the peck bound of the RS-274 reader.
- `ParsedSection` gets a `tool_name: Option<String>` field. A named `TOOL CALL "FLAT-6"` has no tool number. Without the field, two named tools would merge into one section. The RS-274 reader sets `None`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2227-klartext-reader.md`.

### The reader reads

- `BEGIN PGM <name> MM` and `END PGM` (the names must agree; a missing `END PGM` is refused as a truncated program).
- `BLK FORM 0.1 Z` / `0.2` (checked; not part of the toolpath).
- `TOOL CALL` with a tool number or a `"NAME"`, axis Z, `S`, `F` (`DL` / `DR` only when zero). `TOOL DEF` (no effect).
- `L` with `X Y Z`, `IX IY IZ`, `R0`, modal `F`, and `FMAX` for one block only.
- `CC` (both axes or none), `C` with `DR+` / `DR-` (a full circle gives two arcs), `CR` with `R+` / `R-`, and `CT` (tangent to the previous element).
- `CYCL DEF 247` (preset `Q339` 1 to 6, read as work offset G54 to G59).
- `CYCL DEF 200`, `203`, `205`, called by `CYCL CALL` or `M99`. Each infeed goes `Q202` deeper from the surface `Q203`. The tool ends at the higher of the two set-up clearances. Each call records a `cl::Cycle`.
- `FN 0: Qn = <literal>`, `Qn = <literal>`, and Q references in values (`X+Q1`, `X-Q1`).
- `STOP`, `;` comments, `*` structure blocks, `~` continuation lines.
- M functions 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 13, 14, 30, 99, 137, and `M140 MB MAX` / `M140 MB <n>`. `M140 MB MAX` needs `KlartextOptions::tool_axis_max_z`, because the end of the traverse range is a machine value.

### The reader refuses (by name, with the line; the message starts with `block N:`)

`RND`, `CHF`, `LP`, `CP`, `CTP`, `APPR`, `DEP`, FK blocks, `LBL`, `CALL`, `RL`, `RR`, axes other than X/Y/Z, polar words, `FAUTO` / `FU` / `FZ`, `M91`, `M92`, `M89`, `M136` and other M functions, `FN` other than `FN 0`, Q formulas, `BEGIN PGM ... INCH`, a tool axis other than Z, a helix (arc with a Z change), old-style cycles (`CYCL DEF 1.0`), cycles other than 200 / 203 / 205 / 247, `CYCL CALL PAT` / `POS`, and the cycle options that change the motion when they are not zero (`Q210`, `Q212`, `Q213`, `Q257`, `Q379`, `Q395`). The decision record gives the reason for each.

## Tests

New test binary `crates/gcode/tests/klartext` (25 tests). Pinning tests:

Reason for the new top-level test binary: `tests/parse/` is the suite of the RS-274 reader; Klartext is a different input language with its own entry point (`parse_klartext`), so it gets its own directory suite. `camcraft-gcode` then has two small test binaries.


- `klartext_post_golden_reads_back_into_the_stream_motion`: the recorded Klartext post golden (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain-klartext/picomax.nc`) reads back into the motion of its CL stream (`crates/post/tests/klartext/contour.cnc`): points, rapid or feed, feeds, arc centres and directions. It also checks tool, rpm, preset, stops and the line map across the continuation line.
- `klartext_post_golden_needs_the_traverse_end_for_m140`.
- Review fix: `klartext_stop_with_m0_or_m1_records_one_program_stop` (a `STOP M0` or `STOP M1` block records one `ProgramStop`, not two stops).
- Paths: `klartext_fmax_is_blockwise_and_f_is_modal`, `klartext_incremental_words_and_literal_q_parameters`, `klartext_cc_and_c_arcs_with_both_directions_and_a_full_circle`, `klartext_cr_radius_sign_picks_the_minor_or_major_arc`, `klartext_ct_continues_the_tangent_of_the_previous_element`, `klartext_tool_calls_by_number_and_name_split_sections`, `klartext_m_functions_set_spindle_coolant_and_stops`.
- Cycles: `klartext_cycle_200_pecks_from_the_surface_and_ends_at_the_2nd_clearance`, `klartext_cycles_203_and_205_without_chip_breaking_drill_at_cycl_call`, `klartext_cycle_247_selects_the_preset_as_work_offset`, `klartext_unsupported_cycles_and_cycle_options_are_refused_by_name`, `klartext_invalid_cycle_definitions_and_calls_are_refused`.
- Refusals: `klartext_functions_outside_the_slice_are_refused_by_name_and_block` (17 functions, line and block number), `klartext_inch_programs_and_unknown_words_are_refused`, `klartext_program_frame_is_checked`, `klartext_arc_preconditions_are_refused`, `klartext_m140_mb_max_needs_the_traverse_end`.
- Degenerate input (each run on a worker thread with a time limit; a panic or a hang fails): `klartext_every_truncation_of_the_golden_is_refused_without_a_panic` (each prefix before `END PGM`), `klartext_bad_numbers_are_refused` (22 cases), `klartext_huge_programs_parse_or_refuse_in_time` (200 000 blocks, a 1 MB block, 100 000 continuation lines), `klartext_seeded_mutations_of_the_golden_never_panic` (3000 seeded mutations), `klartext_empty_and_comment_only_input_is_refused`.

## Gate results (head 6482595d3, Windows lane `winbuild`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`)

title: fix(drilling): Auto reads the depth in material; add the Deep cycle choice
body:
## What changed

1. **Auto reads the depth in material.** Auto chose the drill cycle by `R plane - bottom`, so the air above a hole's mouth counted as depth. A 3.5 mm spot under a 5 mm gap posted `G73 ... Q18`, with a peck step longer than the hole. Auto now reads the depth from the top of the material over the hole, never from above the R plane:
   - an axial hole (`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`): from the higher of the mouth (`Hole::entry_z`) and the material over the drill disk. The app reads that material (the part, the raw stock, and the stock that the program ahead leaves) and passes it in as `CycleParams::material_top`. The program ahead is simulated only where the raw stock stands above a mouth;
   - a radial hole (`cross.rs`): from the raw stock surface over the mouth, clamped to `0..=r_d`;
   - the setup sheet (`crates/app/src/setup_sheet/operations.rs`) names the cycle that the generator chose (the current cache). Without a current cache it says `auto`.

   Thus uncut stock over a mouth counts as depth, and air does not. The plunge still starts at the R plane, and the R word does not change.
2. **A new cycle choice `Deep`.** In the project file and MCP it is `"deep"`. In the combo it is "Deep peck (full retract)". It gives the existing `CycleKind::Deep`, which every canned-cycle post writes as `G83`. It is appended at combo index 10 and digest byte 10, so older operations keep their indices and stamps. The cross-hole cycle maps it before its `unreachable!` arm.
3. **The cycle words are listed.** `list_operation_types` already lists them (#3449). The test now also asks for `deep`.

Docs: the Drill section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/2443-drill-auto-depth.md`.

**Effect on programs.** Under Auto, a hole whose R plane is high above its mouth can change from `G83` to `G73`, or from `G73` to `G81`. A program that does not use Auto, and a hole whose R plane is at its mouth, posts byte-identical.

4. **The radial peck budget reads the full travel** (review fix). Auto picks the cross-hole cycle by the depth in material, but the pecks run from the R standoff. The budget now reads `r_d - bottom`, so a far standoff (30000 mm, or 1e20) is refused as `peck plan unusable`. It is never looped over. The loop also refuses a peck that makes no progress.
5. **Old caches read Stale** (review fix). Auto's output changes and its parameter digest does not. By the #3704 rule, `GENERATOR_OUTPUT_VERSION` goes from 1 to 2. Every cache saved under version 1 reads Stale once, the post refuses it by name, and it clears on regenerate. As #3704 did:
   - the catalog caches are rebuilt (`cargo xtask catalog`);
   - `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, `first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` and `first-router-part.camproj` are saved again (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`; only stamps and the project version move);
   - the pinned stamps of `deburr_cache_stamp` and `wire_stamp` are captured again.

6. **Uncut stock counts** (found by the quick gate after the review fixes). A depth from the mouth alone hid stock over the hole: a raw bar r20 over a part r10 hid 10 mm of steel, and Auto chose chip breaks where full retracts are needed. Item 1 now reads the material over the mouth. The issue's case (stock faced to the plate top) still reads 3.5 mm and posts `G81`.

## Goldens moved

- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc`: the four drill blocks of `Drill1` change from `G83 ... Q6.` to `G73 ... Q18.` (lines 487, 493, 499 and 505). X, Y, Z, R and F do not change. For example, line 487 is now `G73 X38. Y23. Z-2.803 R22. Q18. F115.`
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.camproj`: the `Drill1` cache holds the four new cycles (`peck`, step 18) in place of `deep` (step 6).
- All other catalog `.camproj` files and the three example projects above: only the stamps and the project file version (83 to 84, the writer on the merged `main`) move. No other `.nc` file changes. `cargo xtask catalog` rebuilds every case with the same program.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_auto_depth`:
  - `auto_measures_a_spot_from_its_mouth_not_from_the_r_plane` (the issue's case: G81, not G73)
  - `auto_reads_a_lower_r_plane_as_the_start_of_the_depth`
  - `the_deep_choice_is_the_full_retract_cycle`
  - `a_cross_hole_reads_its_depth_from_the_mouth_and_takes_deep`
- `mcp` suite: `drill_deep::the_deep_cycle_word_posts_full_retract_pecks_and_rides_the_project_file` (Auto posts G73, `deep` posts G83 through Fanuc, and the word survives a save and an open). `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_names_the_optional_fields_and_enum_words` now asks for `deep`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `cycle_combo::the_deep_peck_reads_in_plain_english` and `every_cycle_has_one_label_and_picks_itself_back` (11 choices).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::tests_auto_depth::a_far_radial_standoff_is_refused_by_the_peck_budget` (explicit Peck, Auto and Deep, at R 30000 and 1e20).
- `camcraft-app` lib: `operation::stamp::tests::a_drill_cache_saved_before_the_2443_bump_reads_stale_and_does_not_post` (the catalog first-part `Drill1` with a pre-bump stamp reads Stale, the post refuses it by name, and once generated again it posts `G73` and no `G83`).
- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_first_part::{rebuilds,regenerates}` with the rebuilt program.
- `drill_auto_material` (new app suite): `uncut_stock_over_the_mouth_is_depth` (7 mm of raw stock over the plate: Auto pecks) and `stock_the_program_ahead_cut_away_is_not_depth` (a Face ahead cuts to the plate top: Auto posts G81, and the setup sheet says `drill`).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::tests_auto_depth::auto_counts_the_material_over_the_mouth` and `a_cross_hole_counts_the_raw_stock_over_its_mouth`.
- `drilling_cross_box::a_cylinder_stock_chain_matches_its_numeric_reference` and `drilling_cross_stock` keep their readings.

## Readings

- Quick gate on the final head 4cbc56ee9 (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 372 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 63.7 min.
- An earlier quick gate on b2ca05b43 had 3 failures:
  - `drilling_cross_box::a_cylinder_stock_chain_matches_its_numeric_reference` and `drilling_cross_stock::a_box_stock_and_an_off_origin_spindle_stand_off_the_raw_stock_plus_the_rim`. The depth from the mouth alone hid the raw stock over a cross hole. Item 6 fixes this, and the two tests pass with their old readings.
  - `egui_app::setup_wcs_tests::the_combo_lists_the_setups_post_range_by_its_names`. Main fixed this test in #4329. The merge of `upstream/main` (4cbc56ee9) brings in that fix.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask catalog` on the final head: no file changes.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on 4cbc56ee9: 51 steps (1 build, 7 `motion`, 43 `app`), 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 43.2 min. The known fails #1950 and #2849 are red as expected.

## Screenshots

The Cycle combo on the Passes tab of a Drill operation. "Before" is the same build with the new entry taken out for that render only.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2443/cycle-combo-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2443/cycle-combo-after.png) |

## Not exercised

- A real machine.

Changelog: Drill: Auto chooses the cycle by the depth in material, measured from the top of the material over each hole, not from the R plane (a shallow spot under a high R plane now drills with G81). New cycle choice "Deep peck (full retract)" (`deep`) posts G83 on any hole.

Fixes #2443

title: feat(mcp): list_posts, select_post, preview_post and save_post_script
body:
## What changed

This PR adds four MCP post tools (`crates/app/src/mcp/post_tools.rs`):

- `list_posts` lists each built-in post and each `.cps` file in the user posts folder. Each row gives the machine kinds that the post serves, `description`, `program_units`, `extension` and the declared options. A file that does not load gives its `problem`. `selected` is the document's post.
- `select_post` runs `SelectPost` through the session History. It is one undo step. `null` selects the default built-in post.
- `preview_post` runs a script (`source` or `path`) on a built-in sample (Facing, Contour, Pocket, Drilling) or on the document stream. It writes no file. It returns `ok`, `program`, `lines`, `warnings` and `swallowed`. A failed script returns `ok: false` and `errors` with the 1-based `line` in the script. The Boa runtime limits stop a script that loops.
- `save_post_script` saves a plain file name in the user posts folder. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`, else `<data dir>/camcraft/posts` (the same order as the user machines folder). The script must load and run before the save. An existing file is replaced only with `overwrite: true`. The write is atomic.

Other changes:

- In a live app session, `save_post_script` needs approval as a `FileWrite`, and `select_post` as a `LimitEdit` (`mcp::live::requires_approval`).
- A hidden test hook `Server::set_user_posts_dir` (an `Env` field) points the folder at a temp folder.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is generated again (128 tools). `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` has the four rows. `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` has a "Post scripts" section.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/2074-mcp-post-tools.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `mcp` suite, `post_tools::*` (6 tests):
  - `list_posts_lists_every_builtin_post_with_what_it_declares`
  - `select_post_is_one_undo_step_and_refuses_a_stranger` (undo and redo)
  - `preview_post_runs_a_script_on_a_sample_and_writes_no_file` (output, warnings, no file)
  - `preview_post_returns_the_1_based_line_of_a_syntax_error_and_stops_a_loop`
  - `save_post_script_writes_a_plain_name_into_the_user_posts_folder_only`
  - `a_live_session_asks_before_a_post_file_write_or_a_post_choice`
- `camcraft-app` lib: `mcp::post_files::tests::*` (folder order, plain names) and `mcp::post_tools::tests::the_error_line_reads_the_script_position`.

## Readings

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 362ab7198): 176 steps, 1 failed: `mcp_doc_drift` (`every_live_tool_is_in_the_guide_and_the_local_prompt`). The site MCP guide did not name the new tools. a8890b3a1 adds them; `mcp_doc_drift` (9 tests) and the `mcp` suite (62 tests) pass on the final head.
- Site tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`): no failure that main does not have.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes: this diff changes no generator or post output.
- A real per-user data folder: the tests use a temp folder through the hook. The folder order is a unit test.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` gets the four tool rows, as the issue asks).

Changelog: MCP: `list_posts`, `select_post` (undoable), `preview_post` (read-only, no file written) and `save_post_script` (a plain file name in the user posts folder, `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`) tools for post authoring and selection.

Fixes #2074

title: feat(laser): the Laser Profile operation
body:
Slice 2b of #4081: the **Laser Profile** operation in the app.

**Stacked on #4270 (slice 1) and #4273 (slice 2a).** The branches of those PRs are in a fork, so this PR targets `main` and its diff includes them. The new work is the two commits after the merge commit `2a3670d48`: `a4cc1cf1f` and `ae360094b`. Merge #4270 and #4273 first. After that, this branch takes `git merge origin/main` and its diff is only slice 2b.

## What changed

- **Registry**:
  - New `OpType::LaserProfile`: stored kind id 49 and digest tag 49, appended.
  - New `Section::Laser` and `Family::Laser`. The Laser family admits only a laser cutter, and a laser cutter admits only that family.
  - The ribbon shows the Laser section on a laser cutter only.
  - The family door refuses laser work elsewhere: "a Laser Profile operation is laser cutting work; ... - mount a laser cutter first".
- **Params**: `LaserOp` has the waterjet's stored shape, with `power` (percent of the source's maximum) in place of the abrasive delay. It reuses the waterjet's lead, side and tab types. The command door checks the power: more than 0, at most 100.
- **Project file**: `LaserDto` (`"laser_profile"`), additive.
- **Generation**: `operation/laser_op.rs` resolves the heights and the laser head's kerf, then calls `motion::laser::laser_profile` (slice 2a).
- **Machine check**: `machine::waterjet::check_xy_ops` holds the X/Y gantry checks once. These are the family, the tool kind, rotary moves, feed ceilings and strokes. The waterjet and the laser call it with their own words. The waterjet sentences do not change.
- **Safety refusals until the laser post exists (slice 3)**:
  - The verification report says "<op>: laser posting is unavailable: beam on/off records, power records and pierce dwell records are not implemented".
  - The stock sim says "<op>: laser stock removal is not judged: the stock sim has no laser model".
  - The lathe voice refuses the op with its own sentence.
- **Tools**: the starter catalog gets `LZ-KERF-020` (`laser_tool(0.2)`). The empty-rack refusal names it. `camcraft_app::laser_tools` re-exports the tools module.
- **UI**:
  - New `laser_page.rs`: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side and arcs on Geometry; the three heights; tabs; leads; and on Feeds the cut feed, **Power**, and pierce time. A power out of range is named on the page.
  - New original glyph `assets/ui/svg/op-laser-profile.svg`: an outlined head, a beam, sparks and the kerf gap. `cargo xtask icons` added only its PNG.
  - The waterjet page's `tab_fields` is shared.
- **MCP**: no new tool. `add_operation` and `edit_operation` reach the kind through the registry and the DTO. The `add_operation` description names the laser kind (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`).
- **Docs**:
  - New guide page `site/content/guide/operations/operations-laser.md`.
  - The operations index and `check-and-post/machines.md` name the laser.
  - Decision: `docs/decisions/4081-laser-op.md`.

## Screenshots

A laser cutter mounted, before (slice 1: no section) and after (the LASER group):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4081/after-laser-ribbon.png)

The Laser Profile's Feeds tab (new page):

![feeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4081/after-laser-feeds.png)

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/machine/laser_profile.rs` (the `machine` suite, 6 tests):
  - The family on a laser cutter only.
  - A holed plate: the hole first, every note in the laser's words, and the laser machine check clean.
  - The tool doors.
  - Create, edit, undo and redo, and the power door.

title: feat(tools): SK50 holders and ER50 collet chucks on the 40 and 50 tapers
body:
Stacked on #4251. This PR contains the commits of #4251. Merge #4251 first; then this PR takes `git merge origin/main` and a new gate. Do not merge this PR before #4251.

## What changed

Third slice of #3919. The built-in holder library gets:

- **SK50** (DIN 69871 / DIN ISO 7388-1 size 50): Ø69.85 gauge, Ø97.5 flange, 3.2 standoff, 15.9 flange. It has ER16-ER50 collet chucks and every Weldon bore (6-20 mm, 1/4-3/4 in). The default gauge length is 100. It is in `crates/tools/src/holder_library_din.rs`, after SK40.
- **ER50** (Ø5-34 collets, Ø78 M64×2 nut, drawn 40 long) in the one ER table. It is on BT40, CAT40, SK40, BT50, CAT50 and SK50, with a default gauge length of 100. There is no standalone ER50 chuck.
- **SK50 is a spindle mount**: `SPINDLE_MOUNTS` has 14 names, with SK50 after SK40. The app test `every_library_taper_is_a_spindle_mount` keeps the list equal to the library.

The ER50 nut is wider than a 40-taper flange. The body is drawn at the nut width up to the flange front, with no flare. The flange steps in from it, so the outline is never smaller than the steel.

Each number and its source is in `docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders-3.md`.

Left out, with the reasons in the decision file:
- SK50 shrink-fit: the slice-2 shrink-fit tables have no SK50 table.
- TG75 / TG100: TG is a trade system, and we found no standard table.
- Morse MT2-MT5: DIN 228 fixes only the taper. The collar below the spindle face has no standard table.
- NMTB 30 / 40: we found no published flange table.
- Hydraulic and milling chucks: each maker designs its own body.
- A standalone ER50 chuck.
- SF32: it waits for the owner's measurements.

## Pinning tests

- `holder_library::din::sk50_tests::*` (new file `crates/tools/src/holder_library_sk50_tests.rs`):
  - `sk50_and_er50_match_the_recorded_table`

  - `a_bt40_er50_body_wider_than_its_flange_is_drawn_whole`

- These tests are updated for the new rows: `the_tapers_and_nuts_match_the_recorded_table`, `the_din_entries_are_listed`, `the_50_taper_entries_are_listed`, `the_shrink_entries_are_listed` (SK50 has no shrink-fit entry), `the_picker_shows_one_weldon_row_for_each_taper` and `the_new_library_tapers_are_spindle_mounts` (post).

winbuild (Windows, 5 jobs):

title: feat(motion): a laser profile generator on the shared sheet laws
body:
Slice 2a of #4081 (the laser profile cut): the generator in the motion crate. The app operation is slice 2b. This PR does not depend on slice 1 (#4270).

## What changed

- **The waterjet generator speaks with a voice from its params.** `WaterjetParams` gets `voice: Voice`. The about 20 hard-coded "waterjet profile" / "waterjet:" texts in `motion::waterjet` (door, planner, tabs, emitter, notes) now read `p.voice`. `sheet::Voice` gets a `short` word for the notes (`plasma`, `wire`, `waterjet`, `laser`) and a new `Voice::LASER` ("laser profile", tool "beam").
- **Every waterjet sentence is the same as before.** The pierce note keeps its abrasive text under the waterjet voice. Under another voice it names the voice's tool ("beam and dwell records are not implemented").
- **New `motion::laser`**: `LaserParams` (the waterjet's numbers without the abrasive delay, plus `power`) and `laser_profile`. It checks the power by name (more than 0, at most 100 % of the source's maximum), converts to `WaterjetParams` with `Voice::LASER`, and runs the same planner, tabs, emitter, kerf law and cover law. A note states the requested power. No CL record carries the power yet (slice 3, the laser post).
- Callers: `crates/app/src/operation/waterjet_op.rs` and the waterjet golden test set `voice: Voice::WATERJET`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4081-laser-motion.md`. It says why the laser rides the waterjet generator (the same sheet rules; no copy of about 500 lines) and why the power is a percent (the Grbl laser mode scales S against `$30`).

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion` lib, `laser::tests`:
- `the_laser_cuts_what_the_waterjet_cuts_and_speaks_as_the_laser`: the same moves as the waterjet for the same numbers. Every note starts with `laser: `, and no note names the abrasive or the jet.
- `the_power_is_refused_by_name_outside_its_range`: 0, -5, 100.5 and NaN are refused. 100 is legal.
- `the_shared_refusals_speak_as_the_laser_profile`: the kerf, clearance, tab count, tab position and empty input refusals say "laser profile:".
- `an_open_run_and_a_missing_silhouette_say_so_in_the_lasers_words`.

The waterjet stays pinned by its unchanged tests: `waterjet::tests` (11), `waterjet_profile` (8), `mcp_waterjet`, and the golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` (no change).

## Gates

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: **not run**. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` reaches every motion and app heavy target (115 steps), because `motion` and `waterjet_op.rs` changed. The change does not alter any path: the waterjet golden and the moves-equality test show this. The heavy run is owed before the PR is flagged ready.

title: feat(mcp): tool component library, compatibility and assembly tools
body:
The parent #4233 is merged (`7cb5da575`); this PR now shows only its own commits.

Process change: yes

## What changed

This PR adds eight MCP tools for tool components, tool assemblies and the user component library. The tools are in three new files of `crates/app/src/mcp/`: `component_tools.rs`, `assembly_tools.rs` and `component_library_tools.rs`.

Read tools:
- `list_tool_components`: lists the built-in components, the user library and the document component table. The filters are `kind`, `scope` and `compatible_with`. A row of a match has `fits: [{as, port}]`. A document row has its library sync status.
- `get_tool_assembly`: gives the component stack of a document tool. It gives each node with its mount (parent, port, Z rotation, stickout `projection_mm`), its MCS frame and its sync status. It also gives the derived cutting diameter and corner radius, the gauge length, and the `links` input form.

Document write tools. Each tool runs the same undoable command as the GUI, in one History step:
- `upsert_tool_component` (`UpsertDocumentComponent`)
- `delete_tool_component` (`DeleteDocumentComponent`)
- `set_tool_assembly` (`SetToolAssembly`; `links: null` clears the stack)
- `sync_tool_component` (`SyncDocumentComponent`)

User library tools. These are file edits through `component_library::store`, not undoable commands:
- `save_library_component`
- `delete_library_component`

Each tool validates its arguments early and refuses by name. A component goes through the MCP door in the `.camproj` wire form (`ComponentDto`, `deny_unknown_fields`). A stack goes through as `LinkDto`. A stated `library_ref` in an upsert or a save is refused. A `builtin:` id is refused for a library save and delete. An optional `library` argument names another `.camcomponents` file, as the cut recipe tools do.

Live GUI gate (`mcp/live.rs`): the two library write tools are `FileWrite`. A stated `library` on `list_tool_components`, `get_tool_assembly` and `sync_tool_component` is `FilePathAccess`.

The `camcraft-mcp` skill lists each new tool (section 4). This is a process file, so the body has the line `Process change: yes`. The PR does not change `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3647-component-mcp-tools.md`.

Docs: the generated tool reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the user guide `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` list the new tools. The `mcp_doc_drift` suite pins both.

No script verb: the skill does not ask for one, and the script host has no component verbs.

## Readings and pinning tests

New submodule `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/component_mcp.rs` in the existing `tool_library_holders` suite (no new test binary). All calls go through the MCP server:
- `component_mcp::mcp_lists_compatible_components_and_reads_a_built_assembly`: `compatible_with` the shared insert gives the two cutter bodies, with `{as: parent, port: CSW1}`. An assembly built by `set_tool_assembly` reads back Ø25, corner radius 0.4, three nodes. Undo, redo and clear work.
- `component_mcp::mcp_edits_a_shared_insert_and_syncs_it_from_the_library`: one upsert of the shared insert updates both tools (corner radius 0.4 to 0.8) in one undo step. A save and a link-only sync, then a newer library copy shows `update_available`. The sync updates both tools, and undo and redo work. A library delete shows `missing_from_library`.
- `component_mcp::mcp_component_tools_refuse_by_name_and_change_nothing`: about twenty named refusals (an incompatible insert, an unknown key, `library_ref`, a no-op, a used component, unknown ids, a bad link key, an empty stack, an insert on a coupling port, unknown kind or scope or argument, `builtin:` ids, id and component together). No refused save writes the library file, and the assembly does not change.

## Gate results (head `dda741331`)

The gate base is `qsmits/issue/3645-component-library` (the #4233 head `745234df7`), not `main`. This PR stacks on that branch.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_library_holders`: 28 passed, 0 failed (3 new tests).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift`: 9 passed. The first quick run found that the generated reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the guide `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` did not list the new tools. The second commit adds them.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base qsmits/issue/3645-component-library`: 169 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (28.3 min, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`). Two earlier runs stopped at the build with `can't find crate for solidcore` (a stale `solidcore` unit in the target folder, not this change); `cargo clean -p solidcore -p solidcore-convert` cleared it.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed (15.9 min).
- No heavy step (P6).

## Not exercised

- A live GUI session (`--mcp-port`) with the approval prompts. Only the classification in `requires_approval` changed.
- The default user library folder. The tests use the `library` argument, so they do not write the user's real library.
- A lathe-held assembly. The resolver refuses it by name (#3643).

## Notes

- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders.rs` goes from 407 to 411 lines: two lines for the module and two lines for the header and Gate map. The test code is in the submodule.
- `mcp/tools.rs` gets one line (`component_tools::all()`). It was already over 400 lines.

Changelog: MCP tools for tool components and assemblies: list_tool_components (with compatible_with), get_tool_assembly, upsert_tool_component, delete_tool_component, set_tool_assembly, sync_tool_component, save_library_component and delete_library_component.

Effort: medium (not escalated)

Fixes #3647

title: feat(tools): shrink-fit chucks, BT50 and CAT50 holders; every taper is a spindle mount
body:
## What changed

Second slice of #3919, and all of #4239.

- **Shrink-fit chucks** (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_shrink.rs`). The library gets DIN 69882-8 shrink-fit chucks on each taper except TTS: BT30, BT40, CAT40, SK30, SK40, ISO30, HSK-A63, HSK-F63, HSK-E40, HSK-E32, BT50 and CAT50 (127 entries, "BT40 Shrink 12 mm").
  - A new clamp kind: `Clamp::Shrink { bore, nose_d, body_d }`.
  - The outline is one envelope: the 4.5-degree nose cone from d2 to d3, under the 45-degree flare from the flange front. At each height the larger of the two is drawn. A short chuck is drawn whole and is not refused.
  - The nose and the body are drawn 2 mm wider in radius than the table (`SHRINK_MARGIN`). Reason: one maker's chuck of the same size is 1.53 mm wider.
- **BT50 and CAT50** (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_fifty.rs`). Each taper gets ER16-ER40 and each Weldon bore, with a default gauge length of 100.
- **Picker.** One grouped "<taper> Shrink" row for each taper, the same as "<taper> Weldon" (#2018). It resolves to the bore that takes the tool's shank (`shrink_for`). An unknown bore is refused by name.
- **#4239.** `SPINDLE_MOUNTS` now lists each library taper (13 names). The app test `every_library_taper_is_a_spindle_mount` keeps the two lists equal. It also loads each library holder in its own mount. An unknown mount ("HSK-A100", "HSK-A99", "R8") is still refused by name.
- The UI clamp texts, the MCP `list_holder_library` output (`"kind": "Shrink"`) and the tool descriptions (with `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`) know the new kind.
- `LibraryError` moved to `holder_library_error.rs`, and the Weldon bore tables moved to `holder_library_weldon.rs`. This keeps `holder_library.rs` under 400 lines (388).
- Each number and its source: `docs/decisions/3919-standard-holders-2.md`. We did not copy a vendor model.

## Pinning tests

- `holder_library::shrink::tests::*`: the recorded rows, the listed entries, the SK40 12 mm and BT40 6 mm outlines point by point, never under the table steel (each entry, default and shortest gauge), a wider maker's chuck stays inside, the grouped picker and its refusal, the envelope edge cases.
- `holder_library::fifty::tests::*`: the BT50 / CAT50 table, the entries, the BT50 ER32 outline, the CAT50 flange position.
- `machine::tooling::tests::the_new_library_tapers_are_spindle_mounts` (post).

- Updated: `holder_library::tests::*`, `holder_library::weldon::tests::*`, and the din / hsk tests now count only the ER and Weldon entries.

Default job count (full parallelism). Log `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3919c-9921f2961.log` (the head SHA is on its first line).

| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
| `camcraft-app` lib | ok, 318 passed |
| `camcraft-app` `holder_library` | ok, 12 passed |
| `camcraft-app` `holder_reference` | ok, 7 passed |
| `camcraft-app` `machine_default_holder` | ok, 14 passed (`every_library_taper_is_a_spindle_mount` included) |

| `camcraft-app` `mcp_holder` | ok, 5 passed |
| `camcraft-ui` lib, filter `tool_holder tool_library_holders` | ok, 12 passed |

An earlier run on head 32a373698 did not compile (a borrow in the grouped picker loop). Commit 9921f2961 fixes it. The `cargo xtask gate quick --base <#4240 branch> --dry-run` plan of that run had 130 steps.

The quick plan against the base branch reaches many `camcraft-app` test binaries, because `crates/app/src/mcp/` changed. winbuild stalls when it links the whole set. For this reason the run has the tools and post steps and the named app and UI holder suites only, the same as #4240. The full app quick plan was not run.

title: fix(xtask): a build step gets the longer stall time of the gate watchdog
body:
## What changed

- `xtask/src/watchdog.rs`: `limit_for` gives a build step the longer stall time (`SLOW_FACTOR`, 4x), as it does for a `--release` or `--ignored` step. A build step is a `cargo test` step with `--no-run`, or a `cargo build` step. With the default of 15 min, a build step can now be silent for 60 min.
- Only the cargo subcommand counts. A test binary that is named `build` (`--test build`) is not a build step.
- Clippy keeps the base time: it checks and does not link.
- The plan line now reads `(4x for --release, --ignored and build steps)`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4101-build-step-stall.md` (option 1 of the issue; options 2 and 3 dropped, with the reasons).

## Why

The v0.27.0 cut gate stopped at step [01] "debug build (--no-run)". Three cold `rust-lld` links wrote no output for 15 min, and the watchdog killed the step. A link is silent by its nature. The watchdog could not tell a slow link from a hang.

## Pinning test

- `watchdog_tests::build_steps_get_the_longer_stall_time`: the quick gate's ui build (`test ... --no-run`) and a `cargo build` get 60 min; a debug test step, a clippy step and a test binary named `build` keep 15 min; the plan line names the build steps.
- The old test `release_and_ignored_steps_get_the_longer_stall_time` is unchanged and passes.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p xtask`: all suites pass (lib 362, and the integration suites).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p xtask -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The "Done means" of the issue asks for a cold release-tier gate on the cut runner that passes step [01]. Only the cut runner can show that.
