title: fix(ui): every input on the operation pages has an accessible name
body:
**Stacked on #4221** (the 2D slice of #1122, which is stacked on #4220 and #4218). The 2D slice names five fields that this guard finds. Until the chain merges, this diff also shows the commits of the three parents (42ca7bfc5, 9886fef31, b852d7257). The commit of this PR is cf3565107. After each parent merges, I merge `main` into this branch.

## What changed

Slice 3 of #1119: the operation pages. Each input on each operation page tab now has an accessible name.

- **The cause.** On `main` 773736856, 1,840 of 1,861 input occurrences on the operation pages had no name. `num` and `combo` set no `labelled_by`. Only the `*_row` variants did, and the pages call the base helpers.
- **A property row names its controls.** `prop_row` opens its row while it draws the row's controls (`layout::named_by`). The seam's fields drawn inside the row take its label as their name (`layout::name_by_row`). These fields are:
  - `num` and its variants, and `num_plain`;
  - `value_with_unit`;
  - `combo`, `combo_owned` and `tool_combo`;
  - `drag_row` (from #4221).

  A field outside an open row takes no name from the seam. Thus a field never takes the name of the row drawn before it, which `row_label_id` (the last row of the frame) could give.
- **The operation header** is a `Grid` with its own labels. Its Tool, Source, Setup and Coolant combos are named through `named_by` with their row labels.
- **Spindle speed** (`spindle_row.rs`) is named by its row.
- **No label twice.** `num_row`, `num_feed_row`, `num_plain_row` and `num_unit_row` already named by the row. They are now the same field as their bases, so no field has the same label two times.
- **Files.** The helpers are in the new file `layout/row_name.rs` (49 lines). `layout/form.rs` grows by 4 lines (420 to 424). It was over the 400-line limit before this PR.
- **Tests that read a row's text.** Seven tests found a row's text with `get_by_label`. The row's control now has the same name, so they now ask for the `Label` node (`get_by_role_and_label(Role::Label, ..)`). In `wire_page_tests`, a click on the row label opened the named combo, so a small `show_row` helper scrolls the label into view instead. No assertion changes.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1119-op-page-names.md`.

Nothing visible changes.

title: feat(chamfer)!: add lead-in and lead-out
body:
## What changed

- Add lead-in and lead-out controls to 2D Chamfer.
- Reuse the existing `Lead` values, shape constructors, UI selectors, DTO values, and stamp writers.
- Reuse the existing linear, quarter-arc, tangential, and perpendicular lead geometry.
- Add Chamfer-specific air-side planning, lead halving, crossing checks, and a hard refusal when no safe lead fits.
- Check each candidate lead with the complete cutter, including the cone, flute, shank, modelled body, and holder.
- Keep `EdgeBreak` credit on the selected edge. Lead moves add no extra edge-break credit.
- Keep old saved open Chamfer projects on their fixed-width approach.
- Default new operations to a 3 mm Perpendicular lead-in and mirror it for lead-out; `None` remains selectable.

The Chamfer page adds only the lead-in and lead-out shape controls. It does not add Contour entry, level links, tabs, cutter compensation, overlap, extensions, or vertical lead-in controls.

## Breaking project-format change

Project format v83 carries the Chamfer lead values.

- An older reader must refuse a v83 file.
- A v82-or-earlier file with no lead field keeps the legacy open-chain approach.
- An explicit `none` value removes the added XY lead.

The project-format break is stated in the PR title.

## Tests

- Focused motion pins: 7 passed.
- Focused app project and stamp pins: 3 passed.
- MCP create, edit, save, load, and reset pin: 1 passed.
- UI compatibility and undo pins: 2 passed.
- The complete motion Chamfer suites, app Chamfer suites, and UI structural field test passed.
- Final quick gate: 821 of 822 steps passed.
  - `mcp_live` failed on `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
  - The failed step passed on a targeted rerun: 1 step, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
  - The rerun took 72 seconds.
- `example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored.
- `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- Light lane: 11 tests passed across 6 steps.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- No PR-owned golden changed.

## Not exercised

- No full manual application click-through ran.
- The full heavy lanes did not run. This is a P6 enhancement, and the current review rules do not require them.
- `graphify update` could not run because `graphify` is not on `PATH`.

Changelog: 2D Chamfer can reuse the existing lead-in and lead-out controls, with cone-safe entry and exit.

Effort: high

Fixes #3237

title: refactor(ui): tool drawing inks are theme tokens
body:
The four PRs under this one (#3990, #3992, #3993, #4072) are merged. The branch merges `main` at 498382c8e (5b9256022). The change is 5d2c2b2d6. The review fix is 25b220b34.

## What changed

The fourth family of #1120: the tool drawing inks.

- Eighteen colour tokens join `Tokens`. Each is also a theme-file key (`colors.<name>`):
  - the tool, holder and profile previews: `tool_ground`, `tool_axis`, `tool_grid`, `tool_flute`, `tool_shank`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge`, `tool_holder`, `tool_note`, `tool_dim`;
  - the library thumbnails: `thumb_flute` (their shank reads `tool_shank`);
  - the refusal and warning inks of the tool pages: `bad_ink`, `warn_ink`;
  - the tool body page: `mount_axis`, `mount_radial`, `mount_tip`, `mount_origin`, `mount_hint`.
- Both tables hold the old values, so no pixel changes. The previews keep their own dark ground in the light theme, as before.
- The module colour consts (`NOTE`, `BAD`, `HOLDER`, `BG`, `BODY`, `EDGE`, `DIM`, `WARN`, `CUT`, `SHANK`) become functions with the same visibility (`note_ink()`, `bad_ink()`, `holder_ink()`, `tool_ground()`, ...). Each reads the live token. The callers change by name only. One colour role is one key: the note grey was a const in five files, the axis line in three.
- `theme::with_alpha(colour, alpha)`: a token's own colour at an alpha, read unmultiplied, so a partly transparent token does not darken twice (the defect of the #3993 review). The holder fills (alpha 90 in the profile, 70 in the preview) use it. `ground_ink::facet_veil` now calls it too.
- Draw sites: `tool_profile_page.rs`, `tool_preview.rs`, `tool_model_view.rs`, `tool_body_page.rs`, `tool_body_lathe_page.rs`, `tool_holder_picker.rs`, `tool_cutter_page.rs`, `tool_cutter_params.rs`, and `tool_library_dialog/` (`holder_view.rs`, `side_view.rs`, `thumbs.rs`, `assembly_group.rs`, `preview.rs`).
- The colour-literal guard loses the ten rows of the tool family. `theme/tables.rs` goes from 82 to 118.
- The example theme and the colour table of the user guide have the eighteen keys.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1120-tool-inks.md`.

## Review fix (25b220b34)

The tool list thumbnails (`thumbs.rs`) and the holder outline (`holder_view.rs`) keep their built shapes, and the shapes carry theme colours. Before the fix, each cache key held only the tool or holder inputs, so a theme change kept the old colours.

- Each cache key now also holds the inks that its shapes carry:
  - thumbnails: `thumb_flute` and `tool_shank`;
  - holder outline: `tool_axis`, `tool_body`, `tool_edge` and `tool_dim`.
- The holder ground and the labels are painted live each frame, so they are not in the key.
- `build` takes the inks from the key, so the key and the shapes cannot disagree.
- The cache lookup of the holder view moves into `drawing()`, so a unit test can call it without a window.

## Pinning tests

In `crates/ui/tests/theme_files/tool_inks.rs`, a new module of the existing `theme_files` test binary (#3187: no new binary):

- `the_built_in_columns_keep_the_tool_drawing_colours`: both tables carry the old literals.
- `each_tool_drawing_ink_is_a_theme_key`: each key sets its own ink.
- `a_holder_fill_keeps_the_colour_of_its_token`: the built-in holder gives the old fills at alpha 90 and 70, and a `#FF000080` token gives `[255, 0, 0]` at alpha 70, not a darker red.

The review fix, as unit tests of the `camcraft-ui` lib (no new binary):

- `tool_library_dialog::thumbs::tests::a_theme_change_of_the_inks_builds_the_row_drawing_again`
- `tool_library_dialog::holder_view::tests::a_theme_change_of_the_inks_builds_the_holder_outline_again`

Each test draws, checks that the same inks build nothing, changes the inks, checks one new build with the new colours and no old colour, and checks that the next drawing holds. With the inks removed from the cache comparison, both tests are red. The still-frame tests `a_document_row_has_a_cached_drawing_and_its_gauge_length` and `a_still_frame_builds_no_holder_outline` stay green.

Also: `theme_example::example_loads_and_holds_the_dark_defaults`, `theme_files::viewport_inks::the_facet_veil_keeps_the_hover_colour_of_a_semi_transparent_token` (now through `with_alpha`) and `theme_files::colour_literals::no_colour_literal_outside_the_allowed_rows`.

The tool library window, a tool open in the library editor (the tool preview), and the tool shape window on its Profile, Body and Holder library tabs, in the dark and light theme. The images come from the off-screen renderer (`egui_kittest` with the headless wgpu device, as in `guide_images`), at 1280 x 720. The images are on the images-only `pr-screenshots` branch of the fork, not on this branch.
